name: Beast Mutations
rows: The creature grows a second head, which seeks to kill all living things and gains a bite attack.
The creature's shadow can detach and attack as a {@creature shadow|MM} or a {@creature specter|MM}.
The creature grows three extra eyes on stalks that provide {@sense truesight} to 60 feet.
Slashing or piercing damage to the creature spurts green bile onto any adjacent creatures, dealing {@damage 1d6} acid damage per proficiency bonus.
The creature grows a long tongue that can knock an adjacent creature {@condition prone} as a bonus action unless it succeeds on a {@dc 10} Strength saving throw.
Once injured, the creature goes berserk and has advantage on all melee attacks, but also grants advantage against melee attacks.
The creature gains immunity to one damage type, while gaining vulnerability to another.
The creature grows bloody wings and gains a fly speed equal to its walking speed.
The creature's natural weapons automatically score a critical hit on a hit, but also deal half the damage dealt from these attack to the creature itself.
The creature grows hard scales that add 2 to its AC, but it suffers disadvantage on all saving throws.

Upon reaching 0 hit points, the creature explodes in a shower of gore, {@condition blinded|PHB|blinding} all creatures with 20 feet for one round unless they succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw.

name: Beast Mutations
rows: Roll twice on the table, ignoring this result if rolled again.

{@b Spawning Pit.} Your skin begins to crawl moments before vermin chew through your flesh and erupt from your body. {@dice 1d3} hostile {@creature Swarm of Crawling Claws|XMM|Swarms of Crawling Claws}, {@creature Swarm of Insects|XMM|Insects}, or {@creature Swarm of Rats|XMM|Rats} appear in unoccupied spaces within 10 feet of you. This also happens the first time you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB} after an {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} check.
{@b Bloodless.} You cannot spend {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} for any reason, including as the result of a spell or other magical effect.

{@b Corporeal Decay.} Your body begins to rapidly decay, giving you a corpselike appearance. When you gain this mutation, roll a number of {@dice d8|d8s} equal to your character level and take Necrotic damage equal to the result. You have the Undead type in addition to other creature types.

{@b Lignify.} Your limbs stiffen and woody tree shoots pierce from beneath your skin. You have {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Fire damage and your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} (all movement types) is reduced by 5 feet per your level of Corruption.

{@b Scion of the Beast.} You carry some of the Great Beast's corruptive nature. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action on your turn, you and another creature of your choice you can see within 60 feet of you each make a Mutation check.

{@b Third Eye.} You grow a third eye. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or remove the {@condition blinded} condition, but you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks.

{@b Extra Digits.} You grow several extra fingers. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on checks to avoid being disarmed, but you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) checks.

{@b Chameleon.} Your skin changes color in stressful situations. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks, but {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Charisma checks.
{@b Oily Skin.} You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on checks made to {@action Escape a Grapple|XPHB}, but you have {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Cold and Fire damage.

{@b Corrosive Blood.} When you become {@status Bloodied|XPHB} for the first time after an {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} roll, creatures within 5 feet of you take Acid damage equal to your character level.
{@b Sticky Feet.} You gain a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} of 15 feet, but your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet.
{@b Luminescent.} You glow with {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} to a range of 30 feet. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks.
{@b Thinning Blood.} Your bodily fluids become thin and watery. You have the {@condition Bleeding|GrimHollowPG24} condition.

{@b Stone Shell.} Your skin swells and hardens into a tumorous rocky texture. You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Piercing and Slashing damage, and {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Acid and Thunder damage.

{@b Arcane Conduit.} Your body becomes a conduit of magic. Add your current Corruption level to your spell save {@variantrule Difficulty Class|XPHB|DC} and your spell attack rolls. When you cast a spell using a spell slot, make a Mutation check.
{@b Malformed Wings.} Spiny, tattered wings burst painfully from your back, giving you a Fly {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} of 20 feet. You cannot move by any other means.

{@b Blood-Fueled Frenzy.} If you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on melee attack rolls, and attack rolls against you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}. On each of your turns, you must first move as far as possible toward the nearest {@status Bloodied|XPHB} creature you can see. If you are within 5 feet of it after moving, you must take the {@action Attack} action to attack that creature with a melee weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

{@b Eldritch Combustion.} Your body fills with unstable eldritch power. If you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} you die instantly, and each creature within 20 feet of you must make a Mutation check.

{@b Permanent Transformation.} You gain the {@charoption Aberrant Horror|GrimHollowPG24|Aberrant Horror Transformation}. If you already have this or another Transformation, you move to the next stage of that Transformation instead.

name: Behir
rows: The scales of a behir resemble a dragon's but are different in many ways in the eyes of a trained observer. While these scales are often found decorating items in an unscrupulous tailor's shop marketed as actual dragon scales, the fact that they are much smoother and more flexible than an actual dragon's makes them much more useful for fashion.

entries: The horn of a behir is composed of a unique keratin that has an odd reaction to the presence of dragons. A dragon's mere presence causes these horns to resonate, usually alerting a behir to the presence of their hated foe. The horns will still function in the hands of anyone else, but the dragon usually must be much closer for the vibrations to be detected.

entries.name: Use:
entries: When within 1 mile of a dragon (whether it in its true form or {@spell polymorph|phb|polymorphed} into a different shape), this horn will begin to vibrate, with the vibrations becoming more pronounced the closer it is to the dragon. This horn does not indicate the direction of the dragon, only its general proximity.

This large, but surprisingly light leathery sack is located at the back of the behir's cavernous mouth, and is roughly the size of a picnic basket. Inside is a mixture of chemicals, fluids and enzymes that when exposed to the open air, erupts in a destructive crackle of lightning. While extremely dangerous, alchemists and weaponsmiths alike will crawl over themselves to obtain some of this powerful energy.

entries.name: Use:
entries: The lightning sack can be thrown by itself up to a range of 20 feet. If thrown, the lightning sack will explode on impact, dealing {@damage 4d10} lightning damage to all creatures in a 10 foot radius, or half that on a successful {@dc 14} Dexterity saving throw.

name: Beholder
rows: The anatomy of a beholder is infinitely alien and strange to any scholar native to the Material Plane. One of the most curious features of the beholder is that aside from its brain, the beholder features a noticeable dearth of internal organs. Instead, any internal space not occupied by brain matter is filled with a large rubbery balloon that seems to act as the beholder's heart, lungs, and stomach. How it achieves all of these simultaneous functions is unknown. This organ is as versatile as its owner, and many scholars are eager to obtain a complete sample for their research into transmutation.

entries: While the eye stalks of the beholder may be severed from its body, they still retain some of the magical energy that allowed them to fire powerful rays at their enemies. Skilled artificers can take these stalks and use them as the cores of magical wands that emit the same types of rays they emitted in life. Alternatively, four of the intact stalks may be used as part of a ritual to summon a {@creature spectator|MM}.
If a player harvests an eye stalk, roll {@dice 1d10}. The type of eye stalk they receive corresponds to the number rolled, as described in the {@creature beholder|MM} statblock.

rows: The main eye of the beholder is unique in that instead of issuing forth a beam of magical energy, it instead does the opposite: emitting a cone of nullification that disrupts the Weave and prevents the functioning of any magic it gazes at. While it is inactive due to being severed from a living beholder, learned wizards know how to transfigure this organ into an anti-magic crystal, the type that can be used to protect their own strongholds against magical incursions.

name: Belua Fight Faction
rows: {@dice 1d2} {@creature Grey Templar hunter|SGttEH-HoS|Grey Templar hunters} with AC 20 {@homebrew |(see SGttEH page 319)}
{@creature Edward Thistlemane|SGttEH-HoS|Thistlemane} ({@creature hunter|SGttEH}, see SGttEH page 319) and 3 Militia {@creature guard|MM|guards} (reroll if rolled previously)

{@creature Annabella Laroche|SGttEH-HoS} ({@creature jaeger|SGttEH} wielding a {@item dream executioner|SGttEH}, {@homebrew |see SGttEH page 347 & 221}) and 2 Grey Templar {@creature zealot|SGttEH|zealots} (reroll if rolled previously)

name: Beneficial Mutations
intro: The following mutations do not require any visible changes or distinctions in the character. In other words, people who have these mutations are not obviously recognized as mutants. Most beneficial mutations don't require an action to use them.
rows: {@b Strengthened bones:} Your Constitution score increases by 2.
{@b Improved reason:} Your Wisdom score increases by 2.
{@b Improved musculature:} Your Strength score increases by 2.
{@b Improved nervous system:} Your Dexterity score increases by 2.
{@b Improved neural processes:} Your Intelligence score increases by 2.
{@b Thick hide:} Your AC can't be less than 14, regardless of the armor you are wearing.
{@b Increased lung capacity:} Add five to the number of minutes you can hold your breath.
{@b Adhesion pads:} Your hands and feet have naturally adhesive pads. Climbing doesn't cost you extra movement and you add your proficiency bonus to Strength (Athletics) checks for climbing.
{@b Slippery skin:} You secrete a slippery oil from your skin. You gain advantage on rolls to slip from another's grip, escape from bonds, squeeze through small openings, and so on.

{@b Telekinetic shield:} You reflexively use telekinesis to ward away attacks. As a reaction (which you take when you are hit by an attack) you can give yourself a +2 bonus to AC against the triggering attack.
{@b Suggestive voice:} Your voice is perfectly modulated for speech. You gain proficiency in Deception and Persuasion.

{@b Processor dreams:} When you sleep, you process information so that after you wake, you have advantage on any Intelligence skill checks held over from the previous day. For example, if you have to determine whether an unknown plant is poisonous, you could "sleep on it" and make the determination the next day with advantage on the Intelligence (Nature) check. If you're a creature that doesn't sleep (such as an elf), you gain this benefit after your equivalent of sleeping (elven trance counts as sleep for this purpose).
{@b Poison resistance:} You have advantage on saving throws against poison, and you have resistance against poison damage.
{@b Disease resistance:} You have advantage on saving throws against disease, and you have resistance against necrotic damage from diseases.
{@b Fire resistance:} You have resistance against fire damage.
{@b Cold resistance:} You have resistance against cold damage.
{@b Psychic resistance:} You have resistance against psychic damage.
{@b Acid resistance:} You have resistance against acid damage.
{@b Piercing resistance:} You have resistance against piercing damage.
{@b Slashing resistance:} You have resistance against slashing damage.
{@b Bludgeoning resistance:} You have resistance against bludgeoning damage.
{@b No scent:} You have no odor. All creatures have disadvantage on using their sense of smell to notice, find, sense, or track you.

{@b Keen scent:} You can sense creatures, objects, and terrain by scent as well as a normal human can by sight. You can detect scents with that degree of accuracy only within 25 feet, but you can sense strong odors from much farther away (far better than a normal human can). Like a hound, you can track creatures by their scent. You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell.

{@b Sense material:} You can sense the presence of any single substance within 25 feet, although you don't learn details or the precise location. You and the GM should work together to determine the substance: water, iron, synth, granite, wood, flesh, salt, and so on. You do not need to concentrate to sense the material.

name: Berbalang
rows: While there is no verifiable use for the ears of a berbalang, they still hold a certain popularity among those that study necromantic magics. It is commonly believed, truthfully or not, that they increase a mage's ability to sense the dead and respond to their hidden desires.

A berbalang is capable of communicating with just about anything, and yet, it rarely speaks. It saves its few precious words only for those that cannot respond: the dead. As frustrating as that may be to any living person trying to extract information from them, it does mean that harvesters can find their tongues in near-mint condition.

entries: One of a berbalang's more interesting abilities is its creation of spectral duplicates created through sheer force of will. Usually used for spying and information gathering, the mental strain does render the real berbalang comatose during the attempt. I suppose that nothing highlights the berbalang's propensity for introversion quite like the fact that it finds even its own company boring enough to sleep through.

entries.name: Use:
entries: While this brain is in your hand, you may spend your action to {@status concentration|PHB|concentrate} on it. If you do so, you summon a spectral double of yourself in an unoccupied space within 60 feet of you. While the duplicate exists, you are {@condition unconscious}. The duplicate disappears when it or you drop to 0 hit points or when you dismiss it (no action required).

Your duplicate has the same statistics and knowledge as you, but cannot cast spells and has no equipment when created. Everything experienced by your duplicate is known to you. All damage dealt by your duplicate is psychic damage. Once this item is used once, it shrivels away and becomes useless.

name: Bheur Hag
rows: Despite resembling the hoar frost that grows on spider webs, the hair of a bheur hag is surprisingly supple and flexible. Possessing traces of the hag's ancient frost magic, these hairs have been repurposed into strings for various inventions, imparting their wintery power wherever they are used.

Absolutely reeking of the foulness that permeated the hag's entire being, drinking this blood has the potential to infect a creature with {@disease crone's disease|HHHVI}. It should also be noted that while the blood smells and tastes as fetid as it looks, alcohol has a neutralising effect on both of these properties. What someone does with that information is entirely out of this writer's control.

Once removed from its taut, frozen flesh, the skull of a bheur hag flashes a constant rictus grin. It stares back at whoever gazes at it, mocking them with thoughts of anxiety and desperation regardless of their current situation. It is dangerous to use in crafting, but when done well, can create an item that oozes with dark magic and the slow of winter.

entries: Not to be confused with the notorious "hag eye" amulet given by hags to their servants, however the two are tightly linked. Despite being severed from its socket, this eye still seems to glare as it did in life.

entries.name: Use:
entries: As an action you may {@condition concentration|PHB|concentrate} on the hag eyeball while it is in your hand. While doing so, you may utilise that hag's hag eye that same way they would have used it in life. If the hag eye is destroyed while you are concentrating on the hag eyeball, you suffer {@damage 3d10} psychic damage and are {@condition blinded} for 24 hours.

name: Black Abishai
rows: An abishai is created when {@deity Tiamat|Dawn War|DMG} interferes with the cycle of life and death, snagging a mortal soul before it can move on and transforming it into a monstrous draconic creature to serve her whims in the Hells. This act permanently scars a soul, staining it with the Dragon Queen's mark for all eternity. Upon the abishai's death, this mark can be captured by an enterprising harvester and used to channel the power of {@deity Tiamat|Dawn War|DMG} against her will. {@b Requires {@item spirit paper|HHHVI}.}

Like real dragons, the abishai are gifted with the power of flight by their queen. The powerful wings that they bear are capable of tremendously high speeds, and like many devils, can be harvested and recrafted into the ever useful {@item infernal wings|HHHVI}.

The needs of {@deity Tiamat|Dawn War|DMG} are many, and she creates her servants to serve specific functions. This usually comes in the form of the abishai's horns which, much like a real dragon, contain much of the essence of their power. The black abishai is a master of infiltration and subterfuge, fueled by the dark magic in their horns. Alchemists have found ways to ground their horns down into a disorienting powder that is prized by thieves and assassins alike.

entries: A sample of a black pudding. Inert due to lacking enough biomass to constitute a full ooze, it nevertheless retains its acidic properties. Can be used as a potent acid. {@b Requires {@item enchanted vial|HHHVI}.}

entries.name: Use:
entries: A vial of black residue can be poured onto nonmagical wood or metal. The black residue eats through 2 inches of these materials per round for the next 10 rounds, after which the ooze becomes too diluted to continue.

name: Blessings
caption: Blessing
rows: Fine dining. Whenever you eat out, the dishes are always clean.
Recently bathed. You always smell clean.
I'm on a diet. You can eat half as much as normal.
Quick sleeper. You never have trouble falling asleep.
Upkeep. Your equipment is always in top repair.
Minty. Your breath is always fresh.
Fast metabolism. You can eat all you want without getting fat.
Shades. The sun is never in your eyes.
Everybody knows your name. Your favorite seat at your favorite tavern is always empty.
Quick reader. You never lose your place while reading.
He saved my spot. Nobody ever cares when you cut in line.
Permanent Press. Your clothes are always wrinkle-free.
Golden smile. Your teeth are always free of debris.
Ready to go. You don't experience bedhead.
This little piggy. Stubbing your toes is a thing of the past.
Give me five. Your high fives are never left hanging.
It's on me. If you're short by 5 copper pieces, the person behind you always covers it.
Who do your hairdo? It's impossible for you to have a bad hair day.
Well mannered. You never burp/fart during social interactions, unless you really want to.
Lovely complexion. Your skin is always clear of blemishes.
Laugh attack. Somebody always laughs at your jokes.
Beer me. You never get served warm ale/mead.
Feathered friends. Birds never poop on you. This may have negative effects on those around you.
Just like mama used to make. The food you are served is always served at the correct temperature.
Rose petal. Your farts don't stink.
Pocket lock-it. Nobody ever tries to pick your pocket.
Looking dapper. Your hair is never greasy.
Smooth moves. You have an advantage when trying to avoid tripping.
Alarm clock. You always manage to wake up right when you need/want to.
Mr. Sandman. You always have pleasant dreams.
Forget the odds. If someone tries to attack you, roll {@dice 1d4}. On a 4, they decide to attack someone else.
Looking sharp. It's impossible for you to look disheveled.
Flipside. Your pillow is always on the cool side.
Minor annoyance. Mosquitoes find you repulsive.
Suave. Your preferred gender finds you slightly attractive. You gain temporary proficiency with all social skills used while talking to your preferred gender.
Know it all. You always have the answer to useless trivia questions. Add 5 to your intelligence rolls when rolling for useless information.
Disarming smile. Once a day your smile grants you advantage to persuasion checks.
Nose for trouble. Once a day gain advantage on an insight check.
Walk softly. Once a day gain advantage on a stealth check.
Saw it coming. Once a day for a single round of combat you can add your perception modifier to your AC.
Commanding presence. Once a day gain advantage on an intimidation check.
Honeyed words. Once a day gain advantage on a persuasion check.
Said the liar. Once a day gain advantage on a deception check.
Triathlete. Once a day gain advantage on an athletics check.
Sheep's clothing. Once a day you can select a creature/person and learn their alignment.
Special dispensation. Once a day gain advantage on a religion check
What's yours is mine. Once a day gain advantage on a sleight of hand check.
Soft landing. Once a day gain advantage on an acrobatics check.
Glass half full. Healing potions have two uses for you.
Divine umbrella. For some reason, you never get wet when it rains, snows, or hails.
Graced tongue. You learn a new language.
Penny pincher. Every time you reach into your coin purse, roll {@dice 1d4}. You gain this number of coppers.
Silver tongue. Once a day gain advantage on a performance check.
Guiding spirit. Once a day gain advantage on a saving throw.
Spirit animal. (Pick any animal.) You gain advantage on all skill rolls used on this animal.
Hawkeye. Once a day gain advantage on a ranged attack.
History buff. Once a day gain advantage on a history check.
Self-diagnosed. Once a day gain advantage on a medicine skill check.
Arcane surge. Once a day when either casting a spell or using a magic weapon, double the damage die.
An apple a day. You have advantage on saving throws against disease.
Night owl. Gain 30ft of dark vision. This stacks with pre-existing dark vision.
Quick footed. Your movement/speed is increased by 5ft.
Early bird. From sunrise Until noon, you have proficiency in all skills.
Star born. From sunset to midnight you have proficiency in all skills.
God smack. Once a day deal double bludgeoning damage.
Strong stomach. You have advantage on all constitution saves to avoid being poisoned.
Footwork. Once a day you can ignore rough terrain for the duration of an encounter.
Undead nightmare. Once a day you can cast Turn Undead on ONE target. No spell slots required.
Thick-skinned. When you take slashing, piercing, or bludgeoning damage, reduce the damage by 1/2 of your Constitution rounded down.
Eagle eye. The range of all ranged attacks/spells is increased by 100ft.
Ignore the pain. Once a day when you are attacked, you can roll {@dice 1d10}. Subtract this number from the damage dealt.
Fueled by pain. If you are dealt 15 points of damage in a single attack, you gain advantage on all rolls made your next turn.
Unmatched immune system. You're resistant to disease.
Shared pain. Once a day, when attacked, you can use a reaction to split the same amount of damage you just received with your attacker.
Sun-kissed. While the sun shines upon you, you gain fire resistance.
Moonchild. While the Moon shines upon you you gain resistance to Cold.
Falling star. If you fall for over 30ft, you can make a melee attack DC 20. If you succeed, you take no damage but deal the damage you would've taken to anyone nearby. This damage is divided equally.
New skill. Gain proficiency in a skill you're not already proficient in.
Rat king. You gain a familiar. This familiar takes the form of a rat. It shares the same stats as a rat. If killed, it returns to you the following day.
Lucky day. You always have an advantage when gambling.
Fortune fairies. Once a week your coin purse gains 2% of the gold it currently has. If you have 100gp, you earn 2gp.
Fey's blessing. You have advantage against being charmed or frightened.
Comeback. Once a day, after throwing a thrown weapon, roll {@dice 1d10}. On a 10, the weapon reappears in your hand.
Return to sender. Once a day, when targeted by a ranged attack/spell, roll {@dice 1d10}. On a 10 the attack/spell targets the attacker instead.
Life-giver. Once a day, when you successfully land an attack, you can heal an ally for the amount of damage you dealt.
Sure-grip. You can no longer be disarmed in combat.
Sure foot. You can no longer be knocked prone.
Anointed. You are resistant to necrotic/unholy damage.
Desecrated. You are resistant to radiant/holy damage.
Death cloak. Once a day, whenever a person dies within 10 ft of you, you regain 3d10hp.

Mind blast. Once a day you can make a wisdom check with a DC of 15. If you succeed, all hostiles within a 15ft radius of you take {@damage 4d4} psychic damage and must immediately make a wisdom/willpower save DC 15. If they fail they are stunned.

Divine javelin. Once a day you can conjure up a javelin of radiant energy. This javelin deals {@damage 2d8} radiant damage if thrown, or {@damage 2d10} radiant damage if used as a melee weapon. It dissipates immediately after use.
Noticed. All ability scores increase by 1
Prodigy. Choose one skill you are proficient in. You now get to double your proficiency with it.
Insane immune system.You are immune to disease.
Blessed. All ability scores increase by 2
Strong mind. You're resistant to psychic damage.
Thick-skinned. You are resistant to piercing, bludgeoning, and slashing damage.
Friend of the elements. You are resistant to Fire, Cold, Lightning, poison, and acid damage.
Known not by death. Once a month, when reduced to 0hp, you bounce back up the following round with full hp, and all class features unused.

name: Blessings
rows: {@skill Medicine} ({@item healer's kit|PHB}, {@item herbalism kit|TLotRR}, ring)

name: Bloodmire Diseases
rows: Bloodburnt Rash: At the start of each of your turns when you are not under the bloodwater, you take {@damage 1d6} fire damage. This disease lasts until you take fire damage equal to half your hit point maximum in this way.

Crimson Sight: Your eyes become bloodshot, your pupils dilate, and your senses of safety and danger become twisted. Whenever you see a fey or humanoid, flip a coin. If it's heads, you consider that creature to be a friendly acquaintance. If it's tails, you consider the creature to be a hostile enemy. You consider any fiend or fiendish villager to be a friendly acquaintance, even if it's under the effect of illusory magic. This disease lasts until you finish a long rest.

Rusting Flesh: Sometimes called the Iron Curse, this disease causes your flesh to corrode and slough off. You take {@damage 1d8} necrotic damage and your maximum hit points are reduced by the same amount each day at dusk. If your hit point maximum drops to 0 in this way, you die. This disease lasts until 7 days have passed.

Blood Lunacy: A rare and weakened form of lycanthropy. You suffer disadvantage on saving throws against contracting lycanthropy. Your hair begins to grow long and thick, and you gain no benefit from finishing a short or long rest during a full moon. This disease lasts until it's cured by magical means.

name: Bloodmire Exploration; Becoming Lost
rows: Amid backtracking and great confusion, the party ends the day up to {@dice 2d6} miles in a random direction away from their destination if sailing, or {@dice 1d6} miles away if walking.
Using the gradual current of blood emanating from the Verdant Heart, the party ends the day up to {@dice 1d6} miles away from their destination despite being lost.

name: Bloodmire Exploration; Bloodmire Navigation DCs
rows: A location in the outskirts of the Bloodmire, or near an outpost
A location near the center of the mire, such as the Verdant Heart.
A location hidden from view, such as a sprite village, secret island, or forgotten fey portal.

name: Bloodmire Exploration; Diseased Foraged Food
rows: The character is {@condition poisoned} for 8 hours and rolls on the {@table Bloodmire Diseases|GriffonsSaddlebag2|Bloodmire disease} table.
The character is {@condition poisoned} for 1 hour.
The character is not nourished but suffers no other ill effects.

name: Bloodmire Exploration; Encounters
rows: A corrupted fey portal that allows instant travel to a realm of shadows and dread during the new moon.
A hidden, quicksand-like pool of diseased blood. Each character must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or become diseased (see {@table Bloodmire Diseases|GriffonsSaddlebag2} table).

{@dice 1d4} carnivorous plants. The same number of characters must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or suffer {@damage 2d8} slashing damage and become diseased (see {@table Bloodmire Diseases|GriffonsSaddlebag2} table) as the plants' vines slice into exposed flesh.
A grove of abundant bloodfern. Spending 1 hour gathering yields {@dice 1d4} pounds per character, up to a maximum of 30 pounds.
A fallen bloodbark tree. Spending 1 hour with an axe yields {@dice 2d12} pounds per character, up to a maximum of 48 pounds.

{@dice 1d4} {@creature giant mosquito|GriffonsSaddlebag2|giant mosquitoes} (see appendix B) ({@chance 60|60%}) or {@creature swarm of giant mosquitoes|GriffonsSaddlebag2|swarms of giant mosquitoes} (see appendix B) ({@chance 40|40%})
{@dice 1d3} {@creature giant blood eel|GriffonsSaddlebag2|giant blood eels} (see appendix B)
{@dice 3d4} {@creature giant frog|MM|giant frogs} ({@chance 50|50%}) or {@creature giant poisonous snake|MM|giant snakes} ({@chance 50|50%})
{@dice 2d6} fugitives ({@creature bandit||outlaws}) hunting for food. They leave peacefully if given rations/supplies, but otherwise attack.
{@dice 1d4} {@creature Crimson Legion Imp|GriffonsSaddlebag2|Crimson Legion imps} (see appendix B) prowling for violence.
A dense cloud of diseased insects. Each character must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or become diseased (see {@table Bloodmire Diseases|GriffonsSaddlebag2} table).

Old fey ruins buried under mud and submerged in the swamp. Murals of the war ({@chance 75|75%}) or carved poetry about Syre ({@chance 25|25%}) can be found with a DC 17 Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check.
A battlefield from the war. Fey and fiendish weapons and armor long corroded ({@chance 90|90%}) or intact ({@chance 10|10%}).
A partially submerged fey monument depicting a bold warrior. A successful DC 18 Intelligence ({@skill Religion}) check recognizes the ancient hero as Syre.
{@dice 1d8} {@creature sprite|MM|sprites} out scouting in secret for intelligence (Reroll if the party is far away from the Verdant Heart).
An intact fey portal that allows instant travel to the sprite village in the Verdant Heart while a waxing crescent moon is overhead.

name: Bloodmire Exploration; Example Dungeons
rows: Hidden and carefully guarded under the bloodwater of a Crimson Legion village is an alchemical laboratory that contains a stockpile of broken fey orbs. Careful investigation could reveal the history of these orbs as well as a way to disable them.

A once-prominent fortress built by Syre and his warriors is now almost completely destroyed by plantlife, mud, and bloodwater. The sturdy yet sunken walls are now home to a variety of monstrous amphibians, reptiles, and other beasts. Perhaps some carved hints about the Bloodmire's origin or ancient artifacts could be salvaged.

High in the canopy, a large number of giant mosquitoes have made a strange hive that's reminiscent of a wasp's nest. Local refugees weren't concerned about the hive until the insects started abducting children and small adults. They suspect that the people stolen are being used to build, or possibly feed, something deep within the hive's tunnels.

One of the very few intact fey portals leads to Syre's hidden demiplane: a tower filled with magical traps, libraries, and fey heirlooms. Whether led there by sprites or found by chance, only the bravest adventurers would be capable of journeying to the end to find the mysterious treasure Syre left behind. However, even the few remaining sprites can't remember what it might be.

A fey portal has become corrupted by the Bloodmire's curses. Each new moon, the portal sparks to life and allows travel to a realm full of shades, dark magic, and terrors of the night. While it's open, this portal allows these strange nightmares to leak out and terrorize the swamp's inhabitants with otherworldly monsters. Unless someone can find a way to close the portal, the Bloodmire may fall completely under its sway.

Rumor tells that a group of bandits have amassed a hoard of treasure somewhere in the Bloodmire that's filled with gold, goods, and supplies stolen from merchants who were careless or desperate enough to travel through the swamp unprotected.

name: Bludgeoning, Force, or Thunder Injury
rows: {@b Destroyed Eye.} You have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight and ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB|Attack Rolls}. This can be restored with the {@spell Regenerate|XPHB} spell.

{@b Broken Arm or Hand.} You can no longer hold anything with two hands, and you can hold only a single object at a time. All {@variantrule Ability Check|XPHB|Ability Checks} and {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB|Attack Rolls} made with it have disadvantage. This can be healed with the {@spell Mend Flesh and Bones|WoBrCa} spell. After 2 weeks it becomes a Major Bruise.

{@b Broken Foot or Leg.} Your speed on foot is halved, and you must use a cane or crutch to move. You fall {@condition Prone|XPHB} after ending your movement when using the {@action Dash|XPHB} action. All {@variantrule Ability Check|XPHB|Ability Checks} and {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB|Attack Rolls} made with it have disadvantage. This can be healed with the {@spell Mend Flesh and Bones|WoBrCa} spell. After 2 weeks it becomes a Major Bruise.

{@b Internal Injury.} You have to move much more carefully when you take your actions. If you take both an action and bonus action on your turn or take a reaction, you lose {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your level. This reduction cannot be reduced. The internal injury can be healed with the {@spell Mend Flesh and Bones|WoBrCa} spell. After 2 weeks the Internal Injury will naturally heal.
{@b Broken Rib.} This has the same effect as the Internal Injury, but the damage you take is equal to half your level (round up).

{@b Limp.} Your speed on foot is reduced by 5 feet. All {@variantrule Ability Check|XPHB|Ability Checks} and {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB|Attack Rolls} made with the foot have disadvantage. You must make a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw after ending your movement when you take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action. If you fail the save, you fall {@condition Prone|XPHB}. This can be healed with the {@spell Heal Minor Wounds|WoBrCa} spell.

{@b Major Bruise.} You get a bad bruise in a place very visible to others. You have disadvantage on Charisma (Persuasion) and advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks. This can be removed with the {@spell Heal Minor Wounds|WoBrCa} spell. After 1 week the Major Bruise will naturally heal.
{@b Bruises.} The bruise doesn't have any adverse effect. This can be removed with the {@spell Heal Minor Wounds|WoBrCa} spell. After 1 week the Bruise will naturally heal.

name: Blue Abishai
rows: An abishai is created when {@deity Tiamat|Dawn War|DMG} interferes with the cycle of life and death, snagging a mortal soul before it can move on and transforming it into a monstrous draconic creature to serve her whims in the Hells. This act permanently scars a soul, staining it with the Dragon Queen's mark for all eternity. Upon the abishai's death, this mark can be captured by an enterprising harvester and used to channel the power of {@deity Tiamat|Dawn War|DMG} against her will. {@b Requires {@item spirit paper|HHHVI}.}

Like real dragons, the abishai are gifted with the power of flight by their queen. The powerful wings that they bear are capable of tremendously high speeds, and like many devils, can be harvested and recrafted into the ever useful {@item infernal wings|HHHVI}.

The needs of {@deity Tiamat|Dawn War|DMG} are many, and she creates her servants to serve specific functions. This usually comes in the form of the abishai's horns which, much like a real dragon, contain much of the essence of their power. The blue abishai are the spellcasters of {@deity Tiamat|Dawn War|DMG|Tiamat's} armies, weaving her draconic magic to destroy her enemies. Once crafted into a wand, an erstwhile spellcaster may use it to unleash the destructive power of {@deity Tiamat|Dawn War|DMG} herself.

name: Blue Energy
rows: The light absorbs the character's life force. The character drops to 0 hit points but is stable.

The character takes 3 ({@damage 1d6}) damage of each of the following types: cold, force, lightning, necrotic, psychic, and radiant. Roll separately for each type. If any result is 6, the character is also pushed 20 feet directly away from the light. If that pushes them off the platform, they fall. If they hit the wall, they take 7 ({@damage 2d6}) bludgeoning damage.

The character's highest and lowest ability scores become swapped. They return to normal when the character finishes a long rest and makes a successful {@dc 12} saving throw using the lower of the two swapped abilities (one check per rest).

The character transforms into a {@creature manticore|MM}. Swap that player's character sheet for the {@creature manticore|MM} stat block. The character returns to normal after completing a long rest and making a successful {@dc 9} Wisdom saving throw (one check per rest). You can substitute {@filter a different challenge 3 creature|bestiary|source=|Challenge Rating=[&3]|miscellaneous=!adventure npc} if you prefer.

The character turns to liquid. The liquid retains a humanoid shape, but the character can't grasp objects or wear armor, clothing, or jewelry. Swap that player's character sheet for the water elemental stat block. The character effectively becomes a water elemental with four differences: the character's size is Medium, it retains its own hit points and its own languages, and it doesn't have the water elemental's Whelm action. The character returns to normal after completing a long rest and making a successful {@dc 7} Wisdom saving throw (one check per rest).

The character's body explodes into motes of light. All their gear and clothing falls to the floor in a heap. It takes the character a minute to reform into a swirl of bobbing lights that resembles a cloud of fireflies. Swap that player's character sheet for the will-o-wisp stat block, with three differences: the character is still alive (not undead), it's Medium size, and it doesn't have the will-o-wisp's Invisibility action. The character returns to normal after completing a long rest and making a successful {@dc 10} Wisdom saving throw (one check per rest).
outro: Characters who transform into something else retain their original alignment, in addition to other exceptions.

name: Blue Slaad
rows: The slime that coats a slaad smells like the bottom of a fetid swamp and looks like it too. It is believed that this slime has an innocuation effect against the diseases and parasitic eggs of the slaads, but this is mostly just conjecture. Otherwise, it is a mere curiosity for eccentric researchers.

entries: Slaadi are creatures of pure chaos, born from the unstable energies in Limbo. As such, their very bodies disrupt the natural order of things and those that consume some of their flesh tend to find that probability itself changes for them, if only temporarily. Beware however, as the universe is not to be trifled with, and it tends to find ways to balance itself out later.

entries.name: Use:
entries: As an action you may eat this item. If you do so, then once within the next 10 minutes you may choose to bend the laws of fate within your favour. If you do so, you gain advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. If you choose not to, this item is wasted. After those 10 minutes have passed, your DM may choose at any time within the next 24 hours to impose disadvantage on 1 attack roll, ability check, or saving throw you make.

rows: The hooked claws of a blue slaad contain wicked hooks that dig into flesh and act as vectors for the transmission of the dreaded "chaos phage." This disease does not live long after the death of its slaad host, however that does not still mean that it cannot be used in nefarious artificing to create a weapon of even deadlier design.

name: Bodak
rows: The infamous mace and skull symbol of {@creature Orcus|MTF} is carved into every bodak's chest, regardless of their origin. These blasphemous symbols maintain a strong connection to {@creature Orcus|MTF} even after the defeat of its bodak, and there are techniques to use them to channel the demon lord's power for dark and powerful curses.

Pure white, blank and incredibly disturbing. Filled with the unholy, necrotic energies of the demon prince {@creature Orcus|MTF}, these eyes can be worked upon by a talented thaumaturge to create a rather morbid set of goggles that allow the wielder to literally see death wherever they look.

entries: One of the varieties of oil that a boggle is capable of creating, a sticky, tar-like substance that traps those unlucky enough to step in it. While not the strongest of substances, it can prove to be quite the nuisance (as anyone with a boggle in their house will discover after they rise from their chamber pot to discover it sticking to their backside).

entries.name: Use:
entries: You may spend an action to coat yourself with this oil. For the next hour, you have advantage on Strength ({@skill Athletics}) checks made to {@action grapple} and any ability check made to maintain a hold on another creature, surface, or object. You can also climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check. Alternatively, you may spend an action to pour this oil on the ground, creating a 5 foot puddle where poured for 1 hour. Any creature that enters that puddle or starts its turn there must succeed on a {@dc 11} Strength saving throw or be {@condition restrained}. On its turn, a creature can use an action to try to extricate itself from the sticky puddle, ending the effect and moving into the nearest safe unoccupied space with a successful {@dc 11} Strength check.

The other variety of oil that a boggle is capable of creating, a slippery substance that makes surfaces virtually impossible to traverse. One of a boggle's most reliable pranks is to simply oil the area around a house's larder, causing anyone entering it to slip and spill all sorts of foodstuffs on themselves.

name: Bone Devil
rows: The bones of the bone devil are considerably durable and feel more like steel than bone. They can be refashioned into a suite of fire-resistant tools, but due to their origin, not many are willing to use them.

Despite their appearance, a bone devil actually does possess skin; a dessicated sheet that is stretched tight over its bones. While those properties are undesirable in a skin, they make for a perfect sheet of vellum. Indeed, the infamous skin-bound abyssal tomes found in dark libraries are often made using bone devil skin.

The stinger of the bone devil's tail is sharp enough to pierce through even the toughest of armor and deliver a potent dose of debilitating venom. With a few modifications, this tail can be adapted into a whip to store and deliver any kind of poison the wielder wishes.

The diaphanous but extraordinarily strong wings of the bone devil. Despite their relatively fragile appearance, they are strong enough to hold the considerably heavy bone devil aloft and allow it to fly at high speeds.

name: Bone Naga
rows: Virtually identical to the bones of an ordinary serpent, except on a larger scale. When ground up into a powder and then brewed into a tea however, it creates an intoxicating drink that some cultures have used for spiritual purposes. Those that have drunk it have claimed visions of long-forgotten histories, but they are inevitably forgotten once the drink has left their system.

Nagas require no glands to produce their venom as their fangs remain venomous even when the naga is reduced to a skeletal form. Proper extraction and then re-smithing allows these fangs to serve as powerful weapons with an extra poisonous punch. Beware though, as a revived naga may not take kindly to the idea of a mortal running around with one of their teeth.

name: Boneclaw
rows: As a reflection of its malformed existence, a boneclaw garbs itself in a shadowy substance in a pale imitation of the grand finery found on real liches. While not nearly as regal, the shadows do possess some trace of the boneclaw's magic and thus are useful for all manners of alchemy and dark magic. {@b Requires {@item enchanted vial|HHHVI}.}

Rather than favoring the dark magic synonymous with liches, a boneclaw utilizes the more mundane, but no less intimidating, eponymous bone claws. Perfectly shaped to reach, rend, and restrain hapless victims, these claws make fantastic weapons for trapping and finishing off wounded opponents.

Although it is imperfect, a boneclaw still possesses a phylactery like a real lich; or it is more accurate to say that the phylactery possesses it. In a mockery of their failure to perform the ritual correctly, a boneclaw is indentured to a mortal creature who serves as the boneclaw's phylactery. So long as the creature lives, so does the boneclaw. It is not always clear who acts as the boneclaw's phylactery, sometimes not even to the boneclaw itself. To circumvent this, certain enchantments can be performed on a well preserved boneclaw head, allowing one to track down the living phylactery and end the menace of the boneclaw, once and for all.

name: Bout of Madness
rows: {@b Cower.} Whenever you fail a Sanity saving throw badly, you may temporarily go insane. When this happens, roll on the following table, to apply a form of insanity your character will temporarily adhere to. Another creature can attempt to snap you out of your madness, by using their action by making a Wisdom (Medicine) check (DC 15). On a success the creature is no longer affected by the Bout of Madness. On a failure that creature cannot attempt it again.
{@b Freeze.} The character is unable to move from their spot by themselves. They can still take actions, if the player wants them to, provided they do not make the character move.

{@b Impulsive.} The character is unable to think strategically and acts impulsively, which may lead to situations where they, for example, use all their powerful abilities when they normally would conserve them. The player can choose in what way the character is negatively impacted by acting impulsively.
{b Aggression.} The character becomes very aggressive. This may out itself in attacking the closest creature, destroying objects, or any other way the player deems fitting.

{@b Hesitation.} The character is unsure of what to do in the current situation. Whenever the character wants to use their action for something, they must succeed on an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw (DC 10), their choice. On a failure they must take any other action of their choice.

{@b Faint.} The character falls unconscious, until you take damage or someone uses their action to shake you awake. At the end of their turns, after awakening, your character must make an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw (DC 15), their choice, as long as their source of madness is within sight. On a failure, they fall unconscious again.

name: Brawl Mishaps
caption: Brawl Mishaps
rows: A {@creature thug|MM} comes charging in from an adjacent room and slams a ship's wheel over the head of a character, dealing 11 ({@damage 2d10}) bludgeoning damage on a hit.

A stray flagon flies through the air and hits One-Eyed-Bill the {@creature wereshark|BelzorMM} ({@adventure appendix B|BelzorMM|12}), who transforms into a human-shark hybrid and attacks whoever is closest.
A hulking {@creature Half-Ogre (Ogrillon)|mm|half-ogre} pirate slams a pair of rogues into one of the tavern's walls, causing it to give way entirely. The brawl then spills out into the street.

One of the lamps lighting the tavern is smashed, and the burning oil spills onto a platter of drinks, starting a serious fire in a 10-foot-square. A creature in the fire takes 11 ({@damage 2d10}) fire damage and ignites, taking 3 ({@damage 1d6}) fire damage at the start of each of their turns. The fire can be doused with an action and spreads at the DM's discretion.

The rotted base of the main mast gives way as a thug is thrown at it, and slides into the room through the ceiling. Each creature in a 5-foot-wide, 30-foot-long line must make a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw or take 16 ({@damage 3d10}) bludgeoning damage.

Someone throws a smoke bomb into the crowd which explodes in a ten-foot-radius, dealing 2 ({@damage 1d4}) force damage to anyone in the area. The area then fills with thick black smoke, heavily obscuring a 15-foot-sphere of the tavern.

name: Brontosaurus
rows: The massive toes of a brontosaurus are strong and durable enough to support its considerable weight. As such, they make wonderful materials to bludgeon one's opponent with.
{@filter Any +1 melee bludgeoning weapon|items|source=dmg|type=melee weapon|category=|weapon damage type=b|bonus=weapon attack and damage rolls (+1)}

One would think that the massive neck of a brontosaurus would not be able to support itself, and yet amazingly it does. Even more amazingly, this is achieved not through magic but by mere physics; the neck of a brontosaurus is actually filled with several air sacks that help support its neck and saves on weight. These air sacks may be repurposed for various tools and equipment, including buoyancy aids for ship hulls.

name: Bronze Scout
rows: The internal mechanisms of the clockwork constructs can seem almost like magic for anyone not trained in the tinkering and gnomish sciences. While they may vary from model to model (and indeed, even among the same type of clockwork), they all share the same design for the core set of gears that power its lifelike movements. Tinkers of all breeds value these mastercrafted servos to use in their own creations, and will pay a decent price to avoid having to make them on their own.

The plating of the bronze scout is forged from a unique method that incorporates quartz and minerals into the smelting process. The result is an alloy that not only resonates with the earth, but also has a distinctive amber tone. Unfortunately, the former trait quickly dissipates once disconnected from the construct, but it still retains the attractive coloring and can be recrafted into a rather fetching suit of armor.

entries: The bronze scout is not built for combat, but it does possess a few tricks up its sleeves (despite its lack of arms). The most notable is a literally shocking ability to release a wave of lightning along the ground to distract its foes while it burrows to safety. The core responsible for this is fragile however, and only recharges when still attached to a functioning scout. As such, although it is useful in a pinch, it is a strictly one-time use item only.

entries.name: Note:
entries: This item can only be harvested if the bronze scout had its {@i lightning flare} ability available at the time of its death.

entries.name: Use:
entries: As an action, you may throw this item at the ground up to 15 feet away from you, causing it to explode on impact. All creatures touching the ground within 15 feet of the explosion must make a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 2d6} lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

name: Bugbear
rows: Despite usually being filthy and riddled with mange, an intact bugbear hide can actually serve as very good leather. It is not uncommon for more nomadic people to wear these tanned hides for both comfort and as a sign of their strength.

name: Bugbear Chief
rows: Despite usually being filthy and riddled with mange, an intact bugbear hide can actually serve as very good leather. It is not uncommon for more nomadic people to wear these tanned hides for both comfort and as a sign of their strength.

entries: The most fearsome of bugbears carry with them the blessing of their god Hruggek which allows them to surge past any danger and debilitations. If you are willing to indulge in your own inner savage, you too can take this blessing by consuming the bugbear's heart, but beware of any side effects.

entries.name: Use:
entries: You may spend an action to consume this heart. If you do so, you have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition charmed}, {@condition frightened}, {@condition paralyzed}, {@condition poisoned}, {@condition stunned}, or {@condition unconscious|PHB|put to sleep} for the next hour. Once this effect wears off, you must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or gain one level of {@condition exhaustion} as the adrenaline filled organ passes through your system.

name: Bugbear Lair Details
intro: An area controlled by bugbears might display the following:
rows: A cluster of smoke-dried heads of slain warriors hangs from a hook
An enormous owl has been carefully, if crudely, painted on the wall
Detailed, sprawling patterns have been scratched into the dirt, centered on a black slate slab
A ring is worn into the dirt around a fire pit, dotted with flecks of old, dried blood
A smashed clay bowl has strewn its contents near the door of a canvas tent
Strings of beads, scraps of cloth, and bone charms hang from prominent objects to mark territory borders
A nightmarish carving looms over a sleeping mat to scare away bad dreams
A cleared area with sturdy restraints anchored deep in the ground, stained with a large amount of old troll blood
A lightweight, camouflaged wooden hut, used by bugbears observing prey
A worn, flat stone with a clear view of the sky directly above

name: Bugbear Trinket Table
rows: {@dice 1d4} days' worth of {@item rations (1 day)|PHB|rations} (mouldy produce)
1 badly carved wooden idol of Hruggek

name: Bugbear Trinkets
intro: The following items might be carried by a bugbear:
rows: A bone figurine of a totem animal (cat, boar, deer, wolf etc.), worn smooth from handling
A stone arrowhead carved with notches
A small bowl of pasty ochre paint
A short string of beads; mostly wood, but every third is polished bone inscribed with a rune
A shrunken head with gemstones stitched in the eye sockets
A cured gnoll stomach containing an acidic mash
A wreath of feathers and dried herbs bound together with tightly woven leather strips
A cracked clay bowl stained with dried blood
A troll's claw, which is still slowly growing

name: Buildable Structures
caption: Buildable Structures table
rows: Any room that costs only 1 or 2 room points

name: Bulette
rows: Capable of puncturing even steel armor, bulette teeth are well regarded as materials for crafting daggers and spears. Some cultures even consider bulette hunting to be a rite of passage, using the weapon made from their kill for the rest of their adult lives.
Capable of powerful digging, the bulette claw makes for a wonderful weapon base, one that is capable of piercing rock and metals alike.

While the bulette relies on its powerful jaws and claws to tunnel through solid rock, it is aided by a layer of rock dissolving slime that it exudes constantly from its hide. When harvested quickly, the hide itself retains this property and can be crafted into protective equipment for subterranean adventurers.

name: Bulezau
rows: Despite their solid appearance, the horns of a bulezau are actually spongiform in nature and are used to cultivate colonies of diseases and other pathogens. Once cleaned however, these horns may be repurposed as a fermentation aid, and in fact there are a few varieties of cheese and alcohol that owe their distinctive spicy flavor to this demonic instrument.

entries: The disease ridden bulezau is covered in a multitude of pulsating boils filled with infected pus. A mere whiff of the miasmas in these boils are enough to ruin the health of any but the hardiest of adventurer and thus must be picked extremely carefully by harvesters. If you can manage to bring them back to an alchemist intact however, they can be brewed into an incredibly deadly tincture.

entries.name: Use:
entries: As an action, you may throw this item at a space within 20 feet of you, causing the boils inside to burst on impact. When you do so, all creatures within 30 feet of the item must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 1d6} necrotic damage.

rows: Anyone that has seen a bulezau in action can attest to the terrifying way that its tail flicks and swats at its enemies, spreading a horrifying disease to whomever it hits. This is largely attributable to the spines on the tail which are not only sharp, but are also hollow and filled with infectious contagions. With a few alchemical alterations however, these spines can be repurposed to actually draw diseases out of the user (so long as they can put up with the pain, that is).

name: Bullywug
rows: A bullywug tongue is remarkably long for their size and incredibly tough. Swamp folk can often be found drying these and using them as rope substitutes.

name: Bullywug Trinket Table
rows: {@dice 1d4} days' worth of {@item rations (1 day)|PHB|rations} (swamp plants and critters)
1 pouch of grey mud (good for pores)
{@dice 1d8} bundles of mildly intoxicating roots and leaves

name: Burial and Treasure Table
intro: The contents of each sealed crypt can be determined randomly as characters force them open. {@b Using the Burial and Treasure Table, roll once for the burial style and twice more for treasure found.}
rows: Copper, silver, and gold coins ({@dice 2d6 × 10} each)
Silver, electrum, and gold coins ({@dice 4d6 × 10} each)

entries.name: Coffins
entries: Wooden coffins fill the chamber. Some are stacked horizontally while others stand upright. It's impossible to reach coffins in the back without dragging those in front out of the room. Any treasure is inside the coffins. The sepulcher holds {@dice 1d20 + 35} coffins.

entries.name: Jugs
entries: Large clay jugs are filled with bones. Each jug contains the bones of one person, sealed in with resincoated linen. Any treasure in the sepulcher is inside the jugs. The sepulcher contains {@dice 1d20 + 40} jugs.

entries.name: Loculi
entries: Loculi are horizontal niches carved into the wall. Each 5-foot section of wall holds {@dice 1d3 + 1} loculi, and each loculus holds the remains of one person. Any treasure is in the loculi, either on the body or beneath it.

entries.name: Sarcophagi
entries: Sarcophagi are carved from stone and sealed with mortar. Each contains the remains of one person—someone of great wealth and importance, judging by their clothing. Treasure is inside the stone caskets. Opening a sarcophagus takes 5 minutes and a successful {@dc 13} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check.

entries.name: Stacked Bodies
entries: The bodies were tightly wrapped in layers of linen and soaked in resin, which is now hard and brittle. Any treasure in the room is inside the wrappings, which must be painstakingly cut and chipped away. The sepulcher contains {@dice 1d20 + 60} bodies.

entries.name: Urns
entries: Funerary urns made of clay or porcelain are stacked across the floor and in shallow wall niches. Urns are filled with ashes and have loose-fitting lids. Any treasure in the sepulcher is in the urns, mixed with the ashes. The sepulcher contains {@dice 1d20 + 80} urns.

name: Byssmol Mountains Encounter
rows: An animal-slide comes down the side of the mountain—it's like a mudslide, but instead of mud its forest critters that roll down the mountain (rabbits, squirrels). Each party member must succeed on a {@dc 14} Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 1d12} bludgeoning damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one.

A SEVERE animal-slide spills down the side of the mountain—it's just like a regular animalslide, but with bears. Each party member must succeed on a {@dc 15} Strength saving throw to push through before the flow grows too strong, taking {@damage 1d6} slashing damage and gaining 1 level of {@condition exhaustion} on a failed save.

Ravaged by the terrible environmental activity in the area, the path forward is insulting— meaning the trees come alive and hurl demoralizing insults. Each party member must succeed on a {@dc 14} Wisdom saving throw or gain 1 level of {@condition exhaustion}.
Patches of evil stones nearby emit toxic negative energy. Each party member must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned} for the next hour.

A sudden flood...OF EMOTIONS bogs the party down with unrelenting nostalgia. Each party member must succeed on a {@dc 15} Charisma saving throw or be pushed into a deep longing for the path, gaining 1 level of {@condition exhaustion}.

A small rock path curves around the mountain but magically it becomes dangerously unstable, wobbling back and forth and up and down like a rope bridge in a quake. Each party member must succeed on a {@dc 12} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check or suffer {@damage 1d10} bludgeoning damage while stumbling.
A terrible, fetid stench pollutes the surroundings. Each party member must succeed on a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw or gain 1 level of {@condition exhaustion}.

Bee Rain! Bees rain down from storm clouds slowing the party's pace and making conditions unbearable. Each party member must succeed on a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw or gain 1 level of {@condition exhaustion}.

name: Cadaver Collector
rows: Just like any machine, the cadaver collector requires lubricant to keep its gears and joints moving smoothly. The cadaver collector however uses a more vile source: the blood and gristle of rotting corpses. As the grisly mixture covers and circulates through the infernal construct, it catalyzes into a substance known as undertaker oil. This oil is highly sought for its ability to preserve corpses regardless of their level of putrefaction, and can be used by anyone to rival the skills of even the greatest embalmer.

Those that have fought a cadaver collector and lived will agree that although the corpses that adorn its body are terrifying, the thing that lingers in the mind for years after is its hollow, unblinking visage. Stylized to resemble a horrific green-eyed skull, the face of the cadaver collector inspires paralyzing fear in both the living and the dead (a trait it shares with my great-uncle Tothbard).

Forged from the hell-blasted flames of Acheron, the steel plates that cover the cadaver collector put to shame anything smelted on the Material Planes. With proper modifications, this steel creates a fearsome suit of armor that protects both the body and the spirit.

entries: In the center of the cadaver collector beats not a heart, but a small, white-hot core of hellish energy that fuels the dark construct. This core is sparked by the sacrifice of dozens of innocent creatures and drives the collector to its dark purpose. It must be handled with extreme care, but when preserved well, its energy can be reused as a very powerful explosive or for particularly difficult crafting purposes.

entries.name: Use:
entries: As an action, you may throw this item to a space within 15 feet, after which, this item explodes in a 10-foot radius burst. All targets within that burst must make a {@dc 18} Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they suffer {@damage 4d6} fire damage and {@damage 4d6} necrotic damage, or half that on a success.

A valiant fighter and leader of others
