name: d100 Character Secrets
caption: Character Secrets
rows: Always wears a {@item hat of disguise}
Used to be a cult leader in another city
Has recurring nightmares of the apocalypse
Has been teaching themselves magic for the last 12 years
Is the champion of an underground fighting pit
Was banished from their home country
Plans to assassinate the leader of the region
Donates almost all their earnings anonymously to an orphanage
Is addicted to {@item potion of healing|dmg|potions of healing}
In love with one of the party members
Has part of a map which leads to a treasure hoard of a killed dragon
Is blackmailing the leader of the city with their secret
Accidentally spent all their money on a shipment of worthless goods
Is a long-lost family member of one of the party members
Lost their house in a game of gambling
Has a twin no one knows about, only one of them is ever seen at a time
Used to be a mighty sorcerer but lost their connection to the arcane
Is completely unable to sleep so they wander the streets at night
Is cursed by a warlock, they fear to die in 472 days unless the warlock is killed
Ran away from home at age 9
Their child is a known criminal in the city, they cut all bonds with them
They take care of their best friend who is a werewolf
Lives as a common person but is of royal descent
Has changed names 5 times in their past due to their stalking ex-romantic partner
Writes and publishes erotic fiction under a different name
Accidentally killed their best friend years ago
In love with the bard who sings every weekend at the tavern
Says they are not religious but goes to a shrine every night to pray
Has a huge stash of platinum hidden under their mattress
Has extra-dimensional rooms in their house
Knows their neighbor his offering shelter to criminals
Gathering information and spying on the martial forces of the city for an army of kobolds
Is being pressured into keeping their mouth shut regarding someone else's secret
Is extremely acrobatic but they never show it off
Spreads misinformation about others to gain advantage for their own business
Put laxatives in the food of the captain of the guard as part of a bigger scheme
Accidentally set fire to a temple of a deity of fire
Sold their neighbors house whilst they were visiting family across the country
Shot a deer on the hunting grounds belonging to a noble family
Under the influence of a curse which makes it unable for them to say their own name
Poisoned the fields of a farmer who insulted them once
Made a deal with a devil to excel in their skills, trade or craft
Stumbled into a planar portal as a child, returned to the material plane 300 years later
Stole a huge amount of diamonds in an impressive heist that people still talk about
Has 2 spouses, one in this city and one in the neighboring town
Grows illegal mushrooms that cause hallucinations in their basement
Trafficked drugs from far across the world
Is responsible for a recent natural disaster
Is actually a devil making infernal deals in disguise
Is in search of an ancient magical family heirloom their siblings do not know about
Accidentally made a cursed magic item that is wreaking havoc amongst wizards
A magic spell changed their gender
Holds a grudge for a person they believe stole their most prized possession
Used to be a dragon but was {@spell true polymorph||true polymorphed} into their current form
Hiding from a group of mercenaries they hired but did not pay
Hides multiple daggers on their person
A magic spell changed their race/species
Knows far more languages than they let on to listen in on other people's conversations
Witnessed a murder which they did not report to the city guard
Used to be a hero back in the day, responsible for saving the city
Can walk on water without consciously using magic
The love of their life sacrificed themselves for them in battle
Used to be a notorious pirate, but changed their  name and appearance to remain free
Has a fetish for a particular sexual experience which they are slightly embarrassed about
They can not go 2 miles away from their home because of a curse
Descendant of an evil wizard who threatened the realms ages ago
Used to protect an ancient relic but they broke their oath
Meets up every night with a couple of other people to dig a tunnel network under the city
Has an arcane powered mechanical heart
Was the only survivor of a plague in their homelands
Has a secret shack outside the city where they go to meditate for days on end
Is actually a continuous illusion cast by their"assistant"
A curse causes them to randomly teleport to a location within 500ft the moment they fall asleep
They are a leader of a crime syndicate
They are hunting one of the party members, waiting for the perfect moment to strike
They are completely incompetent in what they do but they cover it up expertly
Has a doomsday bunker underneath their home
They scammed or lied their way into a position of power
Has a bucket list of creatures they want to kill
Covered up a murder their friend committed
Vowed to take revenge on the murder of their parents
Tricks adventurers into a cave they filled with monsters and a vast amount of traps
Escaped from being sacrificed to a deity, and the followers of the deity are still searching for them
Once cast a nasty curse upon someone else
Meets up every week with friends to play a dice-based game where they pretend to be adventurers

name: d100 Character Traits
caption: Character Traits
rows: A hurried and stressed person, they end their sentences in a slightly higher pitch or a questioning tone.
Easily distracted by mundane things but they always have a cheerful attitude.
An arrogant coward with a royal background, They flaunt their wealth a lot.
Twitchy and nervous. they are easily scared or jolted by mundane things.
A grumpy and discontent individual they always seems to be holding in their anger.
A charming person that always has a compliment for a friend.
Fearless but not very bright, tends to settle arguments with their fists.
Cunning and sly, easily offended when it comes to their wealth.
Cheerful and hyperactive. They almost always have a smile on their face.
Silent and thoughtful. Speaks slowly and uses a minimal amount of words.
Mischievous but with a heart of gold. Would never hurt anyone. Teases people a lot.
Loud and unapologetic. Often makes rude comments and farts a lot. Usually laughs it off.
Often sad, they try to see the good things in bad situations but have a hard time doing so.
A stoic individual, they always rationalize their feelings. They can see most things objectively.
Satisfied and settled down, they are comfortable and happy where they are right now.
Impatient, they are easily irritated by ignorant or slow people. They often tell people to hurry up.
Traumatized by events they experienced, they will stop at nothing to get revenge.
An expressive individual, they talk with their hands and hug others as a form of greeting.
Often under the influence of narcotics, they are always looking for their next fix.
Suspicious, they do not easily trust others. They whisper when talking, so others don't hear.
Easily angered when they see other people getting hurt, protective of those close to them.
Energetic, constantly tapping their feet or fingers. They often can't wait to do something new.
A young and childish soul that has a sense of wonder for anything. They have a little skip in their step.
A weak and diseased individual, they cough after almost every sentence they speak.
Wise beyond their years, they often give advice to others. They speak with a lot of confidence.
Demanding, they require others to do as they are told, they do not take no for an answer.
Charitable, they often share their food and drink with others. Always willing to help out a friend.
Jealous, they wish to get higher up in the world to show off to others.
Observing and quiet, they wait until someone approaches them. They know quite a lot about others.
A bumbling idiot, they say anything that crosses their mind. They speak before they (try to) think.
Shy and apologetic, apologizes and excuses themselves every other sentence.
Kind and welcoming; would make an excellent innkeep if it weren't for their greed.
Ignorant towards the value of currency, finds happiness in simple things.
Thinks everyone is better than them, very insecure.
Does not care what others think of them, dresses and speaks accordingly.
Very bright and intelligent but talents wasted through substance abuse.
Very flirty but almost never engages in any romantic affairs.
An old soul, they are convinced they are very wise but not everyone would agree.
Makes decisions based on the people around him, easily persuaded, could not live without spouse.
Has been hunting a specific creature for years and is thoroughly obsessed with it.
Knows the adventurers by name and has heard of their deeds but is not impressed.
Fidgets with their fingers a lot, can not stay still for even a second.
A very warm parental figure, they are an important part of the community they live in.
A calm individual, not easily jolted or angered. They are hard to intimidate.
Has no patience, they still have a lot to do today and their time will not be wasted.
Angered easily by foolish or childish behavior, does not appreciate jokes.
Completely in love with another individual, will not accept a bad remark about that person.
Uncharismatic but loved by many, his demeanor is extremely kind but very awkward.
Jokes constantly about the stupidity of others but often trips over their own feet.
Scared to death of Dragonborn, they have had a traumatic experience with a dragon.
Very vain and focused on looks, runs hands through their hair/beard often.
Has bad eyesight, does not respond to any visually alarming things.
Claims they come from royalty and act as such, however, nobody knows their heritage.
A liar and a cheat, will do anything for a gold coin, does not like to spend money.
A hulking individual for their race, they are strong but very stupid.
They are very mean to people that are not their gender.
Almost always happy, prefers to skip instead of walk, their pockets are stuffed with candy.
Grim and somber, they are rarely seen in bright daylight and prefer darkness.
Would love to be an adventurer, easily impressed by magical displays of any kind.
Angry with the leadership of their community, blames everything on them.
A gentle person, they feel most at home in the wild, walks barefoot.
A kind and artistic person, they have a sketchbook with them at all times.
A typical scholar, when relaying information they often refer to some book they have read.
A charismatic and pleasant person, they have many valuable connections in the community.
A classless person, they often burp or fart without apologizing.
They have big dreams about becoming renowned and famous with their trade.
A hard worker they practice and toil deep into the night, making them very tired.
Straightforward and to the point, does not care about pleasantries.
Has a bad leg, walks slow but they tough it out without complaint.
They have a dual personality, they are complete opposites in terms of likes and dislikes.
Claims they see the future in their dreams, but they claim it after events have passed.
Wears masks to hide their face, their masks show their emotional state of that day.
Is extremely proud of their kid(s), talks about them a lot.
Clumsy, they often drop things they are handed and when walking bump into other people.
Optimistic, they quite often see a silver lining to a bad situation.
Indifferent, they do not care about a lot of things that others care about.
Pessimistic, they see the worst in the best of things.
Lives by the law and some of their own rules, some of which are a bit weird.
Does not trust people they have not met yet.
Curious, they has a profound interest in the origins of one of the adventurers.
Battles narcolepsy, sometimes falls asleep or dozes off mid sentence.
Has to do some actions and say some things five times in sequence.
Has a hard time believing there is any sort of evil in the world until they see it themselves.
Friendly but quite often judges peoples' worth by their clothing and jewelry.
Forgetful, they often forget people's names, faces but also details about their surroundings.
Creepy, they often stand a little too close for comfort to others without reason.
Diva, they can and shall not live without preposterous luxuries.
Reserved, they keep their emotions in check even in great danger.
Extremely friendly to small humanoids, they have a soft spot for the small folk.
Friendly and very talented but brush off any praise they receive for what they do.
They love to take a bet, they have made a lot of money with it as well.
Easily distracted but they are fascinated and captivated by shiny objects.
Chaotic in their demeanor, they hoard one certain type of furniture in their dwelling.
A careless individual, they love walking in the rain.
Adopted by a different race as a child they have different customs than could be expected.
Extremely lazy they do not care to do any work if it is not necessary.
Very distrustful, they have wild conspiracy theories about things happening in their community.
Indecisive, they doubt themselves a lot, they often change clothing and hairstyle.
Unnervingly sweet in their demeanor, says the most horrible things with a smile.
Slightly unhinged, they can suddenly respond quite extreme or emotional without reason.

name: d100 Drinking Toasts
caption: Drinking Toasts
rows: Here's to the ditch, may it be warm and cozy when we end up there later tonight.
Here's to cheating, stealing, and drinking. May you cheat death, steal hearts, and always drink with me.
May you have warm words on a cold evening, a full moon on a dark night and the road downhill all the way to your door.
Here's to [drink], the cause of, and solution to all life's problems.
Whilst the hearth is still aglow, let the [drink] flow!
Here's to my middlefinger, for always sticking up for me when I needed it most.
To the king, the queen, or whoever rules these bloody lands.
And to those who embrace the night early, we mourn their weak wills and pray for those lonely souls
Here's to doing and drinking, not sitting and thinking.
Cheers, for the liver is evil and must be punished tonight.
If I should stumble out this bar, I hope the night is worth the scar
Here's to those who will have to clean up the mess we leave.
Here's to being single, drinking doubles, and seeing triple.
Over the teeth, over the gums, look out stomach here it comes.
Here's to [drink], not as good as (wo)men, but pretty close.
Drink until the sun comes up, drink until the sun goes down, if you drink on both occassions you will never frown.
Tonight, the only thing I worry about is turning [drink] into piss.
It matters not if the glass is half empty or half full, clearly there's room for more!
Here's to your nose, here's to your chin,here's to the hole, in-between it goes in!
One beer, two beers, three beers, four, still depressed? Drink some more.
As you slide down the banister of life, may the splinters never face the wrong way.
A toast to bread, for without bread, there would be no toast.
Time is never wasted, when you're wasted all the time.
May I alwayss be remembered for what I have done, not what I'm about to do.
I can't find the words that go well with this drink, perhaps they're at the bottom of the glass. Cheers!
I would like to thank my arms for always being by my side, my legs for always supporting me, and my fingers, because I can always count on them.
Lift em high and drain em dry, here's to the person who says "my turn to buy"!
Pain makes you stronger. Tears make you braver. Heartbreak makes you wiser. And [drink] makes you remember none of that.
To mighty fights, wilds nights, and the clink of good coin in our purses!
Let our drinks be full, our spirits hearty, and our blades sharp!
Another day another bender, no retreat no surrender.
To the confusion of our enemies!
More poison, there's things inside me that need killing!
Here's to us! May we live respected and die regretted.
To good luck and taking chances!
May the saddest day of your future, be no worse than the happiest day of your past.
To those who guide us through darkness into light.
Here's to Dame Fortune; may she smile upon you and may you never meet her daughter, Miss Fortune
Life is a waste of time, and time is a waste of life. So let's get wasted all of the time, and have the time of our life.
Life is a jest and all things show it, I thought so once and now I know it.
For every wound, a balm. For every sorrow, cheer. For every storm, a calm. For every thirst, a beer.
Here's to a long life and a happy one. A quick death and an easy one. A good love and an honest one. A cold drink and another one.
May the winds of fortune sail you, may you sail a gentle sea. May it always be the other guy, who says, "this drink's on me.
May misfortune follow you the rest of your life, but never catch up.
May sweet laughter lighten every load. May the spark of arcane magic shorten every road. And may all your friends remember all the favours you are owed!
May you have the hindsight to know where you've been, foresight to know where you're going, and insight to know when you've gone too far
May we get what we want, but never what we deserve.
I drank to your health in company. I drank to your health alone. I drank to your health so many times, I nearly ruined my own.
May we suffer as much sorrow as drops of wine we are about to leave in our glasses!
Always remember to forget the things that made you sad, never forget to remember the things that made you glad.
May we all have the chance to to prove that money does not make you happy.
May your copper turn to gold and your silvers turn to platinum.
May you live as long as you like, and have all you like as long as you live.
A rich man lives in a castle, a poor man lives by the sea. But a whiskey glass and a nice round ass are home sweet home to me.
Health to those I love, wealth to those who love me.
A round to the best, may we never get less than we deserve and more than we may ever need
May our children have wealthy parents.
May your heart be light and happy, may your smile be big and wide and may your pockets always have a coin or two inside!
Steal my gold that's all right, steal my drink you'll get a fight!
A toast to [deity] for [drink] is proof that [deity] loves us and wants us to be happy!
May neighbors respect you, trouble neglect you. Angels protect you and heaven accept you.
May you be in heaven a full half hour before the devil knows you're dead.
To [deity] may they bless these people!
May you always lie, cheat, and steal. Lie beside the one you love, cheat the devil, and steal away from bad company.
To the skies, may we fall long before they do!
Here's to hell: May the stay there be as fun as the way there.
Here's to the night's we won't remember, with the friends we'll never forget.
Here's to those who wish us well, all the rest can go to hell.
To ourselves, as no one is likely to concern themselves with our welfare.
Here's to those who wish us well, all the rest can go to hell.
I would rather be here, with the people in this room, than with the best people in the world!
To making friends in new places!
To those who've seen us at our worst and seen us at our best, and cannot tell the difference.
To family that are friends, and to friends that are family!
Here's to the friends who love us, the losers that lost us and the lucky ones yet to meet us!
Here's to you and here's to me, and if by chance we disagree, to hell with you! And here's to me!
There are good ships, there are wood ships, and ships that sail the sea. But the best ships, are friendships, And may they always be.
Let us raise our drinks in honor of those who came before, and those who are soon to come. To good health, my friends, and a good night to you all.
May the roof above these friends never fall in, and may the friends beneath this roof never fall out.
I don't care what those others say, you people are all right!
Friends may come and friends may go, but [drink] is here to soothe the blow.
If I die before you, raise a glass in my name. If you go before me I'll do the same
Cheers, to whomever loves us even though we may not deserve it.
Here's to roses and lilies in bloom, you in my arms, and me in your room. A door that is locked, a key that is lost and a night that is 50 years long.
Cheers to beers and legs behind your ears.
To not knowing left from right and hoping I'm not left and end up all right!
A drink, to whoever your heart beats for.
May we kiss who we please, and please who we kiss
Here is to the girl on the hill, that says she won't but her sister will. (boy/his brother, person, their sibling)
May all your ups and downs be under the covers!
To sweet love, a long life and a lousy liver!
With this glass, rich, and deep, we cradle our sorrows to sleep.
To the fallen, may they guide our hearts and our blades!
Here's to getting out alive where others did not.
I raise a glass to the fallen, for I am thankful to drink with those that remain standing.
Tonight we'll drown our sorrow untill we remember them on the morrow.

name: d100 Market Stalls
caption: Market Stalls
rows: A female dwarf butcher selling meat of a dragon hatchling. Upon closer inspection it is revealed to be the carcass of a kobold.
A gnome woman selling pet Mimics shaped like small household items. One of the cages is open.
A half-elf man selling hand carved dice, sometimes he plays a few (unfair) games for coin with curious shoppers.
Two halfling brothers selling vegetables; your eye is drawn to peculiar roots seemingly from a far-off country.
An old human lady pushing a cart filled with porcelain cats painted in different motifs. She claims they protect people from evil.
A gnome man running a stall selling precious gemstones, both polished and unpolished. 2 heavily-armored dwarves guard the stall.
An elf woman selling scented oils which calm the nerves and make you sleep better.
A tiefling woman selling silks and cloths of all colors. She gives (unwanted) fashion advice to whomever walks by.
A recruitment stall for an adventuring guild: two humans are handing out pamphlets while a dwarf shouts the perks of joining.
A dragonborn man selling enchanted torches that give off light with adjustable brightness in various colors.
An old gnome woman selling herbs and tinctures for healing and cooking purposes. The sign also says "poison" in thieves' cant.
A young elf man selling flowers, small plants and saplings of trees. A lot of young women swarm around him.
A tiefling man and human man selling high-quality paper and blank books.
A halfling woman selling make-up currently in the process of demonstrating her products on a startled passerby.
A half-orc man selling coal from the local mines. He claims it comes from the deepest mineshaft and thus burns hotter than any other.
A family of halflings selling fresh strawberries (a delicacy known well among the locals).
A tiefling behind a stall that is completely empty except for a red velvet pillow. On top of the pillow rests a jet black stone.
A stall run by a red dragonborn man and a halfling woman selling home-baked cookies and cakes.
A small family of humans running a vegetable stall. They sell non-seasonal vegetables, grown from their greenhouse.
An elf woman selling spices from the East. A favorite among locals is "Dragon's Claw," which makes for a great addition to dark meats.
A half-elf man selling wooden canes carved to resemble animals. The man has a pet snake coiled around his arm.
A gnome man pulling a small display cart laden with portrait drawings, 2 stools and an easel.
A blonde elf woman selling glass snowglobes. In them are displayed carved models of monuments within the city.
A dark-skinned dwarf man selling unrefined iron, tin and copper.
A tall gnome man runs a stall selling nautical instruments and wayfinding equipment.
A blue-skinned tiefling woman in gypsy-styled garments sits behind a table, reading hands and cards.
A stall with an old human man selling roasted nuts.
A family of humans selling dairy products from their farm. The smell of the cheeses is sharp and fills the air.
A human and two dragonborn men selling freshly-caught fish.
A half-orc hunter selling parts of deer he shot the day before. It is busy at the stall and the meat is being sold at auction.
A gnome woman selling wooden and metal spinning tops from a small cart.
A half-elf woman selling inks and quills. She has feathers woven in her hair and ink stained hands.
Three young children with a rickety cart polishing shoes. Upon inspection you see a 4th child attempting to steal from the customers.
A pair of gnomes selling blue carrots. They claim that if stewed and eaten, the carrots will make you see better for a limited time.
A dwarf man dressed in a comically over-the-top miner's outfit selling realistic looking candy rocks and gemstones.
A human man selling crates and boxes of dark oak wood. Supposedly the wood is resistant to fire and flames.
A family of halflings runs a large stall filled with breads. They also make fresh sandwiches from ingredients available elsewhere in the market.
A middle-aged human man pushing a cart filled with cabbages. They are severely overpriced but he seems to be turning a profit.
An elf woman selling bottled spring water. It is not artificially cooled but it is icy cold to the touch.
Two dragonborn women selling brightly-colored kites in different shapes and sizes. A dragon-shaped kite flies above the stall, whether there is wind or not.
A tan human woman selling gloves made of exotic leathers, currently expertly cutting some grey leather with a thin sharp knife.
An elf woman selling 3 types of seasonal wine she taps from barrels into bottles.
A dwarf woman next to a small cart with a massage table. As you walk past she swiftly corrects the neck of a human man.
An extravagant human woman selling hats and scarves. As you walk by, you can smell her strong, flowery perfume.
A gnome man selling a few large, freshly caught swordfish he claimed he caught using a live chicken as bait.
A dragonborn woman selling beeswax prayer candles for various deities.
A human woman selling caged birds. Next to carrier pigeons and ravens she sells brightly colored parakeets and canaries.
A half-orc woman with a large straw-bedded pen filled with young, healthy-looking calves and a few older cows.
A halfling family selling jams and jellies made from local fruits.
Two half-elf brothers selling different flavors of tea. The younger brother sells a special hallucinogenic tea secretly on the side.
A human woman selling sewing equipment. Her most expensive items are adamantine sowing needles and special spidersilk thread.
A red-skinned tiefling man selling fireworks; anything from sparklers and flares to rockets.
A firbolg man with long curly hair selling soap and hair products. The smell of citrus and mint fills the air around the stall.
A pretty well-dressed kobold boy trying to sell polished rocks stalled out on an upside-down crate.
Two young gnome women selling handcrafted dresses and skirts in gnome and halfling sizes.
A rough-looking male dwarf adventurer selling scavenged animal parts, armor and weapons.
A tiefling woman selling vegetable curries made on the spot. She serves them in large hollowed-out coconut bowls.
A gnome man with a small cart filled with music boxes. As you try them, one of them plays the anthem of a rebel organization.
Three human brothers selling apples and apple cider from their family-owned orchard.
A young firbolg woman selling handmade jewelry made mainly from wood and semiprecious gemstones.
A pair of halflings selling potatoes and yams.
A gnome man selling truffles from a cart pulled by his pet pig.
A group of 3 humans selling clams and crawfish. One of them is a sorcerer, on a sale he freezes the produce in a thin layer of ice.
A scruffy goblin woman selling bundled packets of vegetable peels, bones and meat scraps to make soup from.
A dragonborn woman selling sweet candy made from a poisonous cactus. The candy itself is harmless but sales seem slow.
A human man trying to pass off pink bananas as magical fruits. Upon inspection, they are revealed to be regular bananas painted pink.
A male half-orc tailor selling cloth shirts and offering repairs for any type of clothing. His large hands work with astounding precision.
A male human sorcerer at a small stall offering to remove a single memory for gold. The price of the service depends on the memory.
A group of humans and halflings selling fruits and vegetables from their homestead.
A halfling pulling a cart with an oven on it selling smoked salmon. The thin wisp of smoke coming from the oven smells delicious.
A human man and woman selling poultry and eggs.
A halfling woman selling fabrics on rolls used for furniture and drapes.
A gnome man selling pipes and different flavors of tobacco from a small stall.
A family of dwarves selling craftsmen tools and iron nails. They also offer simple repairs for most items on the side.
A human man pulling a small cart with books from his faith. He also sells reading glasses.
A dwarf man wearing a keg on his back from which he taps a potent energizing alcoholic beverage into small shot glasses.
A gnome woman selling various shapes and sizes of glass vials and a few (healing) potions.
A half-elf man selling city maps from a stand. He offers advice on the best taverns and on which places to avoid.
An elf woman selling different types of finely-crafted arrows. She has a keen eye for people who try to steal from her.
An old dragonborn woman selling white tablecloths and doilies.
A human man selling honey he harvested from his own beehives.
A sun-tanned dwarf man selling coconuts and other tropical fruits.
A halfling family selling different types of wheat and flour.
A small group of goliaths selling wooden planks and lumber.
An old gnome man selling various books from an overladen stall.
A young human girl and a young tiefling boy selling lemonade from a makeshift stand.
An elf woman and halfling man selling homemade perfumes. They have various flower, fruity and wood scents on display.
A family of gnomes selling different types of farm animal meats. They also sell hot sausages with a spiced tomato-based sauce.
A young firbolg woman selling seeds for various vegetables and flowers.
A human man selling various tanned leathers and hides from common farm animals.
A dwarf man selling woolen socks with various patterns. He claims it is impossible to lose one sock from the pair.
A couple of halflings selling olives and olive oil. Their specialty is a serving of garlic olives which most customers eat at the stall.
A goliath woman selling carved stone statues and keepsakes of various deities and their symbols.
An old elf man selling a couple of wands and staffs inlaid with crushed precious and semiprecious gemstones.
A dwarf woman selling knives and daggers she forged herself. She also sharpens dull blades for a small fee.
A gnome man with a large reclining chair on wheels offering dentist services. The patients seem to leave in quite some pain.
A half-orc woman selling hunting traps for various types of prey.
A closed red tent with a sign that reads "Auntie Tina's." Upon entering you meet a female gnome offering advice for relationship trouble.
A human boy and a goblin man selling bags of stinky mulch and fertilizer for gardens.
A half-orc man selling mining and lumbering equipment. The pickaxes and axes are made of a dark-tinted steel.

name: d100 More Market Stalls
caption: Market Stalls
rows: An old elf woman selling hand carved flutes and ocarinas. They have fine elven scrolling engraved in them.
Two half-orcs men selling firewood and charcoal.
A human man wearing a thick layered robe selling woolen cloaks and coats.
A gnome woman selling straw idols and bundles that supposedly protect and guard your home against spirits.

Low rumbling, the words strung together
Speaks in third person about themselves
Switches between two types of voices
Mumbles notes to self in between sentences
Draws out most vowels when speaking
Speaks as if they have a cold/blocked nose
Often spits out words with contempt
Uses the words/sounds "uh" and "uhm" a lot

name: Damage Threshold *
outro: * Objects Large or larger

name: Damage to the Ship
rows: The ship has a rupture in its hull and is taking on water. The ship's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} decreases by 5 feet.
The ship has a second rupture in its hull and is taking on even more water. The ship's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} decreases by an additional 5 feet.

The ship has a third rupture in its hull and is slowly sinking. The ship's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} decreases by an additional 5 feet. Unless the ship is repaired, it will sink in {@dice 2d6} rounds.
The ship has been holed and can no longer move or maneuver. It is sinking. Unless the ship is repaired, it will sink in {@dice 1d4} rounds.

entries: When a dao dies, its body disintegrates into a crystalline powder. Fast hands can capture this powder before it loses its magical essence which can then be used as a material component in many spells. {@b Requires {@item enchanted vial|HHHVI}.}

entries.name: Use:
entries: When casting the spell {@spell conjure elemental}, you may use the crystalline powder as a material component to cast the spell as an action instead. The spell is also considered to be cast at one level higher than the spell slot you used to cast it. The crystalline powder then becomes inert and useless.

The burnt remains of a darkling after its absorbed light has burst out. While it is disappointing that most of their body has been made unharvestable, the ash still holds some magical properties as a light nullifier. This should be obvious in that it was the only portion of the darkling's body to not disintegrate when exposed to a light flash.

entries.name: Use:
entries: When you cast the {@spell darkness} spell, you may expend 1 or more pouches of this ash instead of the usual material components. If you do so, the radius of the magical darkness you create expands by 5 feet for every pouch of ash you expend.

name: Darkling Elder

entries: The burnt remains of a darkling after its absorbed light has burst out. While it is disappointing that most of their body has been made unharvestable, the ash still holds some magical properties as a light nullifier. This should be obvious in that it was the only portion of the darkling's body to not disintegrate when exposed to a light flash.

entries.name: Use:
entries: When you cast the {@spell darkness} spell, you may expend 1 or more pouches of this ash instead of the usual material components. If you do so, the radius of the magical darkness you create expands by 5 feet for every pouch of ash you expend.

rows: The ritual to become a darkling elder is painful, risky, and costly. The enchanted tattoos contain traces of metals, rare pigments, and magical reagents that are capable of surviving the light flash that accompanies a darkling's death. It is quite difficult to do so, but carefully sifting through the elder's ashes can reveal these tattoo components, which still carry the light they absorbed and are thus extremely valuable.

name: Darkmantle
rows: Anybody who has been attacked by a darkmantle can attest to the suction power of its tentacles. Reliable even beyond the death of its owner, many Underdark residents have adapted these suckers to be used for medical tools and other implements.
A bony structure on the inside of a darkmantle's head that acts as its ear. Skilled artificers can use this to create a variety of audio enhancing magical items.

name: Days Tracked
rows: Clan Bloodpaw arrives in Anan'Thul and disperses throughout the city to start their search.
{@creature Pack Lord Yz|SandsOfDoom|Yz} and his warband discover Hakkari's Temple, establish a camp, and begin the excavation.
The excavation reaches its mid-way point, with half of area 42 uncovered.

The final chamber of the temple, area 51, is uncovered. {@creature Hakkari, High Priest of Anan'Thul|SandsOfDoom|Hakkari}'s sarcophagus is unearthed, and {@creature Pack Lord Yz|SandsOfDoom|Yz} claims the {@item Hand of Brass|SandsOfDoom} shortly afterward.
{@creature Pack Lord Yz|SandsOfDoom|Yz} leaves Anan'Thul and begins his journey to Kunaten Keep.
{@creature Pack Lord Yz|SandsOfDoom|Yz} arrives at Kunaten Keep.

name: Days Tracked

{@creature Pack Lord Yz|SandsOfDoom14|Yz} and his warband discover Hakkari's Temple, establish a camp, and begin the excavation.

{@creature Pack Lord Yz|SandsOfDoom14|Yz} leaves Anan'Thul and begins his journey to Kunaten Keep.
{@creature Pack Lord Yz|SandsOfDoom14|Yz} arrives at Kunaten Keep.

name: Death Kiss
rows: The crackling blood of a death kiss is as electrified as a field before a storm. Many foolish adventurers find that their metal weapons turn into conductors of their own deaths when used to strike a death kiss.

The tentacles of a death kiss lack any ranged capabilities. Instead they are much more capable in melee combat, being lined with vampiric teeth that can drain a victim of blood. The hollow teeth of the death kiss served as the inspiration for the first hypodermic needles, and thus in a strange way, beholders could be seen as the inventors of this medical breakthrough.

Unlike most beholders, the eye of a death kiss holds no offensive or defensive abilities. However, when removed, boiled, mashed into a paste, and fortified with arcane components, the resulting mixture makes a potent medicine used to treat blood diseases and other maladies. Alternatively, it makes for a powerful lens to aid in the hunting and tracking of one's foes.

name: Death Knight

entries: When the flesh of a defeated death knight is burned in a ritual fire, the resulting ashes retain the same dark aura of its original form. If one has the resolve for it, these ashes can be mixed with oils and special powders then applied to the body to gain certain protections from the undead.

entries.name: Use:
entries: You may mix these ashes with 20 gold pieces worth of rare oils and powdered gems to create a paste that grants certain defences against undead when rubbed into the body. For 24 hours after using it on yourself, undead creatures have disadvantage on any Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks made to find you. In addition, you gain resistance to any necrotic damage dealt from an undead source and advantage on any saving throw imposed by an undead creature.

rows: Blood is a generous term to apply to the coagulated muck that cloys in a death knight's veins. Blacker than the cursed warrior's soul, this substance makes for a versatile reagent in certain desecration rituals and blood curses. Use with caution.

Even though a death knight may fall in battle, its dark curse will eventually form a new body somewhere and force its soul to continue its mockery of life. If one takes its heart and preserves it in a secret ritual, the death knight's new body will be formed without the organ. From then on, the missing heart can be used as a method of tracking the death knight, beating whenever it senses its old master nearby.

name: Death Slaad
rows: The slime that coats a slaad smells like the bottom of a fetid swamp and looks like it too. It is believed that this slime has an innocuation effect against the diseases and parasitic eggs of the slaads, but this is mostly just conjecture. Otherwise, it is a mere curiosity for eccentric researchers.

entries: Slaadi are creatures of pure chaos, born from the unstable energies in Limbo. As such, their very bodies disrupt the natural order of things and those that consume some of their flesh tend to find that probability itself changes for them, if only temporarily. Beware however, as the universe is not to be trifled with, and it tends to find ways to balance itself out later.

entries.name: Use:
entries: As an action you may eat this item. If you do so, then once within the next 10 minutes you may choose to bend the laws of fate within your favour. If you do so, you gain advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. If you choose not to, this item is wasted. After those 10 minutes have passed, your DM may choose at any time within the next 24 hours to impose disadvantage on 1 attack roll, ability check, or saving throw you make.

rows: The hide of a slaad is extraordinarily tough, and even more so once it has evolved into either its {@creature gray slaad|MM|gray} or {@creature death slaad|MM} variants. As befitting of a slaad's possessive and transformative nature, even the skinned hide of a mature slaad will attempt to mutate and change its wearer. It is only with advanced techniques that this property is curtailed and used only to the benefit of its new owner.

name: Death Tyrant
rows: The teeth of a beholder must never be underestimated, even in death. Their jaws possess a wicked bite, and when attached to the handle of an axe, so can your backswing.

The eye of a beholder undergoes a terrible transformation when it transitions into undeath, emitting a cone of negative energy rather than anti-magic. But like a normal beholder eye, this eye can be transformed into a crystal of great power that many powerful wizards enjoy employing in their lairs.

name: Deathlock
rows: The black heart of a deathlock no longer serves any useful biological function. In fact, more often than not, it has ossified from exposure to necromantic energies and more resembles an anatomical model than an actual organ. While the necromantic energies seeped into it are relatively weak, they are admittedly quite captivating to look at, and some shadier mages have been known to use the heart as a morbid arcane focus.

entries: A deathlock rises when the spirit of a mortal bound to a patron fails to uphold their end of a pact. When this occurs, their soul is chained by their wrathful patron, refused entry to the afterlife, and hurtled back into their former body to resume their duty. While this is tragic for the deathlock, this chaining also makes their spirit particularly easy to capture in a ream of spirit paper and made to do your own bidding. {@b Requires {@item spirit paper|HHHVI}.}

entries.name: Use:
entries: As an action, you may tear this item open, releasing the vengeful spirit trapped inside which takes the form of a {@creature specter|MM} (the DM has the creature's statistics) in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. This specter acts next round on its own initiative and follows any verbal orders you give it (no action required). The specter lasts for 1 minute or until it is reduced to 0 hit points, after which it disappears.

rows: Although a deathlock is certainly adept in many dark forms of magic, its physical attributes are not to be laughed at either. In order to ensure that they have the tools to complete their mission, a deathlock's patron grants them a claw powered by necromantic energy that rends the lifeforce from whomever it touches. Proper harvesting of the claw requires one to carve along the ley lines of the wrist to avoid severing its connection to the patron, but when done properly, it can be refashioned into a most wicked weapon.

name: Deathlock Mastermind
rows: The black heart of a deathlock no longer serves any useful biological function. In fact, more often than not, it has ossified from exposure to necromantic energies and more resembles an anatomical model than an actual organ. Proper harvesting of the claw requires one to carve along the ley lines of the wrist to avoid severing its connection to the patron, but when done properly, it can be refashioned into a most wicked weapon.

The deathlocks that have managed to redeem their worth in their patron's eyes are granted greater powers that rival the ones they had in life. This time around however, the deathlock's pact is sealed onto their body to prevent their misuse and squandering. This comes in the form of a brand somewhere on the deathlock that glows with other-planar energy. If harvested intact, the power of the patron can be stolen and repurposed to grant a mage a boost to their arcane abilities. Just don't let the surviving followers of the patron track you down afterwards though...

name: Deep Forest Random Encounters
rows: The party comes across a grove where the smaller trees have been flattened and broken. Large paw prints are sunk deep into the earth.

The party stumbles upon a {@creature forest prowler|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} protecting its injured mate. A successful {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) check allows a character to get close enough to see that the injured beast has been gored by antlers.
{@dice 2d4} {@creature Sticky Slime|HumblewoodCampaignSetting|sticky slimes} begin spilling out of a rotten tree and attack.
A pile of leaves and twigs stirs. A {@creature shambling mound} attacks.

A {@creature hedge witch|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} and their {@creature phase spider} are here, gathering reagents for making potions. They attack only if provoked and offer two {@item potion of healing||potions of healing} in exchange for any unusual flora or animal remains the party might have.

The party discovers a bandit campground in a clearing. {@dice 2d4} {@creature Mapach Bandit|HumblewoodCampaignSetting| mapach bandits} and a {@creature vulpin captain|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} can be found cooking, cleaning their weapons, and squabbling. The bandits are out in the forest hiding 500 gp worth of coin, goods, and heirlooms looted from a caravan. If the bandits are given any reason to distrust the party, they start a fight immediately.

name: Deep Gnome Trinket Table
rows: 1 stone carved likeness of a family member

entries: Despite the fact that a deep scion reverts to its original form upon its death, there is still a mark of its dark patron that lingers for a moment before vanishing into the aether. A quick application of {@item spirit paper|HHHVI} can trap this essence and reuse it for later, hopefully for more altruistic purposes. {@b Requires {@item spirit paper|HHHVI}.}

entries.name: Use:
entries: You may spend an action to tear this item in half. If you do so, all creatures within 300 feet of you must succeed on a {@dc 13} Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition stunned} until the end of your next turn. In addition, any creature that succeeds on the saving throw gains the memories of the last 24 hours of the deep scion from whom this item was harvested.

name: Deep Scion Trinket Table
rows: 1 {@item pouch|PHB} of ocean floor mud (great for sore joints and facial masks)
1 memento of previous life (picture, doll, small piece of jewelry)

name: Defensive Items
footnotes: Shields and bracers can't benefit from armor crafting modifications.

name: Deinonychus
rows: The deinonychus possesses a distinctive sickle shaped claw on its hind feet. These claws make for wonderful sickle substitutes when a metallic version cannot be made.

name: Demesne Surge
rows: Each creature, including yourself, within 30 feet of you that isn't behind total cover must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or take damage equal to your wizard level.
The target of the next spell you cast before the end of your next turn will be determined randomly by the DM after you choose what to cast.
A burst of faerzress energy blinds you until the end of your next turn.
On your next turn, you can't cast any spells that require a spell slot.
You must spend all of your movement on your next turn moving as far away from all other creatures as possible.
You suddenly feel extremely itchy and must immediately make a Constitution saving throw to maintain your {@status concentration} if you are {@status concentration||concentrating} on a spell.
You become intensely paranoid until the end of your next turn and can't take any actions that would directly aid an ally.
You lose your balance and fall {@condition prone}.
You speed is increased by 10 feet on your next turn.
You gain advantage on your next attack roll until the end of your next turn.
You gain advantage on the next saving throw you make until the end of your next turn.
You force one creature you target with a spell that requires a saving throw before the end of your next turn to make their saving throw with disadvantage.
You instantly cast the misty step spell without expending a spell slot or using your bonus action.
You instantly regain hit points equal to half your wizard level (rounded down).
You instantly cast the shield spell without expending a spell slot or using your reaction.
Double the amount of damage you deal to one target with the next damaging spell you cast before the end of your next turn.

Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you that isn't behind total cover must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or take damage equal to your wizard level. If the creature is on a patch of faerzress created by your Radiate Faerzress feature, it takes damage equal to twice your wizard level.

name: Demigod Domains and Spells
caption: Demigod Domains and Spells
rows: {@spell charm person|PHB}, {@spell Tasha's Hideous Laughter|PHB|hideous laughter}

name: Demilich
rows: The disintegrated remains of a demilich's body. Every-time you look away, it seems to move slightly. Can be used as a spell component for powerful and dark necromantic magics.

Rather than a corporeal body, most of the demilich's shape consists of a choking vapour that smells like forgotten tombs. This smoke contains an almost insignificantly small fraction of the demilich's true essence, but if bottled and stored properly, can be turned into an item to track the demilich wherever it may reappear. {@b Requires {@item enchanted vial|HHHVI}.}

The demilich disciples of {@creature Acererak|ToA} practice a particularly notorious necromantic magic: inserting soul gems into their empty eye sockets to steal the spirits of their victims. While taking the gem away from a defeated demilich is simply a matter of picking it up, turning it over to your own control is considerably harder and requires a complicated ritual soon after the demilich's defeat. A successful result grants the bearer a powerful, but dark magical artifact.

name: Demogorgon
rows: The mysterious Y-shaped symbol of Demogorgon that drives all who gaze upon it mad is said to be representative of their spine that branches into two in order to support their dual heads. It is at this nexus that the madness and paranoia of both heads collide, creating a potent magical source capable of breaking the minds of lesser creatures it is used upon.

name: Derro
rows: They say in the Underdark, "talk to four derros and you will find five psychoses." Indeed, the derro are among the more peculiar of the races to be found in the subterranean realm, and absolutely none of them have displayed behavior that could be considered "sane" by our standards. That is not to say that they are invalids, however. In fact, their so-called "madness" has served them well in keeping them alive in their hostile environment, really raising the question of what true madness even means. Either way, their eccentricities leads to their brains all being shaped differently, much like the unique patterns of a snowflake. For the more morbid academics, derro brains provide invaluable research into the nature of psychology, and thus can be sold for a tidy sum.

name: Derro Savant
rows: They say in the Underdark, "talk to four derros and you will find five psychoses." Indeed, the derro are among the more peculiar of the races to be found in the subterranean realm, and absolutely none of them have displayed behavior that could be considered "sane" by our standards. That is not to say that they are invalids, however. In fact, their so-called "madness" has served them well in keeping them alive in their hostile environment, really raising the question of what true madness even means. Either way, their eccentricities leads to their brains all being shaped differently, much like the unique patterns of a snowflake. For the more morbid academics, derro brains provide invaluable research into the nature of psychology, and thus can be sold for a tidy sum.

The derro god, Diirinka, is an odd entity, even among the greater pantheon of deities in the multiverse. First and foremost, it remains unclear if he even exists, or is simply another figment of the shared psychosis of the derro people. Regardless, his mark regularly appears in the form of a gray, black, and white spiral somewhere on the gifted derro that have been touched by Diirinka's magic. It is a simple enough task to take this mark and repurpose it for boons that channel his power...if he even exists at all.

name: Derro Trinket Table
rows: 25 feet of frayed {@item Hempen Rope (50 feet)|PHB|rope}

name: Desert Encounters
caption: Desert Encounter
rows: Vultures picking an elf carcass clean
Stone statue of a man clad in armor
Old boot with a map inside
Road sign too weatherworn to read
Merchant trying to sell a map to a forgotten library
Paladin searching for an evil cult
Skeleton clutching a piece of parchment
Squire weeping for his dead knight
Table set for a feast, not a soul in sight
Swordsman challenging any who pass by to a duel
Hermit who wants to be left alone
Lone skeleton clutching a rusty sword
Tracks of an orc war party
Merchant trying to sell "a magic lamp".
Beautiful woman who disappears when approached
Woman dying of a mortal wound
Broken wagon with rotten goods inside
Giant stone arm sticking out if the sand
Severed head stuck on a pike
Glass bottle with a love letter inside
Familiar tracks, you may be lost
Handsome man who dissipates when approached
Chest marked "Do not open under any circumstance."
Pilgrims on their way to a holy site
Golden statue of a woman holding a spear
Man grieving for his dead horse
Group of children clad in armor
Oasis occupied by a group of travelers
Knight weeping over his dead squire
Demon looking to make a deal
Rusty sword with "Honor" engraved on the blade
Rock in the shape of a crowned head

name: Desert Herds
rows: A group of {@dice 4d6} {@creature Elephant|XMM|Elephants} strolls calmly across the desert. They use their massive tusks to uproot large underground plants to eat. Occasionally, calves stray from the herd, but the protective mothers quickly usher them back.
A herd of a hundred antelopes (use the statistics of {@creature Deer|XMM}) crosses the Wasteland in a large-scale migration. They are skittish and easily frightened.

{@dice 10d10} {@creature Boar|XMM|Boars} stampede across the Wasteland, pursued by a {@creature Bulette|XMM} traveling underground. The thunderous noise of the boars and the rising plume of dust they raise are visible and audible from a mile away. The bulette is unable to catch them.

Roll twice on the {@table Wasteland Creatures|SandsOfDoom} table, rerolling duplicates. The two groups of creatures encountered each other and fought to the death. Nearly a hundred scavengers—{@creature Vulture|XMM|Vultures} and {@creature Hyena|XMM|Hyenas}—are now feasting on the corpses.

A group of {@dice 8d6} {@creature Camel|XMM|Camels} and their {@dice 2d4} calves (camels with 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}) are eating a large patch of spiny plants. The calves are friendly and approach the characters, while the adults bellow and spit bile at anyone who comes near.

A group of {@dice 1d4} {@creature Giant Goat|XMM|Giant Goats} leads {@dice 4d6} {@creature Goat|XMM|Goats} through a craggy canyon, climbing the cliffs to reach a mesa where an additional {@dice 2d6} {@creature Goat|XMM|Goats} await them. There is plenty of grass and shrubbery for the goats to eat. The goats are peaceful and friendly unless attacked.
