name: Gnoll Witherling
rows: A gnoll skeleton that has been transformed into a witherling is much the same as any other. However, prolonged exposure to the elements can cause them to gain a unique layer of dust the consistency (and smell) of extremely aged cheese. While this dust is not overtly magical, it is very useful as pounce for drying the mystical inks that fiendish cults use when scribing their dark tomes and scrolls. Needless to say, this product has a very niche market.
The sharp, irregular teeth of a gnoll. Not worth much other than as a trophy. Harvesters are advised to wash them at the first chance, as they carry the stench of a gnoll's mouth long after removal.

name: Gnome, Deep
rows: The skin of the cavern dwelling gnomish subrace is a distinctive ashy-grey in colour and has adapted over millennia to a subterranean lifestyle. As such, it can be fashioned into a good cloak that provides ample camouflage when spelunking. I wouldn't recommend wearing it around civilised society however.

To find your long lost sibling.
To prove you deserve your parents' love.

entries: Use this area to keep track of the scoring elements of the game!

name: Goblin
rows: Goblins neither possess much of value, nor are made of anything of value. Goblin ears are perhaps the only thing worth carving off of an average goblin, if only because dogs enjoy snacking on them the same way they enjoy pig ears.

name: Goblin Boss
rows: Goblins neither possess much of value, nor are made of anything of value. Goblin ears are perhaps the only thing worth carving off of an average goblin, if only because dogs enjoy snacking on them the same way they enjoy pig ears.

name: Golden Goose Domain Spells
rows: {@spell conjure honkland beings|Honkonomicon}*, {@spell freedom of movement}

name: Good Hunt
rows: Found climbing a steep canyon. The goats put up a stubborn fight if challenged. Each is enough to feed up to twenty people.
Buried half a foot beneath the sand, they leap out aggressively when approached. Each can feed up to five people.
Found stampeding across the desert, each can feed up to twenty people.
Found digging for underground plants, they run at the first sign of danger. Each can feed up to ten people.
Found in an elevated canyon near several nests, each bird can feed one person. The nests contain {@dice 4d4} eggs, with four eggs enough to feed one person.
They are found skulking and tracking the characters but flee at the first hint of danger. Each can feed up to ten people.

name: Good Hunt
rows: Found climbing a steep canyon. The goats put up a stubborn fight if challenged. Each is enough to feed up to twenty people.
Buried half a foot beneath the sand, they leap out aggressively when approached. Each can feed up to five people.
Found stampeding across the desert, each can feed up to twenty people.
Found digging for underground plants, they run at the first sign of danger. Each can feed up to ten people.
Found in an elevated canyon near several nests, each bird can feed one person. The nests contain {@dice 4d4} eggs, with four eggs enough to feed one person.
They are found skulking and tracking the characters but flee at the first hint of danger. Each can feed up to ten people.

name: Goodest Boi Oath Spells
rows: {@spell Dispel Evil and Good|PHB|dispel evil}, {@spell sonic shriek|KTVSCO|thunderous barking}{@sup K}

name: Goose Behaviour
rows: The goose spends its time beating its wings and honking ferociously, but takes no other action.
The goose moves up to its speed towards a hostile creature it can see and makes a beak attack against it.

The goose flies up into the air and remains there honking ferociously. All creatures (including you) that are within 30 feet of the goose and can see and hear it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw versus your ranger spell save DC or become {@condition frightened} of the goose until the end of their next turn.
The goose decides to listen to your commands, and follows them to the best of its ability.
The goose moves up to its speed and attacks the nearest creature (friend or foe) to it, hissing angrily.

The goose regains the use of its honk, makes two attacks whenever it takes the {@action attack} action, and its damage die increases to a {@dice d10}. It then moves up to its speed and attacks the nearest hostile creature it can see.

name: Goose-Blooded Quirks Table
rows: Your head sprouts small, fine feathers instead of conventional hair. The feathers can change colors to suit your mood, granting you advantage on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation} and {@skill Persuasion}) checks.
Your feet are webbed like that of a duck. You have a swimming speed equal to your walking speed.

Your eyes are further apart than most others, granting you a wider field of vision with which to observe your surroundings and potential threats. You can't be {@status surprised} by creatures within 60 feet of you, and creatures within 60 feet of you don't get advantage on their attack rolls as a result of being hidden from you.
Your bones are less dense than usual, making you extremely lightweight, regardless of your size. You count as one size smaller for the purposes of being pulled, pushed, or lifted by another creature.

Your tongue is lined with razor-sharp teeth, granting you a taste for many otherwise unappetizing foodstuffs. You sustain yourself by eating rotting meat, small insects, raw grains, and other difficult-to-digest foodstuffs, and suffer no ill effects from ingesting them.

You secrete a hydrophobic oil, preventing your skin from becoming wet. As a result, you remain warm when wet, and you dry off completely in a matter of minutes, regardless of how wet you previously were. In addition, the lack of moisture grants you resistance to lightning damage.

You have a set of hardened bone spurs on each of your elbows or wrists. These bone spurs can be used as natural weapons, and deal {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage on a hit. You can make an additional attack with your natural weapons as a bonus action when you use your action to make a melee weapon attack, provided your hands aren't full.

At the beginning of each new dawn, you imprint on one creature or moving object you see within the first 10 minutes of waking up. You see this object or creature as a treasured friend who must be protected. The object or creature grants you a single inspiration die, which is a {@dice d6}. This die lasts for 8 hours, or until expended. When you or a treasured friend you can see within 30 feet of you would make a saving throw or an ability check, you can expend your inspiration die and roll it, adding the number rolled to the total of the saving throw or ability check. You can roll the inspiration die after the ability check or saving throw is made, but before you know the outcome.

name: Gorge Treasure
rows: Two {@item backpack|PHB|backpacks} with {@dice 1d6} {@item Rations (1 day)|PHB|rations} each
Morrigy's Field Journal, an incomplete journal for foraging mushrooms
Four unused {@item Hempen Rope (50 feet)|PHB|50-foot-long coils of hemp rope}
outro: In addition, the characters find {@item goggles of night} among the belongings. Calliope informs the characters that the gear they found belongs to the teens. If the characters rescue them, the teens allow the heroes to keep what they found as thanks.

name: Gorgon
rows: The naturally produced oil of the gorgon is a widely sought after lubricant. Crafters from all fields can find some use for it in their work and demand always exceeds supply.

entries: Gorgon Gas Sack
(Only harvestable if the gorgon had its petrifying breath ability available upon death)

The gas gland of a gorgon, located just behind its nasal cavity. Resembles a balloon if it were made from metal foil. When harvested, can be given a good squeeze to produce the same petrifying effect its owner once used.

entries.name: Use:
entries: As an action you may squeeze the sack and release a petrifying gas in a 30-foot cone. Each creature in that area must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target begins to turn to stone and is {@condition restrained}. The {@condition restrained} target must repeat the saving throw at the end of its next turn. On a success, the effects ends on the target. On a failure, the target is {@condition petrified} until freed by the {@spell greater restoration} spell or other magic. Once used, the sack is emptied and becomes useless.

rows: The hooves of a gorgon resemble anvils more than anything else. It is ironic then that these are often reforged by blacksmiths on their own anvils.
{@filter +1 Greatclub, Maul or Warhammer|items|source=|type=|category=specific variant|base item=greatclub__phb;maul__phb;warhammer__phb|bonus=weapon attack and damage rolls (+1)}

It is hard to decide whether it is preferable to die by the hooves or the horn of a gorgon. Either way, a successfully harvested gorgon horn can be refined by any skilled blacksmith into a formidable weapon.

{@filter +1 Lance, Trident, War Pick, Javelin or Spear|items|source=|type=|category=specific variant|base item=lance__phb;war pick__phb;trident__phb;javelin__phb;spear__phb|bonus=weapon attack and damage rolls (+1)}
The iron-like armor plating of a gorgon is incredibly hard and yet is supple and breathes like skin. It is thus a unique and useful material for making fine armors.
{@filter Any +1 Heavy Armor or Shield|items|source=|type=heavy armor;shield|category=specific variant|search=+1}

name: Goristro
rows: The fur of a goristro resembles that of a wild bull and seems to constantly emanate a faint heat. More ostentatious warlocks tend to spin their winter cloaks from this material, but whether or not it has any magical utility is still up for debate.

The blood of the goristro constantly bubbles, even long after it is removed from its source. When prepared into a potion, it can grant the drinker the strength of the demon it came from, but the side effects may not be worth it.

A goristro's hoof is made of the same material as its infamous horns and thus are just as hard. Wielding a hammer forged from these hooves is a sure-fire way to strike fear into the hearts of your enemies.

Castle architects and siege masters have an old joke, that if armies ever learned how to train goristros, they'd both be out of a job. Indeed, the horn of the goristro is stronger than castle stone walls and a single one of these demons are capable of ending a siege by themselves. It takes a master craftsman to properly grind these horns down, but the resulting dust can be used to reinforce a weapon to make it as strong as the demon it was harvested from.

name: Gossip Table
rows: Give the characters some gossip about a random townsperson: choose or randomly determine which person the party gains a bit of information about.
There's a witch in the woods nearby who sells potions and healing remedies, but no one in town likes to visit her. While she acts friendly, the dead animals on her porch are very off-putting.
There's an old man living by himself on the outskirts of town. Sometimes he comes screaming into town when an owlbear knocks down his hut again, but for the most part, he seems to dislike everybody.

{@creature Gellert the Gruesome|KPSC} has a small army of monsters and bandits at his command, and they roam the woods and roads looking for easy marks. Redtower rarely comes under attack, but travelers aren't so lucky.

{@creature Alseid|ToB|Alseids} {@homebrew |(see Tome of Beasts)} tend to the temple of Yarila and Porevit outside of town, near the orchard. Only Cibor talks to them much, but the produce he brings back from trading with them is enormous.
Constable Roch is suspicious of adventurers, and it's best not to get caught being drunk or difficult around town.
The red tower ({@adventure R10|KPSC|2|R10. The Red Tower}) was made from the bones and teeth of the fallen giant Milena and Henrik slew, and his blood soaked the stones placed there forever.

Each time an adventurer perishes in the Scarlet Citadel, an unknown artist slips out by nightfall and paints a stone red at the red tower ({@adventure R10|KPSC|2|R10. The Red Tower}) in their honor. Over time, the stones of the tower have been painted red many, many times.

The stones to build the red tower ({@adventure R10|KPSC|2|R10. The Red Tower}) came from the ruins submerged beneath the pond to the north. Before they were covered in water and moss, there was a property to them that makes them red—possibly even some strange magical energy protecting them from the ravages of time.

Give the party information to warn them on one of the townsfolk who will try to take advantage of them. Either choose or randomly determine who they are warned about: Mayor Broz, Constable Roch, {@creature Konrad of Runkelstad|KPSC|Konrad}, {@creature Witek|KPSC}, Eva, or the merchants.

The party receives a warning about one of the hazards from the {@table Terrain Encounter Table|KPSC} {@homebrew |(see page 30)}. Randomly determine which one they hear about; if that hazard is encountered, they receive advantage on rolls to spot or avoid it.

The party is alerted to the existence of a lifeless clearing in {@adventure E3|KPSC|2|E3. The Lifeless Clearing} and to the suspicion that Gabe from the orchard ({@adventure R13|KPSC|2|R13. Orchard}) snuck out there recently and has been acting strangely since. Additionally, Gellert's henchmen have been spotted in the area more often.

name: Gothic Horror; Grand Cathedral District
rows: A banshee's wail echoes through the cavernous nave, preceding a tragic death.
The beast-repelling incense becomes tainted, allowing monsters to infiltrate the cathedral under the cover of night.
Screams are heard from the abandoned asylum below, along with rattling chains and strange machinery.
A deceased loved one's voice pleads from beyond the grave to meet them in the chamber atop the Pillar of Blood.
The enormous bell towers are suddenly overrun by ravens cawing ominously as they circle overhead.

name: Gothic Horror; New Bridge District
rows: Heavy rainfall causes bodies to float up in the canals from the remains of a previous Hunt. Some seem not entirely dead...
Strange skittering and screeches are heard from within boarded up buildings.
Severed body parts are found arranged ritualistically near the lightning rods of the Scion's fortress.
Ghostly figures are glimpsed wandering the ruins of buildings destroyed in the First War.
The generators in the Scion's fortress suddenly shutdown, plunging the district into darkness.

name: Gothic Horror; Outside the Walls
rows: Strange rituals are glimpsed at night in the ruins of the cosmic seminary.
Half-eaten corpses are found hanging from trees by their guts in the forest surrounding the city.
Glowing eyes are seen peering from the gloom in the acidic ruins of Jägerweiler.
Mournful sobbing is heard from fresh grave sites in the Cemetery of Ash.
Dark riders are seen passing on trails leading to the forest of the Circle of Symbiosis.

name: Gothic Horror; Paterna Iter District
rows: Fresh blood drips down the vines of the sealed black parish church.
Strange chanting is heard from the ruins late at night, along with flickering torchlight.
Partially eaten corpses missing various organs are found across many homes.
Plants in the vertical farms become animated and lash out at workers tending to them.
Guests at a garden party turn on each other in a frenzy, as if possessed by an evil spirit.

name: Gothic Horror; Ruby District
rows: Beastly howls and snarls echo from the depths of the sewers at night.
A mansion long thought abandoned is lit up and music is heard, but it goes silent when investigated.
Strange worms adorning human faces are discovered burrowing into corpses in the communal cemeteries.
Severed body parts are arranged in a grotesque sculpture in the town square.
A little girl's creepy singing voice foretells victims before they are slain by beasts.

name: Gothic Horror; Sanctified District
rows: Wax replicas of nobles are found staring from windows, preceding their disappearance.
Mysterious scratching and movement is heard from portraits on the walls.
Guests at a masquerade ball are slowly poisoned, leading to bloody coughing fits.
Unearthly screams are heard from the catacombs beneath the castles.
Plants in the gardens wither and die overnight, replaced with disturbing bone sculptures.

name: Gothic Horror; Shrouded District
rows: A miner goes mad, convinced the lumps of coal he digs up are fossilized hearts of the dead.
Mysterious symbols and runes are found painted in blood throughout an abandoned warehouse.
Echoing cries are heard from a mine shaft that collapsed years ago, killing all workers inside.
The smog takes on a sinister face and whispers dark secrets to lone wanderers.
A masked plague doctor stalks victims under the cover of the smog, though their murders resemble anything but medical research.

name: Gothic Horror; Waterfront District
rows: Bloated corpses wash up on the shores missing their faces.
The Tidewatcher lighthouse stops rotating at night and blood begins to seep from it.
Sinister shadows flit beneath the surface of the water under the bridges.
Ghostly visages are seen pleading from barred windows at the Abyssal Keep.
A ship is found drifting, its entire crew slaughtered and crucified to the mast.

name: Graveyards: Characteristics
intro: Use the table below, to add a trait to a graveyard.
rows: A small cemetery with markers placed at random.
A small graveyard surrounded by a low iron fence wreathed in ivy.
A small, dusty cemetery where no grass grows.
A small graveyard surrounded by a fieldstone wall.
A small cemetery founded among large fir trees that screen it from casual view.
A small graveyard, completely flat with perfectly even rows of grave markers. The oldest–least visited graves–are in the centre of the graveyard.
A small cemetery where white posies grow over each grave. A small team of gardeners tends the perfectly maintained grounds.
A moderately-sized graveyard with paths lined with small smooth stones. The paths meander through the graves, which are haphazardly placed.
A moderately-sized cemetery lit all night by oil lanterns hung from high iron poles.
A moderately-sized graveyard where a cold wind blows from the east.
A moderately-sized cemetery features rust coloured grass in the oldest section, as if stained with dried blood.
A moderately-sized graveyard. Two statues of armoured knights flank the entrance. A stone wall surrounds the cemetary.
A moderately-sized cemetery with a small stream running through the east corner. Thick hedges surround the whole area.
A moderately-sized graveyard featuring a stone shack in the corner for the caretaker. A special furnace rests outside for cremation services.
A moderately-sized cemetery where all the carving depict skeletal visages.
A moderately sized graveyard with rows of welltended tulips.
A large cemetery dotted with ruins of an ancient settlement or building.
A large graveyard with graves sprawled across several small hills. It includes several small shrines.
A large cemetery set about a white marble fountain at its centre. Wooden benches surround the fountain.
A large graveyard studded with apple trees throughout the grounds. Visitors are free to pick the apples.

name: Graveyards: Epitaphs
intro: Many grave markers are inscribed with personal messages about the person or persons interred within.
rows: A man for all the ages.
The great eye sees but never touches.
He died as he lived. Drunk
The day will come when dragons walk and halflings fly.
Obedient to the law, we lie.
Heroes have the whole earth for their tomb.
To die is to defy immortality.
Defender of Whiteforge, until he took an arrow to the knee.
I told you I was sick.
The whites of their eyes were not enough.
EAs you are now, so once was I. Prepare, therefore, to follow me.
A lady is only as great as her horse and her man, in that order.
Through demons, through devils, through horrors of afar, the swords and the axes and daggers will mar.
In the eyes of the gods we are but moments.
Trust me, if I had no money in life, I have less in death.
The itch of wisdom is a dangerous scratch.
Sing the songs of your ancestors so their spirits will know the words.
By his father's blade he knows his mother's presence.

name: Graveyards: Grave Markings
intro: The grave markers of a cemetery are as unique as the people buried within. At a minimum, most such markers name the person buried within, but they have many other characteristics. Use the tables below to generate interesting grave markers.

name: Graveyards: Headstones
intro: The most common grave marking. Headstones are generally made of stone, stand two to four feet tall and are engraved to denote who is buried beneath. Moderately agile PCs can leap on a headstone. Headstones generally only provide partial cover.
rows: A marble headstone with a rounded top.
A limestone headstone with squared off corners.
A marble headstone covered in cobwebs.
A sandstone headstone with a large crack down the left side.
A granite headstone with a slanted top.
A marble headstone splattered with bird droppings.
A limestone headstone overgrown with ivy.
A sandstone headstone of a strange purple hue.
A white marble headstone that seems to glow in the moonlight.
A limestone headstone that's fallen onto its side.
A granite headstone with the image of a praying child engraved at the top.
A granite headstone with a small door carved into the base.
A marble headstone topped with an angel, arms outstretched.
A sandstone headstone topped with a stooped gargoyle.
A marble headstone leaning far to the right.
A granite headstone whose lettering has been inlaid with gold leaf.
A marble headstone engraved with the image of a whale.
A limestone headstone flanked by small rose bushes.
A granite headstone half sunk into the ground.
A marble headstone topped with an ornate stone sun.

name: Graveyards: Hooks, Complications & Opportunites
intro: Graveyards are a place for the dead, and as such should only be minimally occupied by the living. Exceptions tend to create very interesting circumstances.
rows: A wizard seeks an ebon flower for an important ritual. It only grows in ground seeped with the flesh and blood of orcs. A small flower-cloaked burial mound in an isolated corner of the graveyard holds the bodies of a score of such raiders killed long ago.
The mayor of the town died in his sleep at an old age. At the funeral, which is happening as the PCs enter the area, his grieving daughter throws open the coffin to find it empty.
Someone has being knocking over headstones at night. The local constable sess the issue beneath him but has a few coins in his coffers to anyone who can catch the culprit.

A tribe of {@table Wandering Monster: centaur|RSP|centaurs} have made camp in the middle of the graveyard, claiming the land is part of an ancestral pact agreed upon by the town's founder generations ago.
Legend says a local wizard took the secret of destroying gods to his grave. The PCs have been tipped off that it's not just a turn of phrase and that a tome of knowledge lies in his tomb.
The manager of the local orphanage got drunk and buried the rent money for its own safety in the graveyard. He can't remember which headstone he buried it under.

A group of clerics of the god of death have gathered from all over the area to celebrate a prophet buried here. They've taken all the rooms in the inn and set up a tent city outside the graveyard gates. At night, loud chanting emanates from the graveyard.
A young boy claims to see the image of his dead uncle walking the graveyard at night. Superstitious peasants want to exile the boy to lay the ghost to rest.
Two young lovers, whose parent refuse to let them marry, have sealed themselves inside a mausoleum. When the PCs arrive, screams of terror erupt from within.
Large holes, signs of a {@creature Bulette|mm}, have been spotted at the centre of the cemetery. Several graves have disappeared into the creature's tunnels.

A {@creature necromancer|vgm} has set up shop, selling his services to provide mourners a day with an undead loved one. Many of the populace disapprove of his actions, but a few recently bereaved townsfolk have hired his services.
A small group of {@table Wandering Monster: Vampires|RSP|vampires} has the populace of a village trapped in its graveyard. The vampires seem to be repulsed by the hallowed ground.

A {@creature Young Black Dragon|mm|black dragon} has made a mausoleum his lair, converted the entire property to unhallowed ground. {@table Wandering Monster: Skeletons|RSP|Skeletons} have been spotted at night by villagers who dare to go close.
A gravedigger has discovered an underground tunnel that bears signs of dwarven construction.

The sword of a knight carved into a sarcophagus lid has begun glowing blue. If a paladin of pure heart approaches the sword, the light grows more intense and the sword transforms into an actual weapon.
A young girl was found wandering among the headstones with no memory of how she came to be there. She is otherwise healthy.
All the cats in town vanished a week ago. This morning their corpses were found stacked upon the grave of the town's founder; all their eyes were gouged out.

A strange grey speckled mist hovers over the graveyard, whispering the words of departed loved ones. The mist is thickest in the newest part of the graveyard and seems to emanate from an as yet unfilled grave.

The local militia has posted a reward for the capture of grave robbers plundering the graveyard. For the last three nights, strange sounds have been heard in the cemetery at night and every morning graves were found disturbed and defaced.
{@creature Assassin vine|toa|Assassin vines} have spread from the forest across the oldest parts of the graveyard. Luckily, no one has yet been taken, although several cats and dogs have disappeared.
Large holes, signs of a {@creature ankheg|mm}, have been spotted at the centre of the cemetery. Several graves have disappeared into the creature's tunnels.

name: Graveyards: Mausoleums
intro: A mausoleum is a free-standing structure that holds the dead above ground. They vary in size but often comprise but one room. Most are onestorey affairs.
Mausoleums most often hold multiple bodies and may be owned by families or prosperous organizations. Many are ostentatiously decorated
rows: A one-room square building of stone, with four columns at the entrance.
A rounded granite structure with a red dome.The dome's paint has started to fade.
A two-storey marble building. The second floor is lined with columns.
A simple stone structure with a heavy iron door. The door has four separate locks.
A limestone building; statues of tiefling mages stand in place of columns. Each mage holds a different set of spell components.
A brick structure that was once a small temple. One of the stain glass windows is broken.
A crumbling stone building with a heavy stone door. The door's lintel has shifted, making it very hard to open.
A square structure with a slanted red slate roof. An old oak shades the structure.
A large marble building. Statues of angels stand on the roof above the entrance, their axes crossed. Several have been vandalised.
A small structure set back away from the other graves amongst a copse of trees.
A simple building of wood with a slanted roof and a sliding steel door. The wood is as hard as stone and has been carved with images of clouds and flying dragons.
A stone wall set into a hill, with a locked gate for a door. A narrow stone-lined passageways slopes downwards into the hill.
An ivy covered building of white stone. Three small windows are set about eight feet above the ground.
A small, one-room stone building with a green slanted roof. Weeds grow in profusion around the structure.
A building of moderate size with soldiers carved across the exterior walls.
Three rows of demonic statues flank the path leading up to this small round structure.
A long one-storey building with several doors along the main wall.
A three-storey, round structure with several small parapets. The whole gives the impression of a watchtower or keep.
A small, square building, set atop a small hill, with stone steps leading to its doors.
A set of bronze doors, set into a frame of stone in the earth. Stone stairs lead to the one-room mausoleum below.

name: Graveyards: Minor Events
intro: Graveyards are often surprisingly busy places during the day.
rows: Two labourers are digging a new grave. A pile of moist earth stands to one side.
A mourner kneels in front of a grave, sobbing.
An interment ceremony is taking place. Mourners stand about a grave as a priest reads from a holy book.
A furtive, pale-skinned man skulks among the graves studying their markings.
A gardener tends the graveyard's grass, flowers or trees. He has encyclopaedic knowledge of the surrounding graves.
A couple–or a couple with children–stroll through the graveyard, flowers in hand.

name: Graveyards: Sarcophagi
intro: A box-like container for a corpse. They can be buried like a coffin, but also set above ground in place of a grave. Agile PCs can leap on a sarcophagus. They provide partial to total cover.
rows: The weather-worn image of a man with his hands crossed adorns the lid.
Engraved all along the sides of the box is a battle between man and minotaur.
Carvings of cavorting imps cover each of the sarcophagi's corners.
The lid is smooth and painted with an iconographic lineage.
The lid depicts two lovers in bed entwined around one another.
Several gods are carved into the sides of the box with small kings kneeling at their feet.
A montage of the important rites of a local temple, from birth to burial, is engraved along the sides of the box.
A serpent-like dragon wraps across three sides of the box. The dragon is very life-like. Observant PCs may note that pressing both of its eyes opens the sarcophagus.
The lid is carved with the image of a hundred, crawling beetles.
An elderly bald man is carved into each side of the box. He has a different facial expression in each carving.
The sarcophagus is plain except a single eye carved into the lid.
The runes along one side of this sarcophagus are the instructions for how to construct a catapult.
Blue-green moss grows all over the sarcophagi, obscuring any engraving. The moss is dry, almost desiccated and if disturbs fills the air with dust.
There is no lid yet the insides are bathed in shadow.
The sides are all carved with flame and a single clawed hand adorns the lid.
The statue of an angel with sword outstretched, towers over this sarcophagus.
The ballad of Rose Peak is engraved across the lid in beautiful flowing carven handwriting.
The lid is slightly ajar and has been crudely sealed with plaster.
The statuette of an elderly man, sitting with a book, rests atop the lid. The statuette is hollow and holds the key to the sarcophagi.
An engraved lantern burns at each of the sarcophagus' corners. Enchanted with {@spell Continual Flame|phb}, they fill the surrounds with light.

entries: Not as potent as a black pudding, but highly acidic nonetheless. Some blacksmithing techniques actually use this acid in advanced smithing projects, but the difficulty and volatility of controlling the residue has made this a rather esoteric art-form. {@b Requires {@item enchanted vial|HHHVI}.}

entries.name: Use:
entries: A vial of gray residue can be poured on a piece of nonmagical metal. This ooze will eat through 2 inches of that metal every round for the next 10 rounds, after which it becomes too diluted to continue.

name: Gray Render
rows: A gray render's claw resembles that of a bear's, and like a bear's, they are capable of mauling a target as well as rudimentary grasping. The gray render often employs both these functions when serving its master, slaughtering some prey before dragging the carcass back like an oversized, monstrous puppy.
{@filter +2 Melee Slashing Weapon|items|source=dmg|type=melee weapon|category=|weapon damage type=s|bonus=weapon attack and damage rolls (+2)}

Due to their vaguely psionic and mystical nature, the hide of a gray render has more uses than for simply tanning into a suit of armor (although it is certainly quite useful for that). One use that has always stood out to me, is its use as sheets on a marital bed. It is believed by some cultures that any freshly wed couple that sleeps upon a gray render blanket on their first night as a couple will be loyal to one another for life the way that the gray render is loyal to their chosen master. I cannot verify the validity of this claim, but I can attest that sleeping on a lumpy, tough, gray sheet is not the most romantic way to begin your marriage.
{@item +2 Leather Armor|DMG} or {@item +2 Studded Leather Armor|DMG}

The gray render is known for forming lifelong bonds with a creature that it declares as its master. This need for companionship is so strong that it warps the gray render's brain, enlarging portions responsible for emotional attachment and increasing the production of certain enzymes and hormones. As such, a gray render's brain is a treasure trove for any alchemist looking to mix together a bewildering brew or charming concoction.
{@item Philter of Love|DMG} or {@item Concoction of Companionship|HHHVIII}

name: Gray Slaad
rows: The slime that coats a slaad smells like the bottom of a fetid swamp and looks like it too. It is believed that this slime has an innocuation effect against the diseases and parasitic eggs of the slaads, but this is mostly just conjecture. Otherwise, it is a mere curiosity for eccentric researchers.

entries: Slaadi are creatures of pure chaos, born from the unstable energies in Limbo. As such, their very bodies disrupt the natural order of things and those that consume some of their flesh tend to find that probability itself changes for them, if only temporarily. Beware however, as the universe is not to be trifled with, and it tends to find ways to balance itself out later.

entries.name: Use:
entries: As an action you may eat this item. If you do so, then once within the next 10 minutes you may choose to bend the laws of fate within your favour. If you do so, you gain advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. If you choose not to, this item is wasted. After those 10 minutes have passed, your DM may choose at any time within the next 24 hours to impose disadvantage on 1 attack roll, ability check, or saving throw you make.

rows: The hide of a slaad is extraordinarily tough, and even more so once it has evolved into either its {@creature gray slaad|MM|gray} or {@creature death slaad|MM} variants. As befitting of a slaad's possessive and transformative nature, even the skinned hide of a mature slaad will attempt to mutate and change its wearer. It is only with advanced techniques that this property is curtailed and used only to the benefit of its new owner.

name: Graz'zt
rows: Unlike his beautiful countenance, the heart of Graz'zt is a hideous, shrunken, and shrivelled thing to behold. Graz'zt has neglected all genuine emotions of happiness and love in exachange for indulding in mindless sensual pleasures. This has led to the atrophied condition of his heart, within which is contained the many corruptions and hedonistic acts he has ever committed. The sheer concentration of these depravities make the organ a powerful conduit for particularly foul magic.

name: Great Beast Mutations
caption: Great Beast Mutations
rows: Roll twice on the table, ignoring this result if rolled again.

rows.name: Spawning Pit
entries: Your skin begins to crawl moments before vermin chew through your flesh and erupt from your body. {@dice 1d3} {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} {@creature Swarm of Crawling Claws|XMM|Swarms of Crawling Claws}, {@creature Swarm of Insects|XMM|Insects}, or {@creature Swarm of Rats|XMM|Rats} appear in unoccupied spaces within 10 feet of you. This also happens the first time you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB} after an {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} check.

rows.name: Bloodless
entries: You cannot spend {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} for any reason, including as the result of a spell or other {@variantrule Magical Effect|XPHB}.

rows.name: Corporeal Decay
entries: Your body begins to rapidly decay, giving you a corpselike appearance. When you gain this mutation, roll a number of {@dice 1d8;2d8;3d8;4d8;5d8;6d8;7d8;8d8;9d8;10d8;11d8;12d8;13d8;14d8;15d8;16d8;17d8;18d8;19d8;20d8;|d8s} equal to your character level and take Necrotic damage equal to the result. You have the Undead type in addition to other creature types.

rows.name: Lignify
entries: Your limbs stiffen and woody tree shoots pierce from beneath your skin. You have {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Fire damage and your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} (all movement types) is reduced by 5 feet per your level of {@condition Corruption|GrimHollowCG24}.

rows.name: Scion of the Beast
entries: You carry some of the Great Beast's corruptive nature. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action on your turn, you and another creature of your choice you can see within 60 feet of you each make a {@adventure Mutation check|GrimHollowCG24|20|Great Beast Mutations}.

rows.name: Third Eye
entries: You grow a third eye. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or remove the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition, but you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks.

rows.name: Extra Digits
entries: Your grow several extra fingers. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on checks to avoid being disarmed, but you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) checks.

rows.name: Chameleon
entries: Your skin changes color in stressful situations. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks, but {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Charisma checks.

rows.name: Oily Skin
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on checks made to escape a {@condition Grappled|XPHB|Grapple}, but you have {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Cold and Fire damage.

rows.name: Corrosive Blood
entries: When you become {@status Bloodied|XPHB} for the first time after an {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} roll, creatures within 5 feet of you take Acid damage equal to your character level.

rows.name: Sticky feet
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} of 15 feet, but your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet.

rows.name: Luminescent
entries: You glow with {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} to a range of 30 feet. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks.

rows.name: Thinning Blood
entries: Your bodily fluids become thin and watery. You have the {@condition Bleeding|GrimHollowCG24} condition.

rows.name: Stone Shell
entries: Your skin swells and hardens into a tumorous rocky texture. You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Piercing and Slashing damage, and {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Acid and Thunder damage.

rows.name: Arcane Conduit
entries: Your body becomes a conduit of magic. Add your current {@condition Corruption|GrimHollowCG24} level to your spell save DC and your spell attack rolls. When you cast a spell using a spell slot, make a {@adventure Mutation check|GrimHollowCG24|20|Great Beast Mutations}.

rows.name: Malformed Wings
entries: Spiny, tattered wings burst painfully from your back, giving you a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 20 feet. You cannot move by any other means.

rows.name: Blood-Fueled Frenzy
entries: If you are Bloodied, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on melee attack rolls, and attack rolls against you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}. On each of your turns, you must first move as far as possible toward the nearest {@status Bloodied|XPHB} creature you can see. If you are within 5 feet of it after moving, you must take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action to attack that creature with a melee weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

rows.name: Eldritch Combustion
entries: Your body fills with unStable eldritch power. If you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} you die instantly, and each creature within 20 feet of you must make a {@adventure Mutation check|GrimHollowCG24|20|Great Beast Mutations}.

rows.name: Permanent Transformation
entries: You gain the {@charoption Aberrant Horror|GrimHollowPG24|Aberrant Horror Transformation}. If you already have this or another Transformation, you move to the next stage of that Transformation instead.

name: Greater Mana Ley Line Backlash
rows: If the next spell you cast targets only one creature and doesn't have a range of self, it instead targets up to four random creatures (GM's choice) within the spell's range.
If the next spell you cast deals damage, one target (GM's choice) gains resistance to that damage type.
The next spell you cast fails and is lost.
You have disadvantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
You lose your highest level spell slot up to 3rd level.
You can't cast a spell until the start of your next turn.
Treat the next spell you cast as if it were cast with a spell slot 1 level lower than the one expended to cast it. If this effect would make the spell's level 0 or lower, the spell fails and is lost.

name: Greater Mana Ley Line Beneficial Effects

items: {@b {@i Successful Tap.}} You immediately gain the benefits of a {@spell greater restoration} spell.

rows: If the next spell you cast targets only one creature and doesn't have a range of self, it instead targets up to four creatures of your choice within the spell's range.
If the next spell you cast deals damage, it ignores resistances to its damage type.
If the next spell you cast has material components worth up to 1,000 gp, you ignore it.
You have advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
You regain one of your expended spell slots of your choice, up to 3rd level.
If the next spell you cast forces a creature to make a saving throw to resist its effects, one target of the spell (your choice) has disadvantage on its first saving throw made against the spell.
Treat the next spell you cast as if it were cast with a spell slot one level higher than the one expended to cast it.
Choose one of the effects listed above.

items: 1 {@item Cantrip Spell Scroll|KTKCG|scroll} of {@spell minor illusion|PHB}
A handful of colorful gems worth 250 gp

name: Green Abishai
rows: An abishai is created when {@deity Tiamat|Dawn War|DMG} interferes with the cycle of life and death, snagging a mortal soul before it can move on and transforming it into a monstrous draconic creature to serve her whims in the Hells. This act permanently scars a soul, staining it with the Dragon Queen's mark for all eternity. Upon the abishai's death, this mark can be captured by an enterprising harvester and used to channel the power of {@deity Tiamat|Dawn War|DMG} against her will. {@b Requires {@item spirit paper|HHHVI}.}

Like real dragons, the abishai are gifted with the power of flight by their queen. The powerful wings that they bear are capable of tremendously high speeds, and like many devils, can be harvested and recrafted into the ever useful {@item infernal wings|HHHVI}.

The needs of {@deity Tiamat|Dawn War|DMG} are many, and she creates her servants to serve specific functions. This usually comes in the form of the abishai's horns which, much like a real dragon, contain much of the essence of their power. The green abishai serve as the emissaries of the Dragon Queen, their horns granting them mind altering abilities to influence weak-willed mortals. Their horns carry on their manipulative natures and can be transformed into a magical implement that allows the user to continue the crafty tricks of the ever scheming {@deity Tiamat|Dawn War|DMG}.

name: Green Hag
rows: The hair of a green hag flows like rotten reeds at the bottom of a swamp. While unpleasant to both observe and to hold, it possesses some weak magical properties and is often used by seedier alchemists looking for cheap substitutes for higher quality ingredients.

Absolutely reeking of the foulness that permeated the hag's entire being, drinking this blood has the potential to infect a creature with {@disease crone's disease|HHHVI}. It should also be noted that while the blood smells and tastes as fetid as it looks, alcohol has a neutralising effect on both of these properties. What someone does with that information is entirely out of this writer's control.

Green hags are notorious for their ability to mimic sounds to lure or scare intruders to their lairs. This ability lingers behind in their skulls and artificers can draw out this latent power to create a magical trinket with much of the same property. In several ways, the hag would probably have enjoyed the idea of its carcass being used for such a macabre activity.

entries: Not to be confused with the notorious "hag eye" amulet given by hags to their servants, however the two are tightly linked. Despite being severed from its socket, this eye still seems to glare as it did in life.

entries.name: Use:
entries: As an action you may {@status concentration|PHB|concentrate} on the hag eyeball while it is in your hand. While doing so, you may utilise that hag's hag eye that same way they would have used it in life. If the hag eye is destroyed while you are {@status concentration|PHB|concentrating} on the hag eyeball, you suffer {@damage 3d10} psychic damage and are {@condition blinded} for 24 hours.

name: Green Slaad
rows: The slime that coats a slaad smells like the bottom of a fetid swamp and looks like it too. It is believed that this slime has an innocuation effect against the diseases and parasitic eggs of the slaads, but this is mostly just conjecture. Otherwise, it is a mere curiosity for eccentric researchers.

entries: Slaadi are creatures of pure chaos, born from the unstable energies in Limbo. As such, their very bodies disrupt the natural order of things and those that consume some of their flesh tend to find that probability itself changes for them, if only temporarily. Beware however, as the universe is not to be trifled with, and it tends to find ways to balance itself out later.

entries.name: Use:
entries: As an action you may eat this item. If you do so, then once within the next 10 minutes you may choose to bend the laws of fate within your favour. If you do so, you gain advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. If you choose not to, this item is wasted. After those 10 minutes have passed, your DM may choose at any time within the next 24 hours to impose disadvantage on 1 attack roll, ability check, or saving throw you make.

Only one of a green slaad's claws have much value; the one it used to cast spells with before it became a slaad. This claw is suffused with both the magic of its old life as well as the chaotic energies of Limbo. As such, it grants its wielder incredible, if unreliable, power.

entries.name: Use:
entries: This claw may be used as an {@item arcane focus|PHB}. If you do so, when a creature you can see is forced to roll a saving throw due to a spell you cast, you may force that creature to roll at disadvantage. Once you do so, you must finish a long rest before you can use this feature again. Any time before you regain the use of this feature, the DM can have you roll on the {@table Wild Magic Surge|PHB} table in the {@book Player's Handbook|PHB} immediately after you cast a spell of 1st level or higher. You then regain the use of this ability.

name: Grell
rows: The formidable tentacles of a grell make fine whips once they are removed, dried, treated and fitted with a handle. Many Underdark societies have been seen using whips made from grells, for both their strength and their intimidation factor.

entries: A grell's poison is known to paralyse hapless victims, leaving them helpless as the grell flies away with them to be devoured. By removing the gland located where its tentacles meet its body, this poison can be extracted and used against one's own enemies.

entries.name: Use:
entries: Can be used to coat up to 5 pieces of slashing or piercing ammunition or one slashing or piercing weapon. Applying the poison takes 1 minute. For the next minute, any creature successfully hit must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned}. The {@condition poisoned} target is {@condition paralyzed}, and it can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

rows: The hide of a grell is extremely sensitive to certain stimuli that completely bypasses the sense of most humanoids. Extremely difficult to remove intact, this hide can be used to craft armors that grant its wearer a sixth-sense similar to the grell's own.

name: Grick
rows: The deadly tentacle of a grick is both rubbery and sharp. However, after prolonged tenderising, boiling, and seasoning, these tentacles make for a delicacy that several Underdark races have come to enjoy. It is usually served with a sauce reduced from the grick's own blood. It is an acquired taste to say the least.

The skin of a grick has a unique shade and hue that allows it to blend into its rocky surroundings with ease. While difficult to remove properly from its rubbery carcass, the resulting hide makes for good camouflage clothes.

name: Grievous Wound

chapter.name: The GM's Guide to Dark Fantasy

rows: {@b {@i Permanent Wound.}} You have sustained a serious wound that is most likely permanent. Roll on the Permanent Wound Table and apply the result.
{@b {@i Internal Bleeding*.}} You have suffered an internal hemorrhage and bruising. Your hit point maximum is halved.
{@b {@i Concussion.}} You have received a minor concussion and struggle to focus on complicated tasks. You gain the dazed condition.
{@b {@i Laceration.}} You have taken a deep injury which you are bleeding from. You gain the bleeding condition.

{@b {@i Deep Wound*.}} You have taken a blow that under different circumstances would kill most humanoids. When you are reduced to 0 hit points, you start with an additional failed death saving throw.
{@b {@i Battered*.}} Your muscles ache and you have had the wind knocked out of you. You gain a level of {@condition exhaustion}.
{@b {@i Sprained Wrist*.}} You have badly sprained your wrist, unable to use it effectively. You are unable to hold objects in one of your hands and you cannot take actions that require that arm.
{@b {@i Damaged Eardrum.}} You have suffered a blow to the head and your hearing has been impaired. You gain the {@condition deafened} condition.
{@b {@i System Shock.}} You have suffered a severe nervous system shock. You have disadvantage in Dexterity checks to determine initiative.

{@b {@i Sprained Ankle*.}} You have badly sprained your ankle, unable to use it effectively. Your speed on foot is halved and you cannot take the dash action. If you receive this result a second time your speed on foot becomes 0.
{@b {@i Close Call*.}} You narrowly miss an otherwise dangerous blow. Instead of being reduced to 0 hit points, you fall to 1 hit point instead, and become {@condition prone}.
footnotes: Results with a * next to them can be taken more than once.

name: Grievous Wounds
caption: Grievous Wounds

rows.name: Permanent Wound
entries: You sustain a grisly wound that may haunt you forever. Roll 1d10 on the {@table Permanent Wounds|GrimHollowCG24} table and apply the result.

rows.name: Festering Wound
entries: Your injury becomes infected, causing a fever. You have the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. While {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws. A creature cannot ignore this instance of the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition through {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}.

rows.name: Internal Bleeding{@sup *}
entries: You suffer an internal hemorrhage and bruising. Your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is reduced by three times your character level.

rows.name: Wracked With Pain
entries: Your injury causes intense pain that limits your agility. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity saving throws.

rows.name: Concussion
entries: A brain contusion leaves you struggling to focus. You gain the {@condition Dazed|GrimHollowCG24} condition.

rows.name: Laceration
entries: lood wells unabaited from a deep injury. You gain the {@condition Bleeding|GrimHollowCG24} condition.

rows.name: Deep Wound{@sup *}
entries: You endure a blow that would kill many, but merely staggers you. When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you start with one failed {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB}.

rows.name: Battered{@sup *}
entries: Your muscles ache and you have had the wind knocked out of you. You gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level.

rows.name: Injured Wrist{@sup *}
entries: You have badly sprained your wrist or fractured a bone in your arm and are unable to use it effectively. You are unable to hold objects in one of your hands and you cannot take actions that require that arm.

rows.name: Damaged Eardrum
entries: A blow to your head impairs your hearing. You have the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition.

rows.name: System Shock
entries: You suffer a severe nervous shock. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} rolls.

rows.name: Injured Leg{@sup *}
entries: An injury to your leg or foot slows your movement. Reduce your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} by 10 feet, to a minimum of 5 feet. Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} can't be increased, and you can't take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action.

rows.name: Torn Muscle{@sup *}
entries: This injury reduces your combat prowess. When you deal damage with a Weapon Attack or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, roll {@dice 1d4;1d6;1d8;1d10;1d12|1d4} and subtract the result from the damage dealt. Each additional time you receive this wound, increase the size of the die rolled (to 1d6, 1d8, 1d10, and 1d12). After reaching the maximum die size listed, replace further Torn Muscle results with Injured Leg.

rows.name: Stymied Recovery
entries: Your injury slows your overall recovery. The total number of {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} you can spend during a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Alternative Rest System|GrimHollowCG24|Quick Rest} is equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).

rows.name: Severe Swelling
entries: Your swollen injuries give you an uncouth appearance. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) and Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) checks.

rows.name: Close Call{@sup *}
entries: You narrowly miss an otherwise dangerous blow. Instead of being reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you have 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} and have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

footnotes: Results with a {@sup *} next to them can be taken more than once

name: Griffon
rows: The talons of a griffon contain a unique collagen in them that when rendered creates a high quality adhesive. This glue is prized by leatherworkers and most can never find enough to meet their demand.
The pristine feathers of a griffon carry an almost supernatural aerodynamic quality to them. Fletchers and sharpshooters prize good condition griffon feathers for crafting high quality arrows.

A griffon can spot prey while flying miles overhead, and spot potential rivals from great distances. Their magical eyes have long been used as as charms and medicines by mountain-folk, but the utilisation of their eyes has been perfected by artificers capable of turning them into an eyes of the eagle mask.
