name: Ogre
rows: An ogre has a repugnant odor that seems to combine mouldy cheese, sour feet, and dank mud all at once. The fat around their rotund bellies seem to be the most potent source of this smell, and it takes a very stalwart alchemist to render this fat into tallow to make a vaguely magical candle.
The tough skin of an ogre is undoubtedly smelly and unpleasant. However, when tanned, it makes for a very durable leather, and many tanners would be glad to have them.
Brutish, rough, and very large, the hands of an ogre are meant for little more than wielding a club to smash those smaller than their owner.

name: Oinoloth

entries: Even a casual whiff of this ichor would inform you that it is not safe for humanoid consumption; it reeks of decomposition, decay, and death. Despite this, it does actually have many benefits that can restore a body's vitality instantly. However, as with everything involving a yugoloth, doing so comes with a price. {@b Requires {@item enchanted vial|HHHVI}.}

entries.name: Use:
entries: You may drink this potion as an action. If you do so, you instantly regain all hit points and you end one disease or condition from yourself from a choice of: {@condition blinded}, {@condition deafened}, {@condition paralyzed}, or {@condition poisoned}. You then gain 1 level of {@condition exhaustion}, and your hit point maximum is reduced by {@dice 2d6}. This reduction can be removed only by a {@spell wish} spell or by the {@spell greater restoration} spell being cast on you three times within the same hour. You die if your hit point maximum is reduced to 0.

Undulating and pulsating even after removal, these pustules contain concentrated doses of the oinoloth's plagues and it is common to see them prick these open as they spread their invisible death. A very steady hand needs to handle these, but afterwards, they can be thrown at one's enemies as disease bombs.

entries.name: Use:
entries: As an action, you may throw this pustule at a space within 20 feet of you, blighting the area within 10 feet of that spot similar to the bringer of plagues ability of the {@creature oinoloth|MTF} {@homebrew |(your DM has the stats)}.

rows: The claws of an oinoloth are fascinating structures, resembling syringes more than actual nails. These sharp, hollow tubes allow the oinoloth to deliver virulent payloads to their foes. With a little bit of adjustment, these claws can make a deadly pair of gloves that can bring both fast and slow deaths to one's opponent.

Despite their wide ranging forms, all yugoloths possess the same heart. It is the magic inherent in this heart that both ties them to their home plane of Gehenna and makes them materially unstable enough to teleport at a whim.

name: Oni
rows: The horns of an oni are incredibly hard and serve only to add to the oni's devilish appearance. They carry only trace amounts of the oni's innate magic, but they make good magical implements. Cannibalistic cults have often taken to using these horns as ceremonial flasks in their depraved rituals.
Despite being ogres, oni blood carries regenerative properties usually only seen in trolls. This powerful blood is one of the many potential catalysts used for brewing the ubiquitous healing potion.

The eyes of an oni appear to glow long after they have been pried from their foul sockets. If you are willing to use them, they can be crafted into goggles useful for the adventurer with no darkvision.
The hands of an oni are much like any other ogre's; tough and powerful. When taken to a blacksmith with a magical bent, they can be crafted into gauntlets of ogre power just like any other ogre's.
The heart of an oni is black as a moonless night and just as terrifying. Used as a conduit, an amulet crafted from this organ can grant the wearer some of the oni's magical properties.

name: Optional Rule: Crafting Skill Proficiency
rows: Usually an apprentice, assistant, or self-taught practitioner. Knows how to use the tools properly but has little skill with more difficult materials and no ability to make new ideas.

A craftsmen that serves their village or works in a specific role within their profession. Knows a few things very well, but most likely would not be able to understand the complexities of more exotic materials.

The highest level of skill that most ordinary people could hope to attain. Capable of establishing a good trade in a city or in service of a noble. Experienced in almost all aspects of their profession and can work with some confidence on rarer materials.

While hard work and dedication is always valuable, only a few people possess the inherent talent to push the limits of their craft farther than ordinary people. These talented individuals can be considered masters of their art; capable of not just reproduction, but innovation.

An absolute master of their art. Most likely was either an adventurer in their past, or learned their trade from a supernatural force, as this would be the only way for them to become accustomed to the legendary materials that they work with. Capable of crafting any item that falls under their profession.

entries: The gift of fertility that was granted to the orcs by their deity, {@deity Luthic|Orc|VGM}, also gave their other fluids full compatibility with other humanoids. As such, drinking the blood of an orc can temporarily grant other humanoids some of the legendary ferocity of the orcs.

entries: When you drink this vial of blood, you feel more aggressive for the next 10 minutes. During this time, you may spend your bonus action to move up to your speed toward a hostile creature you can see. After the 10 minutes have passed, you must succeed on a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw or suffer one point of {@condition exhaustion}.

entries: You may spend your action to eat this heart. If you do so, for the next hour you gain the ability to spend your action to allow up to three allies within 120 feet of you that can hear you to use their reactions to make one weapon attack each. This benefit cannot be taken by any character with elvish ancestry.

rows: Ritual scarring is common among blades of {@deity Ilneval|Orc|VGM}, both as a means of proving one's devotion and of proving one's strength. While many may find them horrifying to look at, there do exist collectors that appreciate the unique patterns that a blade of {@deity Ilneval|Orc|VGM} will make in their skin, paying a premium for experienced blades that have also had the most time and practice to expand their marks.

The fact that this eye seems to always glare at anyone with elvish ancestry should probably just be ignored.

name: Orc Nurtured One of Yurtrus

Luckily for most of us however, the disease cannot live long once exposed to the elements, and stops being a vector very soon after the death of its carrier. On the other hand, alchemists that have an interest in spreading maladies may make use of {@item enchanted vial|HHHVI|enchanted vials} to gather this ichor and brew it into a most insidious poison. {@b Requires {@item enchanted vial|HHHVI}.}

rows: Orcish war chiefs famously decorate their large tusks with all manner of jewelery and precious stones, presumably so you can be dazzled by their riches before they bite your head off. Many merchants will pay a good price for these tusks, if only for the sheer novelty of it.

name: Orcus
rows: As befitting of his monstrous love for reusing the bodies of the dead to bolster his own strength, the body of Orcus is actually made from the corpses of the strongest enemies he slew on the path to power. In particular are his massive bat-like wings that most believe he took from a defeated balor, ripping them off the living demon's body before it could immolate itself in death. As one of his first grabs for true dominance in the Abyss, these wings have been with Orcus for countless ages and have grown in strength with him, infused with all his corrupted majesty and influence.

name: Origin
rows: A letter of recommendation from the {@book Silver Company|BITCEH|2|Silver Company} is in your pocket; you are a mercenary looking for employment among the prestigious organisation in the valley.
You have nowhere to go home to. The conflict in the East has forced you from your home. Taking what little skills you have, perhaps {@book Kathkacha|BITCPI|4} will have a place for you.
Odd dreams plague your sleep, dreams of blood and violence. As if sleepwalking, you found yourself drawn to this place looking for answers, and perhaps a good night's rest at last.
{@book Kathkacha|BITCPI|4} is rich in {@item copper|phb}, wine, and opportunity. You know well of the wealth in this place and are determined to partake in its bounty.

Blood was spilled in {@book Kathkacha|BITCPI|4}, and it is blood you seek. Whether it was a family member or friend that died doesn't matter; you will find the perpetrators and bring them to justice, or death.
You are driven by a higher purpose. This land is ailing and you will bring justice, hope, and life... or plunge it into darkness as you see fit.

name: Orthon

entries: Aside from being incredibly intimidating, the tusks of an orthon serve a practical purpose in their tracking duties. The orthon is capable of attuning their tusks to their quarry, causing them to vibrate like dowsing rods as they approach. While it is impossible to replicate this ability once the tusks have been removed from their skull, they can be used in a one-time ritual in order to track a particularly elusive target.

entries.name: Use:
entries: If you grind an orthon tusk into a fine powder, you may burn it along with a possession or piece of a creature you wish to track in order to designate them as your quarry for the next 24 hours. Once a creature has been designated as your quarry, you become constantly aware of their distance and direction from you so long as they are on the same plane of existence as you. Any magical effect that disrupts divination magic will also disrupt this effect.

rows: Orthons are some of the most prodigious trackers that have ever graced the multiverse. This is in no small part due to their extraordinary senses. In particular, their eyes are capable of seeing across multiple spectrums and through magical obfuscation. By transforming these eyes into lenses, the wearer can also gain the honed sight and tracking ability of the orthon.

Despite their massive size, the orthon is notable for their ability to sneak up on their targets with ease. This is due to their unique skin that is capable of true invisibility greater than the simple camouflage or displacement of lesser creatures. As such, these hides are highly prized as a leather base for making magical equipment for those that are stealthily inclined.

name: Otyugh
rows: As disgusting as the idea may sound, otyugh bile, capable of digesting just about anything, actually makes for a very good medicine for indigestion. A common remedy prescibred by a village's medicine woman is a dose of diluted otyugh bile mixed with a spoonful of honey (mostly to mask the taste).

entries: An otyugh's saliva is not actually poisonous, but it is loaded with so much bacteria and disease that it may as well be.

entries.name: Use:
entries: This saliva can be used to coat up to 5 pieces of slashing or piercing ammunition or one slashing or piercing weapon. Applying the poison takes 1 minute. For the next minute, any creature successfully hit must make a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw against disease or become {@condition poisoned} until the disease is cured. For every 24 hours that elapse, the target must repeat the saving throw, reducing its hit point maximum by {@dice 1d10} on a failure. The disease is cured on a success. The target dies if the disease reduces its hit point maximum to 0. This reduction to the target's hit point maximum lasts until the disease is cured.

rows: The tentacles of an otyugh are tipped with incredibly sharp needles that both pierce its foes and allow it to drag them around. Underdark slavers are often found with whips made from these tentacles, designed to capture their prey alive.

An odd cluster of nerves at the section in which the otyugh's tentacles meet its back. The composition is incompatible with the more complicated brain structure of a humanoid, but it actually does work on simpler life forms like beasts.

name: Owlbear
rows: The feathers of an owlbear are noticeably soft and downy, in contrast to their more ferocious appearance. While these feathers make for poor fletching, they actually do make fantastic bedding material, and owlbear feather stuffed pillows are the hallmark of any well equipped bedroom.

The liver of an owlbear is a potent medicinal ingredient, used to treat everything from indigestion, to kidney stones, to mudgut. Unfortunately, this very property has led to owlbears facing overhunting in some regions.

Ask anybody who has once tried to hide from an owlbear, and they will tell you of how futile that effort is. Their keen eyesight, hearing, and sense of smell, combined with their eerie owl-like tendency to twist their heads behind them while tracking, make them a terrifying predator to elude. A scarf made from a part of their carcass also grants some level of these senses, giving its owner some level of heightened awareness.

name: Pages of Anguish
intro: {@i Pages of Anguish}, the title of which was chosen by an edgy tiefling named Anguish. He truly earned that name in the end, after hours with Maddgoth. The pages are water-stained, suggesting Maddgoth froze him in ice.

name: Party Shenanigans Table - 1 Hour
rows: You gorge yourself in the different pastries presented before you. Regain {@dice 2d6 + 2} hit points and gain {@dice 1d6} special treats, which last for 8 hours. A creature can use a bonus action to eat one of those treats, gaining {@dice 1d4 + 4} temporary hit points. For the next 12 hours, your speed is halved.

You bust a move on the dance floor, grooving to your heart's delight. Regain a number of hit points equal to {@dice 2d8} + your Charisma modifier. Make a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) check. On a result of 18 or higher, you are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Kinetic Jaunt|SCC} spell for the next {@dice 1d8} hours.

You engage in a lyrical battle against a blue-haired gnome of funky beats. Make a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) and a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check. On a result of 15 or higher for one of the two checks, the battle ends in a draw. Gain 1 level of {@condition Exhaustion}, which can be removed on a short rest. On a result of 15 or higher for both checks, you barely emerge victorious in the contest of syllables. Gain proficiency in the {@skill Performance} skill. If you are already proficient in this skill, you gain advantage on Charisma checks for the next {@dice 1d8} hours. On a result of 14 or lower for both checks, the funky gnome wipes the floor with your tumbling butt. You become {@condition Stunned} for the next {@dice 1d4} hours.

An elf clad in black leather and sporting a wild hairstyle challenges you to an epic duel in their children's card game. Make an Intelligence or Wisdom check. You can add your proficiency bonus to this roll if you have proficiency with the Playing Card Set. On a result of 18 or higher, you miraculously win the match, impressing the eccentric elf and attaining his favor. Gain a single {@i Monster Card}, choosing from Fey, Demon, Shadow, Undead or Warrior. Each of those cards can be used to cast the {@spell Summon Fey|TCE}, {@spell Summon Lesser Demons|XGE}, {@spell Summon Shadowspawn|TCE}, {@spell Summon Undead|TCE}, or Summon Warrior Spirit (UA) spells, respectively. You must use your own spell slots in order to cast one of these spells through their respective card. When you do so, they don't require material components.

A strange hooded sorcerer throws a mysterious dust in your face. You fall into a magical slumber and take a {@b very good} nap. Gain the effects of a long rest. If magic can't put you to sleep, you enter a sneezing fit instead. Gain a penalty of -2 to any ability checks or saving throws you make in the next {@dice 1d4} hours.

You eat the wrong cockatrice sandwich, and end up spending a not-so-great time on the privy chamber. You take {@damage 2d6} psychic damage, and become {@condition Poisoned} for the next {@dice 2d4} hours.

You meet a talking magical unicorn who starts lecturing you on the power of friendship. Make a Constitution saving throw, a Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check or an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check. On a result of 15 or higher, you manage to survive the encounter with your mind intact. Gain 1 level of {@condition Exhaustion}. For the next 24 hours, you have a +1 bonus to your Intelligence modifier. If the result is 14 or lower, your eyes are opened to the unrivaled magic one can find within their bonds. For the next {@dice 1d4} weeks, you may cast the {@spell Friends|PHB} cantrip at will without material components, but have disadvantage on saving throws to resist being {@condition Charmed}.

You play a few matches of life-sized chess with the local party-goers. Make four Intelligence or Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) checks. You can add your proficiency bonus to the rolls if you have proficiency with the Dragonchess Set. On a result of 15 or higher for a check, your wits prove superior to your opponent's for that match. If you win at least three of your matches, a member of the audience decides to reward you for the good games. Gain one common wondrous item of the DM's choosing. If you win all four of your matches, gain proficiency with the Dragonchess set if you didn't already have it. If you lose three or more of your matches, the taste of utter defeat crushes your self-confidence. For the next {@dice 1d4} days, you have disadvantage on any Intelligence or Charisma checks and saving throws you make.

name: Party Shenanigans Table - 1 Minute
rows: You quickly grab what you can from the food servings. Gain {@dice 1d4} special treats, which last for 8 hours. A creature can use a bonus action to eat one of those treats, gaining {@dice 1d4 + 4} temporary hit points.

You try to bust a move on the dance floor, but end up slipping on a magical banana. Take {@damage 1d8} psychic damage, and gain a {@i Banana Peel}. It can be destroyed by a creature as a bonus action, granting them 2 sorcery points. These points are added to any sorcery points they have from another source, but can be used only on Metamagic.

A drunken dancer hurriedly approaches, and then promptly pukes all of their lunch over you. Take {@damage 1d6} acid damage and {@damage 1d6} psychic damage. Roll a {@dice d20}. If the number rolled is a 3 or lower, you become infected with the Sewer Plague.

You bump into the most gorgeous creature you've ever seen in your life, only for it to then escape your sight among the crowd. Gain a penalty of -2 to any Charisma ability checks or saving throws you make in the next 8 hours. {@b Special:} If you get this outcome again in less than 30 days, you can roll a {@dice d6}. If the number rolled is a 5 or 6, you meet with the original creature you stumbled upon. Gain a bonus of +4 to any Charisma ability checks or saving throws you make in the next 8 hours.

A couple of newlywed beholders ask you to take their painting. Make a Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) or a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) check. On a result of 15 or higher, they greatly enjoy your depiction. Gain a tip of 50 gold. {@b Special:} On a result of 25 or higher, they perceive your work as a magnum opus, wanting to buy it from you instead. Make a Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check. On a result of 15 or lower, you sell the painting cheap for 300 gold. On a result of 16 or higher, you manage to bargain your way into a better deal, selling your work for 1000 gold.

A halfling bard with pink clothes tries to flirt his way into your life, but then accidentally turns himself into a pickle. Funniest thing you've ever seen. For the next {@dice 1d4} hours, you are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Tasha's Hideous Laughter|PHB} spell.

You are suddenly recruited as the substitute priest for a wedding taking place in the ballroom. The universe decides that you are very good at it. For the next week, you gain access to the {@spell Ceremony|XGE} spell. It is considered a spell from your class list, and you always have it prepared; but it doesn't count against the number of spells you prepare each day. Once per long rest, you may cast it without expending a spell slot. {@b Special:} Whenever you get this outcome a total of 3 times, roll a {@dice d6}. If the number rolled is a 5 or 6, your priestdom is officially recognized by reality. You may cast the {@spell Ceremony|XGE} spell at will, without expending a spell slot.

A hurried autognome appears before you, seemingly trying to relay something urgent. Roll a {@dice d4}. On a 1 or 2, you are unable to understand any of it, prompting them to forcefully implant a chip into your head. Take {@damage 1d6} piercing damage. For the next 8 hours, you are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Comprehend Languages|PHB} spell. On a 3 or 4, you discover that they wanted to tell you a new joke they just made up. It is a pun about locks. Take {@damage 1d6} psychic damage. For the next 8 hours, you have advantage on saving throws to resist being {@condition Charmed} or {@condition Frightened}.

name: Party Shenanigans Table - 8 Hours
rows: You take part in a lavish banquet of glorious proportions. You are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Heroes' Feast|PHB} spell. For the next 24 hours, your speed is halved.

You perform a series of group dances with choreographic perfection, even though you've never met any of your partners before. Gain 2 levels of {@condition Exhaustion}. For the next 24 hours, you are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Kinetic Jaunt|SCC} spell.

You spend a relaxing time on the hot tub with a bunch of fellow partygoers. The magical healing waters wash your worries away, leaving your body perhaps a little {@i too relaxed}. You are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Heal|PHB} spell. For the next 24 hours, you have resistance to acid, cold, fire, and poison damage, but gain a penalty of -4 to your Strength modifier and disadvantage on any Strength checks or Constitution saving throws you make.

You participate on a cart race against a gnome artificer of red and blue clothes, along with many other curious competitors. Make a Dexterity check. You can add your proficiency bonus to this roll if you have proficiency with land vehicles. On a result of 16 or higher, you place in the top 5. Gain a +2 bonus to ability checks and saving throws for the next {@dice 2d6} hours. On a result of 20 or higher, you place 1st in the race. Gain proficiency with land vehicles if you didn't already have it, and a +4 bonus to ability checks and saving throws for the next {@dice 2d8} hours.

You are taken by a hefty aristocrat through a {@i 'Socializing 101'} emergency crash course. For the next 24 hours, you learn the {@spell Charm Monster|XGE} spell and may cast the {@spell Friends|PHB} cantrip at will. {@b Special:} If you get this outcome a total of 3 times, you gain proficiency in the {@skill Persuasion} skill. If you are already proficient in this skill, you gain expertise with it instead (does not stack with similar features).

You are enraptured by a changeling mime, whose loony antics leave you dumbfounded out of your mind. Make a Wisdom check. On a result of 15 or higher, you are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Confusion|PHB} spell for the next {@dice 1d4} hours. On a result of 14 or lower, you are treated as being under the effects of the {@spell Mental Prison|XGE} spell for the next {@dice 2d6} hours.

name: Party Shenanigans Table - 10 Minutes
rows: You take your time to taste what the platters have to offer. Regain a number of hit points equal to {@dice 2d4} + your proficiency bonus. If you currently have no hit points to be recovered, gain a number of temporary hit points equal to four times your character level instead.

You engage in merrymaking with a friendly group of astral space hamsters, spending their interdimensional vacation in this party. Their bright energy permeates over to you, healing a bit of your soul in the process. Regain all of your expended spell slots. If you have no spell slots to be regained, then for the next 24 hours you may cast one spell of 5th level of lower once without expending a spell slot. If you don't possess a spellcasting ability, then for the next 24 hours you gain access to one use of the Action Surge feature from the Fighter class.
An interplanar trader offers you a small white pill, said to unlock the secrets of time-saving. Lose 50 gold. The pill can be consumed as a bonus action, granting you the effects of a short rest.

You get swept up in a makeshift slapping contest to determine the greatest gentlefolk of all. Make a Constitution saving throw ({@dc 14}). You take {@damage 3d4} psychic damage and {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Make a Strength ({@skill Athletics}), Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) or Charisma ({@skill Performance}) check. On a result of 18 or higher, you emerge victorious as the greatest slapper of this era. Your unarmed strikes can now be made in the form of slaps, dealing additional psychic damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

You engage in a lengthy discussion with a grey-haired human artificer, arguing about which beverage has the best flavor. After proving your taste buds to be superior, he whips out a strange firearm and warps you through a green portal. You arrive at a random location within a plane of the DM's choosing. If you are still in that plane after 24 hours, the human appears before you through a similar portal, and teleports you back to your original plane.

You are confused for an important political figure of a different plane's monarchy, leading a disguised royal agent to make an attempt at your life. Roll a {@dice d20}. On a 10 or higher, you manage to avoid their wrath by a hair's breadth, getting scarred from the experience. Gain {@dice 1d4} levels of {@condition Exhaustion}. On a 9 or lower, the agent manages to put a curse on you before getting suddenly consumed by a drunken owlbear sailor. For the next 24 hours, you cannot regain hit points in any way, or acquire any temporary hit points.

name: Party Shenanigans Table - 24 Hours
rows: You are met by a pompous elf wearing a white sleeveless coat with shoulder pads and a raised collar. He announces himself to be the greatest gamer of all, and challenges you for the title of King of Cards. Make an Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma check. You can add your proficiency bonus to this roll if you have proficiency with the Playing Card Set. On a result of 22 or higher, you emerge victorious against the egocentric elf, taking his greatest treasure as your reward. You gain the {@i Azure-Eyes Silver Dragon} card. This item can be used to cast the {@spell Summon Draconic Spirit|FTD} spell without material components. You must use your own spell slots in order to cast it through the card in this way. When you do so, the summoned spirit benefits from all three family types. {@b Special:} This outcome can only happen if you've gained a {@i Monster Card} item from a previous roll of the Party Shenanigans table. If this prerequisite is not met, you go through four outings of the fourth outcome from the 1-hour section instead.

After chatting the hours away in the counter, you are offered an extravagant cocktail from the local warforged bartender, which unbeknownst to you is spiked with wild magic. Roll a {@dice d6}. Choose a spell of a level equal to the number rolled, from any spell list. It is now considered a spell from your class list, and you always have it prepared; but it doesn't count against the number of spells you prepare each day. If you don't possess a spellcasting ability, then you may cast it by expending a number of hit dice equal to the spell's level. When casting the spell in this way, it doesn't require material components.

You end up being pulled along into a secret heist of one of the many vaults in this seemingly infinite venue. Roll a {@dice d20}. On a 9 or lower, gain one magic item with a rarity of Uncommon or lower. On a 10 or higher, gain one magic item with a rarity of Rare or lower. On a 16 or higher, gain one magic item with a rarity of Very Rare or lower. Which item is given to your character, as well as what rarity that variant of it possesses, can either be determined by the DM or left entirely to your choice (with their approval). The effects of that decision on the campaign are left to the DM's discretion. {@b Special:} Whenever this outcome is experienced by player characters a total of 3 times, the DM must roll a {@dice d6}. On a 4 or lower, one of the party's chief stewards takes knowledge of this repeated robbery, seeking monetary transference in return. You and all of your party members lose every gold (or platinum) piece you are currently in possession of.

You meet and spend the day with an elder dragon archpriest, who offers you the redefining of your own soul. You may change your current subclass if you wish so. This can only be done once per character. The effects of this decision on the campaign are left to the DM's discretion.

You are reunited with a being you once met in this never-ending party. Roll a {@dice d6}. On a 3 or lower, the creature is hostile towards you. They will attempt to engage in combat with you and your companions, and may follow your trail even after you leave your patron's realm (if they are capable of doing so). The creature's stats and abilities, as well as how their battle with you affects your companions' time in the party, are left to the DM's discretion. If the number rolled is a 4 or higher, you and the creature develop a lasting friendship. They will attempt to accompany you after leaving your patron's realm, doing their best to help on your group's quests. At the DM's discretion, they can become a reoccurring or permanent ally NPC.

After experiencing the joys of Happy Hour, you decide to take part in a grand drinking contest; only to find out you can't hold your liquor nearly as well as you thought. For the next {@dice 2d4} days, you have disadvantage on any attack rolls, ability checks or saving throws you make.

While dilly-dallying your way through the multifarious chambers of this realm, you end up taking a peek into a room you shouldn't have. The DM must choose one specific type of creature, object, scenery and event. For the next year, you become {@condition Frightened} whenever you catch sight of the chosen subjects. The condition lasts for as long as one of the subjects remains in your sight. {@b Example:} The chosen subjects can be a lute, a bathroom, and a fey creature. Your character will instantly become {@condition Frightened} when seeing any of those things.

You gain the one-in-a-million chance to meet the very entity who makes all of this possible: {@b your patron, the Party Lord}. You can ask up to five questions, as per the {@spell Commune|PHB} spell. The answers are left to the DM's discretion. Make a Charisma check. You may cast any number of spells or apply any number of effects on yourself before making the roll. On a result of 25 or higher, your patron's time with you proves entertaining enough for them to dole out a gift of appreciation. You gain one use of the {@spell Wish|PHB} spell. This can only be done once per year. {@b Special:} This outcome can only happen if your character is the holder of this subclass. If this prerequisite is not met, you go through two different outcomes from the 8-hour section instead. You must make a separate roll to determine each one.

name: Patron Promises
rows: Kill an ancient silver dragon and eat its heart.
Convert the high priest of Emerset to betray his deity and serve you.
Visit the realm of Nazirun and burn the sacred Book of Ascension.
Obey every demand and serve you without question for the next 10 years.
Get the Queen of Rendeburg to pose for a portrait that I paint.
Make 1,000 people all sing your name during the Winter Festival.
Free the Dream Stalker from the depths of the Feywitch Prison.
Build a temple to you in the capital city.
Find a way to summon you into this world.
Let you take possession of my body during the night of the full moon.
Find and complete the secret puzzle box of Lamenchard's Lament.
Kill the archon of the cult that opposes you.
Recruit 1,000 new people into your service.
Create a new festival in your name that is celebrated in all Seven Kingdoms of Thendrae.

name: Patron Sacrifices
rows: The life of my precious pet.
This last copy of a rare, precious book.
The beating heart of a unicorn.
My ability to feel strong emotions.

name: Pegasus
rows: Pure white, majestic, and incredibly durable, the hair of a pegasus is coveted as a crafting material. Everything from rope, to instruments, to bows have been strung with pegasus hair, and always sold at a premium.

The hooves of a pegasus can be ground down and rendered into a glue like a regular horse's. This glue however has a certain glittery imperfection in it that is actually enjoyed by noble ladies fond of extravagance. This glue has been converted into various cosmetics or as a final flourish to an already decadent gown.
Pegasus blood is a brilliant sheen of silver with a rainbow reflection on its surface. Well known as a medicine, it is often sold to middle-aged men as a fertility potion.

The glorious wings of a pegasus, resembling two nimbuses on a corporeal body. It takes a very steady hand to remove these fragile appendages without ruining them, but if done correctly, they can be used as ingredients in the ever useful potion of flying.

name: Per Rest Abilities
outro: {@b Maximum abilities to keep track of: 3}

name: Perils of the Deeps; Random Shipwreck Encounters
caption: Random Shipwreck Encounters
rows: A coven of {@creature sea hag|FleeMortals|sea hags} and their pet {@creature warp shark|Arcadia27} lair in this rotting galleon, now decorated with the bones of drowned sailors.
This merchant ship contains potions or magic items, and is now home to {@creature arcane remora|Arcadia27|arcane remoras} who are slowly draining the cargo of its magic.

This underwater ship was built atop a living dragon turtle, and is now a dragon turtle skeleton infested with {@creature swarm of zombie worms|Arcadia27|swarms of zombie worms}. If the characters are 12th level or higher, the {@creature dragon turtle skeleton|Arcadia27|dragon turtle} is an Undead creature with immunity to poison damage, exhaustion, and the poisoned condition, and whose Steam Breath attack deals necrotic damage instead of fire damage.

A young {@creature hound shark|Arcadia27} lives in the wreckage of this caravel. The shark is friendly to any creature who feeds them meat and succeeds on a DC 12 Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) check, made with advantage if the meat is fresh fish.
This ancient frigate appears to be empty of life, but an {@creature aranoth|Arcadia27} lurks nearby, hungry for new memories.

This {@item rainbow scale boat|Arcadia27} bobs on the surface of the water, frozen in a block of unmelting ice. The ice can be melted by dealing 200 fire damage to it within 1 minute, or by using the destroy water option of the {@spell create or destroy water} spell cast at 3rd level, or cast three times at 1st level.

Every inch of this sloop is covered with a layer of sparkling frost. The water within 30 feet of it is unusually clear and bone-chillingly cold, thanks to the the {@creature rime elemental|Arcadia27|rime elementals} (use the {@creature ice mephit} stat block, but with a swimming speed of 30 feet and the ability to breathe underwater) stranded inside the ship. Each creature who starts their turn in this water or within the ship, or who enters either area for the first time on a turn, takes 3 ({@damage 1d6}) cold damage.

Carved fins decorate the hull and rails of this once-beautiful schooner, whose prow still bears the name {@i Feasting Fin}, but which has been split into two jagged halves by some colossal force. The captain's quarters contain waterlogged scrolls, as well as three {@item spell scroll||spell scrolls} of {@spell water breathing} in a sealed case and six bottles of fine rum.

This barnacle-encrusted trireme is swarming with similarly barnacle-encrusted skeletons. The ship's {@creature shipwreck skeleton|Arcadia27|former crew} each use the {@creature skeleton} stat block but have a swimming speed of 30 feet and the following action option: {@b {@i Barnacle-Encrusted Oar.}} {@atk mw} {@hit 2} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d10}) bludgeoning damage and 3 ({@damage 1d6}) piercing damage.
A {@creature giant spider crab|Arcadia27} and a {@creature giant sea horse} are locked in combat atop this sunken longboat.
This {@item sharkboat|Arcadia27} is in pristine condition, but is trapped under a massive {@creature megalodon|Arcadia27} carcass.

The water is fetid and murky around this strange vessel, whose front half is buried beneath the ocean floor at a steep angle. Originally a planar craft that suffered a malfunction when transiting between planes, its presence has spawned an {@creature eldritch anemone|Arcadia27} dwelling in the shadow of the listing hull.

name: Permanent Wound

chapter.name: The GM's Guide to Dark Fantasy

rows: {@b {@i Fatal Wound.}} Through an unrecoverable injury you have been fatally wounded. You are now dead.
{@b {@i Lost Arm*.}} You have suffered a serious injury to your arm or have lost it entirely. You are unable to hold objects in one of your arms and you cannot take actions that require two arms.

{@b {@i Lost Leg*.}} You have suffered a serious injury to your leg or have lost it entirely. Your speed on foot is halved and you cannot take the dash action. If you receive this result again your speed on foot becomes 0.

{@b {@i Lost Eye*.}} You have lost the use of a good eye. You have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) and Intelligence (Investigation) checks that rely on sight. If you receive this result again, you gain the {@condition blinded} condition.

{@b {@i Scarred Lungs.}} Undertaking vigorous activities causes you to break out in a coughing fit. If you take an action, you cannot take a bonus action until your next turn. If you take a bonus action you cannot take an action until your next turn.

{@b {@i Hideous Scar.}} You have been horribly and visibly scared. You have disadvantage on Charisma (Performance) and Charisma (Persuasion) checks. Additionally, indifferent NPC's may prefer not to converse with you.
footnotes: Results with a * next to them can be taken more than once.

name: Permanent Wounds
caption: Permanent Wounds

rows.name: Fatal Wound
entries: Through an unrecoverable injury, you have been fatally wounded. You are now dead but can be brought back through normal methods.

rows.name: Lost Arm{@sup *}
entries: A serious injury disables or destroys one of your arms. You can't use that arm to wield a weapon or a shield, or to perform the Somatic component of a spell.

rows.name: Lost Leg{@sup *}
entries: A serious injury disables or destroys one of your legs. Reduce your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} by 15 feet, to a minimum of 5 feet. Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} can't be increased, and you can't take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action. If you receive this result again your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by another 15 feet (to a minimum of 5 feet).

rows.name: Lost Eye{@sup *}
entries: You lose an eye. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) and Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks that rely on sight. If you receive this result again, you gain the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition.

rows.name: Dizzy Spells
entries: Undertaking vigorous activities leaves you addled. On odd numbered combat rounds, if you take an action, you cannot take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} until the start of your next turn. If you take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you cannot take an action until the start of your next turn.

rows.name: Scarred Lungs
entries: Your injury makes it a struggle to breathe. Your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} maximum is permanently reduced by 1 for each of your character levels. Additionally, when you gain a level, your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is reduced by 1.

rows.name: Hideous Scar
entries: You are horribly and visibly scarred. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) and Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) checks and {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) checks.

rows.name: Adrenaline Rush
entries: Your injuries make you vulnerable to further damage, but your survival instincts are heightened in moments of danger. If you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, any {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} against you becomes a normal hit. If you are not {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, attack rolls made against you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

rows.name: Hesitant
entries: Your psyche has been scarred more than your body. The first time after a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} that you have to make a saving throw to avoid the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, you are {@condition Frightened|XPHB} even if you succeed on the saving throw.

rows.name: Old Pain
entries: This lingering injury causes you intense pain when it flares up. When you roll a natural 1 on any {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn.

footnotes: Results with a {@sup *} next to them can be taken more than once

name: Personal Assistant Plot Hooks
intro: Roll on or choose from the Personal Assistant Plot Hooks table to determine how the personal assistant is introduced to the party.
rows: The Ruler sends their personal assistant to follow the party to make sure the characters don't find the zombie army hiding in the catacombs. But what is that groaning sound, and why do folks keep disappearing?

The personal assistant desperately needs someone to convince the Ruler that they're dead so they can escape this realm. They used their 10-minute lunch break just to ask the party for help. How will they fake their death?
The personal assistant needs to organize a birthday party for the Ruler, but they don't know where to start. Will someone help them with a very special day?

The Ruler wants—nay—{@i needs} a very specific dish made from some very rare ingredients from a very dangerous location. A mere personal assistant can't handle this themselves, and they desperately need kind adventurers' aid. Who will step up to the plate?

The neighboring realm's Ruler has a crown that makes them look glorious ... so glorious that the Ruler of this realm has grown quite envious. They want the personal assistant to steal the crown so they can have it for themselves. The personal assistant hires the characters to help with the heist, and really hopes they have a good plan!

The personal assistant wants to unionize, but they're terrified of the Ruler. (Rightfully so.) The personal assistant asks for the characters' help organizing their coworkers, but soon after the Ruler asks the party to report any whispers of unions to them. Who will the party side with, and if it's the Ruler, how will this betrayal play out?

name: Personal Missions Table
rows: {@background Cult Initiate|SGttEH}, {@background Inquisitor|SGttEH}, {@background Marked for Death|SGttEH}
{@background Amnesiac|SGttEH}, {@background Cult Initiate|SGttEH}, {@background Marked for Death|SGttEH}
{@background Marked for Death|SGttEH}, {@background Amnesiac|SGttEH}, {@background Worthless Husk|SGttEH}

name: Peryton
rows: The large horns of a peryton are considered quite striking for their strange black lustre. Whether used as a decoration or ground up for medicine, they tend to fetch a decent price. There is also a rumour that a set of dice crafted from the horns of a peryton are particularly easy to use in cheating. This is unsubstantiated, however.
Perytons have a strange fixation with hearts. While theories abound of their origin in regards to the eating of hearts, it can be confirmed that a peryton's own heart does carry dark magical energy.
The black wings of a peryton are incredibly powerful and agile. When removed properly, they can be used as ingredients in the ever useful potion of flying.

name: Phoenix
rows: Regardless of their end form, the creation of an elder elemental is an event so momentous that it breaks reality itself for a brief moment. This leads to the creation of an entropy shard: a piece of reality inside every elder elemental that they retain from their multiverse-shattering births. Resembling a pure white piece of glass about the size of a hand, this shard holds pure, primal power and should only be handled by the most experienced harvesters and crafters.

As a phoenix reaches the end of its current life, it bursts into a fiery nova that consumes its body entirely, allowing it to be reborn inside the cinder-egg and restore its strength. Although the cinder-egg tends to constitute whatever is left of the phoenix's material form, you may be able to gather some remnant ashes that contain traces of the phoenix's legendary regenerative power. When a skilled blacksmith adds these ashes to their furnace, they are able to create a legendary suit of armor that grants the user the same eternal presence as the phoenix itself.

name: Piece of Culture
rows: A book written by Ikarian Devos, a sage of the {@book Aegan Empire|BITCPI|7|The Aegan Empire}.
A parchment drawing of an eastern soldier.
A charcoal sketch of the {@book Brass Palace|BITCPI|5|The Brass Palace}.
An {@item ululu|BloodInTheCompany}, a small percussive Helviti instrument. Doubles as a {@item club|phb}.
A short story about {@book Flambard Hawk|BITCEH|5|Flambard Hawk} by Galos Gafinger. Almost certainly non-factual.
A bronze locket containing a painting of the current King of the {@book Aegan Empire|BITCPI|7|The Aegan Empire}, King Hekari.

name: Piercer
rows: The horrible smelling musk of a piercer, while unpleasant, is not debilitatingly so. Ironically enough, this musk can undergo an alchemical process to be transformed into a rather expensive perfume. Of course, those marketing it are usually reluctant to tell their buyers what it is made out of.

The slug-like piercer is covered in a rock-like shell that gives it the appearance of a stalactite or stalagmite. This hard shell has been repurposed into many things in Underdark societies including bowls, furniture, and various tools.

name: Piercing Injury
rows: {@b Lose an Eye.} You have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight and ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB|Attack Rolls}. This can be restored with the {@spell Regenerate|XPHB} spell.

{@b Blood Loss.} You lose maximum {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your level at the end of your turns. Casting {@spell Heal Minor Wounds|WoBrCa} or making a DC 15 Wisdom (medicine) check, using a charge of the healer's kit, will stop the blood loss. Making a DC 15 Wisdom (medicine) check, without the use of a healer's kit will stop the bleeding for an hour.

{@b Broken Arm or Hand.} You can no longer hold anything with two hands, and you can hold only a single object at a time. All {@variantrule Ability Check|XPHB|Ability Checks} and {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB|Attack Rolls} made with it have disadvantage. This can be healed with the {@spell Mend Flesh and Bones|WoBrCa} spell. After 2 weeks it becomes a Major Cut scar.

{@b Broken Foot or Leg.} Your speed on foot is halved, and you must use a cane or crutch to move. You fall {@condition Prone|XPHB} after ending your movement when using the {@action Dash|XPHB} action. All {@variantrule Ability Check|XPHB|Ability Checks} and {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB|Attack Rolls} made with it have disadvantage. This can be healed with the {@spell Mend Flesh and Bones|WoBrCa} spell. After 2 weeks it becomes a Major Cut scar.

{@b Internal Injury.} You have to move much more carefully when you take your actions. If you take both an action and bonus action on your turn or take a reaction, you lose {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your level. This health loss cannot be reduced. The internal injury can be healed with the {@spell Mend Flesh and Bones|WoBrCa} spell. After 2 weeks the Internal Injury will naturally heal.
{@b Broken Rib.} This has the same effect as the Internal Injury, but the damage you take is equal to half your level (round up).

{@b Limp.} Your speed on foot is reduced by 5 feet. All {@variantrule Ability Check|XPHB|Ability Checks} and {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB|Attack Rolls} made with the foot have disadvantage. You must make a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw after ending your movement when you take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action. If you fail the save, you fall {@condition Prone|XPHB}. This can be healed with the {@spell Heal Minor Wounds|WoBrCa} spell.

{@b Major Cuts.} You get a bad cut in a place very visible to others. You have disadvantage on Charisma (Persuasion) and advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks. This can be removed with the {@spell Heal Minor Wounds|WoBrCa} spell. After 1 week the Major Cuts will naturally heal and turn into a scar, which has no adverse effects.
{@b Cuts.} The cuts don't have any adverse effect. This can be removed with the {@spell Heal Minor Wounds|WoBrCa} spell. After 1 week the cuts will naturally heal.

name: Pit Fiend
rows: A pit fiend's blood hisses, boils, and bubbles long after it has been removed from its body, as if the fiend's wrath at its enemies continues even after its death. Cooling this blood and separating out the plasma can create a potion that grants the drinker the same unholy vitality of its original owner.

entries: A pit fiend's venom is one of the most insidious of all the fiends. Besides the horrible pain they inflict on their victim, its corrupting influence even blocks out magical assistance, keeping wounds open and bleeding even in the face of divine help.

entries.name: Use:
entries: Can be used to up to 15 pieces of slashing or piercing ammunition or 1 slashing or piercing weapon for 1 hour. Applying takes 1 minute. Any creature successfully hit must succeed on a {@dc 21} Constitution saving throw or become {@condition poisoned}. While {@condition poisoned} in this way, the target can't regain hit points, and it takes {@damage 6d6} poison damage at the start of each of its turns. The {@condition poisoned} target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

rows: For many hapless adventurers, a pit fiend's claw is the last thing they ever see. If reforged into a weapon however, it may be the last thing your enemies ever see.

The mighty wings of the pit fiend are among the finest of all the devils. Massive canvases capable of cloaking even the pit fiend's massive frame, they make for the ideal material to craft a pair of infernal wings.

A pit fiend is one of the most terrifying beings in the entire multiverse. As such, it stands to reason that anybody that is wearing the severed head of a pit fiend as a helmet should be considered even more terrifying. Indeed, if one can detach this fiend's head from its body, haul it back to an artificer for reforging, and then wear it proudly despite knowing the retribution that they may face from those that pit fiend considered its ally; that person rightfully deserves to be feared by the lessers around them.

entries: The ubiquitous dust dropped by the wings of pixies. Incredibly magical, yet volatile, it is virtually impossible for a non-pixie to determine what will happen when sprinkled on a creature.

entries.name: Use:
entries: As an action, you may sprinkle some pixie dust on a creature next to you. If sprinkled on an unwilling creature, they may resist any resulting effect by succeeding on a {@dc 12} Wisdom saving throw. If sprinkled on a willing creature, or an unwilling creature that failed their saving throw, roll {@dice 1d10} and consult the pixie dust effect table for the result. A small pouch of pixie dust has enough dust in it for 3 uses.

name: Plagues and Curses
caption: Plagues and Curses
rows: {@b The Hunger.} Humanoids feel an intense hunger and a drive toward cannibalism. Any who give into this impulse slowly transform into {@creature ghoul|MM|ghouls}.

{@b Restless Dead.} Any humanoid who dies in the region rises as a specific type of undead creature after one minute. {@creature zombie|MM|Zombies} and {@creature shadow|MM|shadows} are commonly associated with this curse.
{@b Hysteria.} Those who sleep in the affected region develop {@disease cackle fever}, as described in the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}. Afflicted individuals can spread the disease as normal.

{@b Broken Mirrors.} Reflections in mirrors mock the people who cast them, and if anyone gets too close, the reflection may reach out of the mirror and strike at them. These spirits have the statistics of {@creature ghost|MM|ghosts} or {@creature shadow|MM|shadows}, except that they have a speed of 0 and are banished if the mirror is shattered. If mirror ghosts use the Possession trait, the ghost is destroyed as soon as it leaves its host (or is driven from it).

name: Plain Gnoll Lair Details
intro: An area controlled by gutter gnolls might display the following:
rows: A ramshackle totem topped with a hyena skull daubed with symbols
Most of the grass here has been ripped up, and what little remains is trampled flat; the site of a recent kill
A looted and smashed wagon, reeking of hyena and smeared with musk
A leveled circle with inedible detritus scattered about where gnolls have spent an evening
An overturned cart on a rise with a good view of the road, acting as a windbreak for those watching for travelers
Quiet but constant chattering and occasional, sudden whoops from unseen hyenas
The tracks of a lone traveler lead one way before doubling back, and are rapidly overtaken by a throng of clawed footprints
Trees, or similar prominent land marks, are smeared with stinking white paste and marked by many strong, blunted claws
A circle of carefully smoothed grass around a large stone which is spattered with spots of dried blood
Grasses and twigs have been woven together into a camouflaged hunting blind

name: Plain Gnoll Trinkets
intro: The following items might be carried by a plains gnoll:
rows: A string of {@dice 2d6} body parts from various races, roll on this table for {@table Plain Gnoll Trinkets body parts|RotH|body parts}.
A scrap of plate armor bearing the crest of a noble house
A bone patterned with a red, clay paint
The dried and shrunken head of a hyena
A badly damaged ornamental knife made from a shard of volcanic glass
A wallet with embossed initials containing {@dice 1d4} gold pieces
Three mismatched leather boots of good quality, slightly chewed
A semicircle of skin ripped from a gnoll's ear
An iron spike fixed in the place of a missing tooth
A bundle of singed coarse fur, smelling of herbs and old blood

name: Plain Gnoll Trinkets body parts
intro: The following body parts might make up a plain gnoll trinket

name: Plains Locale
rows: Still living roots from a tree hit by lightning that have captured a fragment of primal power
Small snaring weeds with an unpleasant thistle
Small red berries the hum slightly when held
A small spindly white tuber root
Black flakes of sludge like substance
Strange grass that looks like it is gilded
A strange plant that looks like it is burned

name: Planar Destinations and Moons
rows: Portals to the Material Plane are green
Not visible in Eberron's sky; impossibly black, portals are inaccessible
Dull white with large black chasm crossing it

name: Plane of Air: Ceaseless Storm Effects
rows: You are struck by lightning and must succeed on a {@dc 17} Constitution save or take {@damage 6d10} lightning damage, or half as much on a success.
You are battered by violent winds and must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 4d6} bludgeoning damage.

A {@spell thunderclap|XGE} explodes nearby. You must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 3d8} thunder damage, or half as much on a success. If you were {@status concentration||concentrating} on a spell, the spell ends if you fail the saving throw. Deaf creatures are unaffected.
An {@creature air elemental|MM} makes a single Slam attack against you: {@hit 8} to hit, {@damage 2d8 + 5} bludgeoning damage. It slips away before it can be retaliated against.
Gravitational forces render you {@condition unconscious} until the start of your next turn or until you take damage.
You are blown {@dice 10d10} ft. in a random direction.
You are miraculously unharmed by the storm.

name: Planetar

entries: A planetar is known for its ability to hear lies whenever they are spoken. Their ears carry on this trait even in death and can be seen twitching when falsehood passes through them.

entries.name: Use:
entries: While holding two of these ears, you have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) ability checks to detect a lie being spoken.

The blood of an angel flows with radiant energy that brings life to all it touches (it clearly didn't work hard enough for its original owner though). Many of the most desperate people actively seek angels in an attempt to harvest their blood as a panacea, without putting much thought into the worse fate that awaits them should they succeed.

entries.name: Use:
entries: When you drink this blood, you regain {@dice 6d8 + 3} hit points and are freed from any curse (except the curse of the fallen), disease, poison, blindness, and deafness.

rows: There is perhaps nothing more distinctive than the silhouette of glorious white angel wings against a radiant light. As some of the most powerful magical wings in all the planes, these make for almost perfect base materials for the ever-useful {@item wings of flying|DMG}.

The celestial bones of a planetar are stronger than steel and carry a charge of radiant energy within them long after their owner's demise. While most radiantly infused weapons are designed to force evil creatures to scurry away, weapons forged from the ever-vigilant planetars are designed to keep evil creatures nearby, ensuring they meet their divine judgement.

name: Plants
rows: You can eat this herb as an action, curing yourself of the {@condition poisoned} condition.
A berry that explodes when subjected to an impact. Makes a firecracker-like sound.
Possess antidotal agents, but it will not work by itself.
A Mysterious berry, said to be hated by dragons.

When given to a lynian they are {@condition charmed} by you as if under the {@spell charm person} spell for 1 hour. A lynian always knows when a creature has felvine and will react violently if it is not given it willingly.
A plant that has flammable properties. Can be crushed and thrown into a campfire to light it.
You can use an action to eat this herb, regaining 1d4 hit points.
An empty berry that can grow anywhere.
A lightweight and extremely strong plant.
Berry covered in needle-like thorns. Deals 1 piercing damage when picked up.
You are cured of blight, or blight-like spells or effects when you eat this berry.
Releases a smelly paint-like juice when broken.
A plant with leaves coated in sticky sap. The sap can be used as a simple glue.
A nut that violently ejects its contents when struck.
Chewing it releases oxygen, allowing you to breathe underwater for 1 minute.
Possesses antidotal agents, but it will not work by itself.
Works as a {@item Hot Drink|AGMH} but only for 1 hour.
Works as a {@item Cool Drink|AGMH} but only for 1 hour.
A bright red strawberry from scorching climes.
A bright red strawberry from scorching climes.
When you eat this seed, your Strength score increases by +2 for 1 minute. Once the effect wears off you gain one level of {@condition exhaustion}.
A large, beautifully colored flowering plant
Upon collection the creature must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or become {@condition poisoned} for 24 hours
A plant that looks to the heavens when it blooms. Its petals are used to make dye.
footnotes: You can find plants in all regions, in all sorts of different environments. You may find them in the middle of a grassy field, up a cliff, or perhaps under a tree.

When you succeed on an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check to locate a plant in an area. You must then make a Wisdom ({@skill Nature}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check against the locations Plant resource DC. On a success, you roll on the locations plant resources table.

name: Plesiosaurus
rows: The jaw of the plesiosaurus is lined with dozens of needle-like teeth. Their particular shape lends itself well to making powerful arrow-heads, and many primitive cultures have been discovered with quivers full of them.

entries: Darkness speaks, but shadows listen.
In stillness, the heart finds its dread.
Feathers fall, yet souls remain bound.
Crypts may close, but secrets never rest.
Moonlight masks a myriad of sins.
Life is but a dream within a nightmare.

name: Point-Buy a Familiar
rows: Increase Armor Class by 1 (up to a maximum of 15).
Increase Hit Die by one {@dice d4} (up to a maximum of {@dice 3d4} total Hit Dice).
Increase walking speed by 10 feet (to a maximum of 40 feet), or decrease walking speed by 10 feet and add a 30-foot burrowing, flying, or swimming speed.
Increase an ability score by 2 (so its modifier increases by 1; familiar ability scores have a maximum of 18).
Choose one ability score and gain proficiency in saving throws using the chosen ability.
Gain resistance to two specific types of damage, or gain the damage resistances of the base creature.
Gain immunity to a specific type of damage or a condition.
Gain {@sense blindsight} out to a range of 30 feet, {@sense darkvision} out to a range of 60 feet, or {@sense tremorsense|MM} out to a range of 30 feet.
Speak and understand one language of your choice.
Gain one trait (up to a maximum of three total traits).
Gain one melee weapon or ranged weapon attack (can only be taken once for a maximum of two total attack actions).
Weapon attacks can deal a damage type other than bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing.
Gain one action that is not a weapon attack (can only be taken once up to a maximum of two actions that aren't attacks).

name: Poison Ingredients
caption: Poison Ingredients
rows: {@bold Toxin Modifier}: Change poison damage to cold or necrotic damage; target is still {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute on a failed Constitution saving throw; this toxin is still considered poison damage when combining with other ingredients.
{@bold Toxin Modifier}: Changes any poison {@bold Effect} to be non-lethal and only incapacitates the target.

{@bold Special (Toxin Effect)}: Slowly paralyzes opponent. Target makes a DC 5 + {@italic Alchemy Modifier} Constitution saving throw each turn for 4 turns. While under this effect, target is considered slowed by the {@spell slow} spell. On a failed save, the target is considered {@condition paralyzed} for 4 rounds. Cannot be modified or altered by other ingredients.
{@bold Toxin Modifier}: The target will not notice any poison damage {@bold Effect} in their system until they take 5 rounds of damage from the toxin.
{@bold Special (Potion & Toxin Modifier)}: The final {@bold Effect} after all other calculations is the exact opposite. This is up to the DM's discretion on the specifics per potion/poison.

{@bold Toxin Modifier}: Change poison damage to fire or acid damage; target is still {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute on a failed Constitution saving throw; this toxin is still considered poison damage when combining with other ingredients.
{@bold Special (Potion & Toxin Modifier)}: Delay the {@bold Effect} of an ingredient this was combined with by {@dice 1d6} rounds.
{@bold Toxin Modifier}: While {@condition poisoned}, target's movement speed is reduced by 10 ft for 1 minute. Cannot be altered by other ingredients.
{@bold Toxin Modifier}: While {@condition poisoned}, target has disadvantage on ability checks. Cannot be altered by other ingredients.
{@bold Special (Potion & Toxin Modifier)}: Makes the potion or toxin more stable and safer to craft.
{@bold Toxin Modifier}: Double the dice rolled of any {@bold Toxin Effect}, but reduce that {@bold Effect} duration by half. This modifier can stack.

{@bold Toxin Modifier}: Change poison damage to radiant damage; target is still {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute on a failed Constitution saving throw; this toxin is still considered poison damage when combining with other ingredients.
{@bold Toxin Modifier}: Increase the dice-type by 1 size for any {@bold Toxin Effect}.
{@bold Toxin Effect}: {@dice 1d4} + Alchemy Modifier poison damage per round; target is {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute.

name: Poison Injury
rows: {@b Poisoned Muscles.} You get disadvantage on all {@variantrule Ability Check|XPHB|Ability Checks}, {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB|Saving Throws}, and {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB|Attack Rolls}. This can be healed with the {@spell Mend Flesh and Bones|WoBrCa} spell. After 2 weeks it becomes Major Poison Bumps.

{@b Poisoned Heart.} Your hit point maximum decreases by an amount equal to your level at the end of every day. If your hitpoint maximum drops to 0 you are {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} but stable. This can be healed with the {@spell Mend Flesh and Bones|WoBrCa} spell or by making a DC 15 Wisdom (medicine) check using a charge of a healer's kit at the end of a Long Rest. Once it is healed you regain all your lost {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

Poisoned Lungs. When you use verbal components to cast a spell or speak during combat, you lose {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half your level (round up). This can be healed with the {@spell Mend Flesh and Bones|WoBrCa} spell. After 2 weeks it heals naturally.
{@b Poisoned Brain.} You get disadvantage on all Wisdom and Intelligence checks and saves. This can be healed with the {@spell Mend Flesh and Bones|WoBrCa} spell. After 2 weeks it heals naturally.
{@b Poisoned Wound.} You become {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} for 1 hour. After that hour you get Poison Bumps.

{@b Major Poison Bumps.} You get many poison bumps in a place very visible for others. You have disadvantage on Charisma (Persuasion) and advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks. This can be removed with the {@spell Heal Minor Wounds|WoBrCa} spell.
{@b Minor Poison Bumps.} The poison bumps don't have any adverse effect. This can be removed with the {@spell Heal Minor Wounds|WoBrCa} spell.

name: Political Intrigue; Bonds
caption: Bonds
rows: My parent or guardian used to take me to meetings at their guild hall. I would listen to speeches and rallies and that's what radicalized me. To this day I consider the local guild hall a second home.
I'll never forget what it was like to see the people I love suffer at the hands of injustice.
My mentor taught me everything I know and I'm carrying on their work.
This manifesto changed my life and worldview. I refer to it a lot and carry a copy with me everywhere.
Nothing is more important than impressing my family.
Someone important to me had their livelihood ruined by a political entity, and I'm determined to make sure it never happens to anyone else.
I learned about politics from a traveling theatre troupe that came through town and did political satire. I've been a volunteer at (or donor to) the local theatre ever since.

My most treasured possession is a piece of paper with the following written on it: "It is not your responsibility to finish the work of perfecting the world, but you are not free to desist from it either."
Someone stood up for me once and it saved me. In turn, I will always stand up for others.
My nation (or city) and its people are all that matter to me.
My allies are the only people I trust.
I know the city's sewers (or other hiding places) like the back of my hand.
I love someone who doesn't share my worldview.
I've spent most of my life in the local tavern. Everyone knows me there and I know everyone.
My family escaped persecution and I was raised on their stories.
I've been writing in my journal every night ever since I could remember. It comes with me everywhere and contains all my thoughts and ideas.
I'm obsessed with embarrassing my political rival.
I'm writing what I believe will be the political manifesto of its time.
I have to protect my fortune from the undeserving people who want to take it from me.
The local library is a sacred place to me; it's where I think, read, write, and plan.

name: Political Intrigue; Flaws
caption: Flaws
rows: When things seem overwhelming I become nihilistic or melancholic.
I tend to drastically overestimate my own influence and power.
Once I get a little bit of authority I get really bossy.
I tend to think in black and white, right and wrong; the gray is harder for me to see.
I put my causes first—and second and third, often to the detriment of my health and happiness.
There are times when it would be safer (and maybe smarter) to back down, but I never do that.
I get bogged down in details and can be slow to act.
I believe I know what's best for everyone.
I always speak my mind, even when propriety (or danger) says I should shut my mouth.
I would risk the lives of strangers to bring about my goals.
My political work feels like a burden. I wish I could be free of it.
As much as I care about the common people, I don't really know what their lives are really like.
I act before considering the consequences; I'll deal with them later.
I would do anything to hide my failures.
I got into all this political stuff because I like when people do what I want.
I secretly worry that my work is worthless and I'll never make a difference.
I care more about my personal glory than any cause.
I've sacrificed love and companionship for my cause.
I have no use for those who question my political analysis.
People either get it or they don't—and if they don't, I can't be bothered with them.

name: Political Intrigue; Ideals
caption: Ideals
rows: {@b Equity.} Everyone deserves economic, social, and political rights.
{@b Collective Power.} When we come together, we're more powerful than any noble, royal, or elected official.
{@b Collective Responsibility.} When people are suffering, it's everyone's job to help to alleviate that suffering.
{@b Change.} Society and its systems of power must evolve to meet changing needs. Complacency leads to harm.
{@b Order.} Social stability is everything. Chaos will reign unless we keep it in check.
{@b Intellect.} There is no one who understands political science, strategy, and philosophy like I do, and I'm always striving to learn and know more.
{@b Strategy.} The world is a chess board; knowing how to move the pieces ensures victory.
{@b Pacifism.} Violence doesn't permanently solve problems. I strive for a world free from war.
{@b Power.} If I can attain enough power, no one can harm my community or me.
{@b Performance.} I like people to notice me and know my work.
{@b Hope.} No matter how bad things get, we must never give up.
{@b Work.} There's nothing more stimulating than the minutiae of bureaucracy and politics.
{@b Status.} Being in this position comes with an undeniable rise in rank and respect. I like that.
{@b Destiny.} This work is my calling and nothing can pull me away from it.
{@b Influence.} I want to be known by name and reputation and better yet, followed for my beliefs.
{@b Retribution.} Someone or an entity in power harmed me, and I'm going to make sure they pay.
{@b Redemption.} At some point in my past I was part of the problem, and I'll only feel absolved if I solve those problems.
{@b Faith.} My religion teaches that civic involvement is part of my duty as an adherent.
{@b Free Thinking.} Curiosity and discovery are what allow progress to be made and what prevent complacency and stagnation.
{@b A Life Well Lived.} I want to die knowing that I did everything I can to help.

name: Political Intrigue; Personality Traits
caption: Personality Traits (Choose Two)
rows: All I need is what I can carry. Possessions are a distraction.
I really can't tolerate "roughing it." I'll do anything I can to avoid having to eat, sleep, or spend time in a place I deem beneath me.
I'm a sore loser (and sometimes a sore winner).
I idolize a leader or activist from many generations ago. Their work guides me; I think and talk about them a lot.
I love winning arguments so much that I sometimes start them.
I feel most confident, powerful, and at ease when I'm given the floor and am addressing a group about my beliefs.
I've read every single book I can find about political science and social movements.
I have a hard time with idleness; I can't sit still.
If I see that someone needs help, I step in.
I love solving puzzles; the harder the better. Societal problems are just big puzzles.
I would give someone the shirt off my back if they said they needed it. Or even if they said they liked it.
I love being in charge. Few are as cut out to lead, manage, and direct as I am.
I was put on this earth to stick it to the System, and that's what I'll do.
There's basically nothing I don't have an opinion on.
As far as I am concerned, strangers are just friends you haven't met yet.
I've never met a paradigm I didn't want to subvert.
I love getting attention for my work and achievements.
I am drawn to rebels and iconoclasts even if their beliefs differ from mine.
I hate being the center of attention. I crave anonymity.

name: Poor Hunt
rows: Gathered around the skeleton of a manticore, they eat the iron from its body. Each is enough to feed one person.
Discovered inside a deep, dark hole, these insects exhibit an unnatural hunger. Each swarm provides enough food to feed one person.
{@dice 1d6+1} {@creature Giant Poisonous Snake|MM|Giant Poisonous Snakes} [{@creature Giant Venomous Snake|XMM}]
Coiled around their nest in a narrow cave, they guard one egg for each snake present. Two of them are needed to feed one person and each egg can feed one person.
At the bottom of a sloped sand pit, they gather to feast on a rotting hyena. It takes two of them to feed one person.
They aimlessly drift as a small swarm in search for prey. Three of them feed one person.
Starving and malnourished, they track the characters and eventually corner them. Each can feed up to ten people.

name: Poor Tavern Random Events and Adventure Hooks
intro: A Poor lifestyle gets you a flophouse with just a few overcrowded rooms or a taphouse where anyone staying the night simply sleeps in the common room. If you pay early in the day you might get the use of a threadbare blanket, otherwise the accommodations are little more than bad food, bad company, and floor space.
rows: Local farmers are preparing an assault on a goblin camp because no one else will help.
It's oddly quiet around the common room. People keep to themselves and wallow in their own sorrows.
The only dish is a lumpy stew from a huge cauldron that looks like it's never met a brush.
The bartender is also a bonesetter, the closest thing this area has to a healer.
There is a terrible smell coming from a back room, but the innkeeper pretends not to notice anything.
Water drips down from a crack in the ceiling. Is it even raining outside?
An undertaker comes in and walks slowly through the room, measuring everyone with his eyes.
A member of the City Watch hauls one of the patrons outside for a beating in the street.
A girl selling wilted flowers tries to sell to the patrons before the barkeep chases her back out into the street.
More than once, someone tries to pickpocket you clumsily.
The depressed innkeeper shares with you that this was once a thriving business, before the curse on his family.
A few locals are playing dice for copper pieces.
A bounty hunter comes in for a drink, trailing an elf with a gag and a chain leash.
The half-orc bouncer says he'll throw you out if you do that again. What exactly did you do?
The innkeeper looks nervously at a group of mercenaries shouting abuse at other patrons.
A man looks you up and down and says you look tough enough to make some extra coin if you have the stomach.
A halfling with little talent picks out some sort of tune on a battered looking instrument.
A tough-looking mercenary at the bar loudly tells racist jokes, not caring who hears her.
Two children come in to tug at the clothes of a drunk who is passed out under a table. He doesn't respond.
Someone dumps their drink over the head of a half-elf, muttering how it ain't natural for races to mix.

name: Poor Taverns (2 gp)
intro: A Poor lifestyle gets you a flophouse with just a few overcrowded rooms or a taphouse where anyone staying the night simply sleeps in the common room. If you pay early in the day you might get the use of a threadbare blanket, otherwise the accommodations are little more than bad food, bad company, and floor space.

Portal, Link PA#1, Blink Strike, Link PA#2, Falling Dodge
