name: Portal Malfunction Effects
rows: The portal does not function, but draws magical power from the user in an attempt to power itself. Any spell on a creature that touches the portal ends.

The portal does not function, but draws magical power from the user's items in an attempt to power itself. If a creature touches the portal while carrying any items that contain charges, the creature must roll a {@dice d6} and subtract the rolled number of charges from each of those items.
The portal does not function. The user must succeed on a DC 20 Strength saving throw or be pushed back 15 feet from the portal.

The portal does not function. Instead, a wave of forceful energy pulses from the portal in a 30-foot radius. Each creature within the radius must make a DC 15 Strength saving throw. A creature takes {@damage 3d10} force damage and is knocked {@condition prone} on a failed save. A creature that succeeds on its saving throw takes half the damage and isn't knocked {@condition prone}.

The portal functions, but the user takes {@damage 3d10} force damage and the portal sends them to the wrong destination. To determine where the user ends up, use the table in the teleport spell description as a mishap.
Nothing happens. The portal does not function.

name: Positive Surges
rows: The smell of your favorite food fills the air around you.
Small plants grow to full bloom around your feet.
Your clothes become cleaned, and faded dyes return to full brightness.
Your body becomes sheathed in a thin layer of protective energy. You gain temporary hitpoints equal to the spell's level + your spellcasting ability modifier.
You are innervated. Your movement speed increases by 15 feet until the end of your next turn.

The energy of the spell flashes brightly. A target of your choice within 5 feet of the target of the spell must make a Constitution saving throw against your Spell Save DC or be blinded until the end of your next turn.
The energy of the spell becomes raw and without defined form. If the spell deals damage, you can choose to change its damage type to force damage.
With a surge of energy, you are able to shift your position. You may immediately teleport to a point of your choice within 10 feet of you.
Arcs of chaotic energy emanate from the spell. A random hostile creature within 15 feet of the target of the spell takes 1d8 lightning damage.
Enemy attacks are pushed away. The next attack against you before the start of your next turn has disadvantage.

The air around you crackles. Until the start of your next turn, if a creature within 30 feet of you hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to deal 1d4 lightning damage to the attacker. This damage increases by 1d4 for every level of the spell above 1st.
If you cast a spell before the end of your next turn, roll on this table and gain a positive effect.
You become energetic. You gain the effects of the haste spell until the end of your next turn, ignoring the lethargy.
The spell amplifies. If the spell deals damage, it deals an extra 1d6 damage to each target, increasing by an additional 1d6 for every level of the spell above 1st.
If you take damage from a spell before the start of your next turn, you can roll 1d8 and reduce the damage by the number rolled.
The spell becomes unusually stable. If the spell requires concentration, you have advantage on constitution saving throws you make to maintain it.
The spell seems to guide itself towards your targets. You have advantage on the attack roll, and targets have disadvantage on saving throws, for this spell.

The spell is efficient, allowing you to siphon excess magic. You regain a 1st level spell slot if you have expended any. If you have the Font of Magic feature, you can choose to regain 2 sorcery points instead.
Roll twice on this table and gain both effects; reroll 20s.

name: Potential Losses
caption: Potential Losses
rows: {@b Family.} You have family in Dread Metrol. Are they safe, or currently threatened by plague or the Watch?
{@b Property.} You own a home or business in Dread Metrol. It may not currently be open, but you love it and want to get back to it.
{@b Friend.} You have a close friend who's not an adventurer—perhaps an old mentor, former comrade-in-arms, apprentice, or servant.
{@b Reputation.} You've developed a reputation and don't want to lose it. What are you known for? Heroism? Intellect? Generosity? Courage?
{@b Lover.} This could be a long, deep relationship, or someone you just met last night, but it's someone you truly care about.

{@b Power.} Your character's abilities are somehow at risk. This fits well for a cleric or warlock—if you don't follow the proper path, you could lose your magic—but depending on your twist, it could work for any character.

name: Potion and Oil
rows: {@item Potion of Hide from Undead|5EPotion Making}
{@item Potion of the Magic Fang|5EPotion Making}
{@item Potion of Diminution|DMG}, {@item Potion of Growth|DMG}

footnotes.name: Harvesting Components
entries: During a long or short rest, you can search for exotic plants nearby. Choose a plant from the Potion and Oil table that is in your current region and roll a Survival Check vs the DC of the plant. If you make the check, roll 1d4 to see how many you harvest.

footnotes.name: Brewing Potions
entries: To brew a potion, you must have the required number of plants as stated in the # to Brew section of the Potion and Oil table. Potions are brewed in towns only. The equipment to brew them can be found in an alchemist, potion, or herbalist shop. Not all potions are created equal. Ask your DM how many potions you can make during your stay in town.

name: Potion Fraud
rows: The potion works as expected, but it has a strange or unpleasant taste.
The potion has been intentionally mislabeled and is actually {@filter a different potion of an uncommon rarity|items|type=potion|rarity=uncommon} (chosen by the GM).
The potion has been diluted. If the potion's effect has a duration, it lasts only half as long as normal. If the potion heals or deals damage, the amount of each is halved.

The potion is defective. When consumed, it has a {@chance 50|50%} chance of having the opposite of its intended effect or of giving an additional negative effect (included in the {@table Potions for Sale|HumblewoodTales} table).
The potion is a dud; it does nothing when consumed.

name: Potion Ingredients
caption: Potion Ingredients
rows: {@bold Special (Potion Effect)}: Can combine with any other {@bold Potion Effect} ingredient to become a food source for 1 day. Cannot be altered by other ingredients.
{@bold Special (Potion & Toxin Modifier)}: The final Effect after all other calculations is the exact opposite. This is up to the DM's discretion on the specifics per potion/poison.
{@bold Potion Modifier}: Increase the dice-type by 1 size for any healing {@bold Effect}.
{@bold Special (Potion & Toxin Modifier)}: Delay the {@bold Effect} of an ingredient this was combined with by {@dice 1d6} rounds.
{@bold Potion Effect}: Stabilizes body heat to resist cold weather or wet condition penalties for 1 hour. Cannot be altered by other ingredients.

{@bold Potion Modifier}: Double the dice rolled of any healing {@bold Effect}, but divide the total of the dice by 2 (rounding down); Then, the recipient receives that amount of healing per round for 2 rounds.
{@bold Potion Effect}: Removes {@dice 1d6} rounds of poison in the target's system, but cannot remove it completely. One round of poison damage will still occur at minimum.
{@bold Special (Potion & Toxin Modifier)}: Makes the potion or toxin more stable and safer to craft.

{@bold Special (Potion Effect}: Reduce any disease or poison's potency by half for {@dice 2d12} hours. Only hinders already existing poisons or diseases in the body. Cannot be altered by other ingredients.
{@bold Potion Modifier}: Double the dice rolled of any healing {@bold Effect}, but remove all Alchemy Modifier bonuses. This modifier can stack.
{@bold Potion Effect}: Heals for {@dice 2d4} + Alchemy Modifier.

name: Potion Miscibility Mishap
intro: What happens when potions are mixed?.
rows: The effects of the complex potion with the least remaining duration immediately end. You take 1d6 damage per round that was remaining in the effects that just ended. This damage can not drop you below 1hp.

The effects of the complex potion with the least remaining duration immediately end. You instantly gain 2d4 years of age. If this effect would increase your age beyond your normal lifespan, make a Constitution save. If you fail, you die of old age. If you succeed, you remain alive but you gain 2 exhaustion levels.
The effects of the complex potion with the least remaining duration immediately end. You suffer disadvantage on all saves for 1 minute.
The effects of the complex potion with the least remaining duration immediately end. You gain the effects of the faerie fire spell for 1 minute.
The effects of the complex potion with the least remaining duration immediately end. You become poisoned for 1 minute.
The effects of the complex potion with the least remaining duration immediately end..
You gain advantage on all saves for 1 minute.
You instantly become 2d4 years younger. This effect can not reduce your age below the point at which members of your race become an adult.
All effects from complex potions remain in effect until the duration of all complex potions run out.
You instantly gain temporary hp equal to your character level.

name: Potion Mishaps
rows: The potion fumes turn your skin green. Only a {@spell remove curse|phb} spell can end this effect.
A large, unsightly wart grows in a prominent position on your body.
The destroyed potion explodes, catching you on fire and dealing {@dice 1d6} fire damage each turn until you use an action to render yourself prone and put it out.
The potion releases a toxic miasma, as if you had cast the spell {@spell stinking cloud|phb} centered on yourself.
Roll 1d100. This is the percentage of your hair that falls out.
The potion ignites in a loud flash and an explosive bang. You are blinded and deafened for one minute.
Smoke from the potion deadens your senses. Everything smells and tastes like dirt for 24 hours.
The potion's fumes cloud your mind, and you forget all events that happened within the last hour.
Within 20 feet of you, all plants wilt and die, and all food and milk spoils.
One randomly determined item on your person is transported to the Ethereal Plane.

name: Potion of Augmented Reality Effects
rows: For 1 hour, the creature is under the effect of a {@spell true seeing} spell. For 1 minute, it's under the effect of a {@spell haste} spell (no {@status concentration} required).
For 1 hour, the creature is under the effect of a {@spell true seeing} spell. For 10 minutes, it's under the effect of a {@spell slow} spell (no {@status concentration} required).
For 1 hour, the creature is under the effect of a {@spell true seeing} spell. For 10 minutes, it's under the effect of a {@spell bless} spell (no {@status concentration} required).

For 1 hour, the creature is under the effect of a {@spell true seeing} spell. For 10 minutes, the creature must make a successful {@dc 11} Wisdom saving throw at the start of each of its turns or it spends its turn doing nothing.
For 1 hour, the creature is under the effect of a {@spell true seeing} spell and it gains 10 temporary hit points.

For 1 hour, the creature is under the effect of a {@spell true seeing} spell and its hit point maximum is reduced by 10. If it loses hit points after drinking the potion, they aren't recovered automatically at the end of the hour when the creature's hit point maximum returns to normal.

For 1 hour, the creature is under the effect of a {@spell true seeing} spell. For the same duration, it's illuminated by {@spell faerie fire} (the creature sheds {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} in a 10-foot radius, it can't benefit from {@condition invisible|PHB|invisibility}, and attackers who can see the illumination have advantage when attacking the creature; no {@status concentration} required).

For 1 hour, the creature is under the effect of a {@spell Blindness/Deafness|PHB|blindness} spell. For the same duration, the creature also gains {@sense tremorsense|MM} (10 feet), and this new sense extends into the Ethereal Plane.

name: Powerful Mutations
intro: The following mutations do not require any visible changes in the character until used. People who have these mutations are not obviously recognizable as mutants if they don't use their powers. Some of these mutations require using an action to activate or use them.
rows: {@b Darkvision:} You have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray. (Reroll this mutation if you already have darkvision as a trait from your species.)
{@b No breath:} You do not need to breathe.
{@b No water:} You do not need to drink to survive.
{@b Chameleon skin:} Your skin changes colors as you wish. You gain proficiency in the Stealth skill.

{@b Savage bite:} Your mouth is able to open surprisingly wide, revealing hidden, pointed teeth when you wish it. As your action, you can make a bite attack that deals {@damage 1d4} piercing damage. Your bite has the finesse and light weapon properties. You have proficiency with this attack.

{@b Gluey globs:} You can produce gluey globs at your fingertips. Climbing doesn't cost you extra movement and you add your proficiency bonus to Strength (Athletics) checks for climbing. As your action, you can fling these globs as a ranged weapon attack against one creature within 10 feet. If you hit, the target has disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity checks and saves for one round. The globs have the light and thrown weapon properties. You have proficiency with this attack.
{@b Face dancing:} You can alter your features. You add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to create a visual disguise for yourself.
{@b Sense numenera:} As your action, you can sense the presence of a functioning numenera device or numenera ability within 60 feet. You do not learn details or the precise location.

{@b Hidden stinger:} You have a retractable stinger in your hand, elbow, knee, or foot. When you make an unarmed strike with that part of your body, the stinger injects poison into your target. In addition to your unarmed strike damage, a creature hit by the stinger must make a Constitution saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Con modifier) or take {@damage 1d4} poison damage.

{@b Spit needles:} You have special glands that make poisoned needles (most creatures with this mutation have the glands in their mouth). As your action, you can spit a needle as a ranged weapon attack at a target within 10 feet. If you hit, the needle deals 1 piercing damage and the target must make a Constitution saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Con modifier) or take {@damage 1d4} poison damage. The needles have the light weapon property. You have proficiency with this attack.

{@b Spit acid:} As your action, you can spit acid from your mouth as a ranged weapon attack at one target within 10 feet. If you hit, it deals {@damage 1d4} acid damage. You have proficiency with this attack.

{@b Spit webs:} You can make up to 10 feet of a strong, rope-like material each day at the rate of about 1 foot per minute. As your action, you can spit globs of webbing from your mouth as a ranged weapon attack at a target within 10 feet. If you hit, the target has disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity checks and saves for one round. The globs have the light and thrown weapon properties. You have proficiency with this attack.
{@b Filtered lungs:} You have advantage on saving throws against attacks using gas, mist, or vapor. You add double your proficiency bonus to the number of minutes you can hold your breath.

{@b Electronics-disrupting field:} As an action, you can spend one Hit Die to disrupt electronic devices (such as many kinds of numenera items, including automatons). Each device within 10 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Con modifier). Creatures are incapacitated for 1 round if they fail, or have disadvantage for 1 round if they succeed. The effect automatically ends for a device if it is no longer within 10 feet of you.

{@b Flesh-disrupting field:} As an action, you can spend one Hit Die to disrupt flesh. Each creature within 10 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Con modifier). A target takes {@damage 1d6} necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

{@b Thought-disrupting field:} As an action, you can spend one Hit Die to disrupt thoughts. Each creature within 10 feet of you must make an Intelligence saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Int modifier). On a successful save, a target has disadvantage on Intelligence checks and saves and takes {@damage 1d6} psychic damage on a failed save.

{@b Magnetic flesh:} You attract or repel metal when you desire. Small metal objects cling to you. Climbing on metal doesn't cost you extra movement and you add your proficiency bonus to climbing rolls on metal. You have advantage on keeping your grip on a metal item. As a reaction (which you take when you are hit by an attack from a metal opponent or metal weapon) you can give yourself a +2 bonus to AC against the triggering attack.

{@b Gravity negation:} As your move, you can spend one Hit Die to negate gravity on yourself for the next 10 minutes. When this is active, you can use your move to concentrate on floating in any direction up to half your basic walking speed. If you don't use your move to direct your motion, you drift with the wind or with any momentum you have gained.

{@b Telepathy:} As an action, you can spend one Hit Die to make telepathic contact with another creature within 60 feet. Communication is two-way, but the other party must be willing and able to communicate. You don't have to see the target, but you must know that it's within range. You can have more than one active contact at once, but you must establish contact with each target individually. Each contact lasts up to 10 minutes. If you spend an additional Hit Die when you establish contact, it lasts for a full day instead of 10 minutes.

{@b Pyrokinesis:} You can cause a flammable object you can see within 10 feet to spontaneously catch fire. Make a spell attack against your target. If you hit, it deals {@damage 1d4} fire damage. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for this mutation. After you use pyrokinesis, you have disadvantage with it until you complete a short or long rest.

{@b Telekinesis:} As an action, you can activate your ability to exert force on objects within 25 feet. This ability lasts for one hour. You can use this force to move objects, push against objects, and so on. For example, as an action you could lift and pull a light object anywhere within range to yourself, or move a heavy object (like a piece of furniture) about 10 feet. Any telekinetic action that would require a Strength check uses your Intelligence. This mutation lacks the fine control to wield a weapon or move objects with much speed, so in most situations, it's not a means of attack. You can't use this mutation to move your own body or anything you are holding or carrying. The power lasts for one hour. After you've used telekinesis for an hour, it has disadvantage until you complete a short or long rest.

{@b Phaseshifting:} As an action, you can pass slowly through a solid barrier at a rate of 1 inch per round (minimum of one round to pass through the barrier). You can't perceive anything or take actions (other than continuing to move through the barrier) until you pass entirely through the barrier. You can't pass through barriers made of energy (such as wall of fire) or force. After you use phase shifting, you have disadvantage on all rolls until you complete a short or long rest. If you use phaseshifting while you have disadvantage from it, you can't use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

{@b Power device:} As an action, you can spend Hit Dice to recharge an iron flesh device or numenera relic. For an uncommon item, adding 1 charge (or one use for a depleted relic) costs 1 Hit Die, a rare item costs 2 Hit Dice, a very rare item costs 3 Hit Dice, and a legendary item costs 4 Hit Dice. After you've used this mutation, you have disadvantage on all Intelligence rolls and can't use it again until you've completed a short or long rest.

{@b Drain power:} As an action, you can touch an iron flesh device or numenera relic, draining its power and using it to heal yourself. The number of hit points you regain depends on the rarity of the device or relic: {@dice 1d8} for common or uncommon, {@dice 2d8} for rare, {@dice 3d8} for very rare, or {@dice 5d8} for legendary. You recover these hit points at a rate of {@dice 1d8} per round, and you must use your action each round and maintain concentration; if you are interrupted, the healing ends. This completely drains the device, even if interrupted before you're finished (at the GM's discretion, an item may retain some charges or only have to make a depletion roll if partially drained). Because you need to maintain contact and concentration with the item to use this ability, it is all but impossible to use it on an item held or worn by an unwilling creature.
{@b Regeneration:} Whenever you spend Hit Dice to regain hit points, add your proficiency bonus to each Hit Die you roll for healing.

{@b Feed off pain:} Any time a creature within 10 feet takes at least 6 points of damage in one attack, you heal 1 hit point. You can feed off any creature in this way, whether friend or foe. This never heals you more than 1 point per round.

A heavy precipitation forms. Visibility is limited to {@dice 1d4 * 10|1d4 x 10} feet.

name: Previous Adventure
rows: You were a bodyguard for an Eastern merchant. You quit before he went south to the {@book jungle|BITCPI|7|The Untamed Jungles}, never to return.
You tried to steal a piece of jewellery from a wealthy lord. You successfully escaped with all your hands!
You fought as a {@background Variant Entertainer (Gladiator)|phb|gladiator} in a tournament. First place is overrated.
You served on an {@book Aegan|BITCPI|7|The Aegan Empire} scouting vessel, and the things you saw on the high seas do not bear retelling.
You did a job for a {@class wizard|phb}. You're not sure what the point of it was, but at least he paid well.
A bandit hunt you were on was interrupted by an ungodly howling. You found the bandits the next morning, parts of them.

name: Previous Occupation
rows: You were a craftsman; you worked with either stone, {@item copper|phb}, or {@item iron|phb} for money.
You used your skill with a quill to write for commissions.
You were an artist. You illustrated books and murals from where you were from.
You were a mercenary, and made money performing jobs for the highest bidder.
You were a professional soldier working for the local militia.
You worked on the farms, living a simple life.

name: Previous Relationship
rows: You were friends with a merchant from the {@book Aegan Empire|BITCPI|7|The Aegan Empire}, and often listened to her stories about her technologically advanced homeland.
You kept company with a thief who would sometimes take you on drunken adventures.
You were good friends with a priest of the Eternal Queen, and often talked about the gods and history.

You had a brief relationship with a {@race tiefling|phb}, or another rare sight in the {@book Pevic Continent|BITCPI|2}. For better or worse you were the talk of the town until they left without a word.
You had an enmity with a {@book Helveti Mercenary|BITCPI|7|The Helveti} from the Wendigo {@book Comanda|BITCPI|4|The Helveti Comanda}, which caused you no end of trouble.
You would frequently bump into a {@class wizard|phb}, who seemed to find you very curious for some reason.

name: Progenitus Creature Adaptations
caption: Use the table to determine how a creature mutates when under the influence of Progenitus.
intro: The Adaptation Table provided in this page is used to determine mutations for creatures under the influence of Progenitus, when they are summoned, spawned, or first enter its domain. Alternatively, it can also be adapted for use with monstrosities warped by powerful magic or other means, providing a versatile tool for enhancing a variety of beings with unique mutations, always keeping your encounters fresh. Each mutation is designed to enhance a creature's capabilities in unique ways, affecting its abilities, appearance, and combat strategies.
rows: The creature's skin hardens into a shell, increasing its AC by 2.
Grows venomous fangs, adding 4 (1d8) poison damage to bite attacks.
Sprouts leathery wings, gaining a flying speed of 60 ft., or increasing its flying speed by 30 ft.
Grows two additional limbs, granting an extra claw attack during its turn.
Gains fast healing, regaining 5 hit points at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 hit point.
The creature's eyes become imbued with magic, granting the ability to see through magical darkness out to a range of 120 ft.
Grows tentacles, increasing the reach of its melee weapon attacks by 10 ft.

Gains a 30-foot cone breath weapon once per short rest as an action. Each creature in the area must make a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw, taking 28 (8d6) acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage (determined randomly) on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.
Muscles bulge with power, increasing the creature's Strength score by 2, up to a maximum of 30.
Develops a mental shield, gaining advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
The creature's skin matches its surroundings, granting advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide.

Can emit a powerful screech once per short rest as an action. Each creature within 20 feet must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition stunned} until the end of its next turn.
The creature's weapon attacks become magical.
Emits toxic spores. Each other creature starting its turn within 5 ft. of the monstrosity must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw or be poisoned until the start of its next turn.
Radiates decay in a 10-ft radius, dealing 3 (1d6) necrotic damage to creatures entering or starting their turn in it.
The creature gains 50 current and maximum hit points.
Gains truesight out to a range of 30 ft.
Becomes more flexible, gaining advantage on Dexterity ability checks, attack rolls, and saving throws.
Gains telepathy out to a range of 120 ft.
Can teleport up to 30 ft. to an unoccupied space it can see as a bonus action.

entries: The PCs stage a dramatic re-enactment of the PCs' adventures and accomplishments in founding their domain, establishing their status as rightful rulers.
{@b Relevant Skills} Intelligence (History), Charisma (Performance)

{@b Special} PCs using visual and auditory illusions to augment their performance have advantage. PCs can perform in any common area (disadvantage), on a small stage (cost 100 gp), or on an elaborate stage in the noble section of the festival grounds (1000 gp, grants advantage on the check).

The PCs lampoon the follies, missteps, embarrassing rumors, and other shortcomings of the leaders of other nations, merchant guilds, religious orders, or other noteworthy organizations through satire and clever wit.
{@b Relevant Skills} Charisma (Persuasion), Charisma (Performance)
{@b Special} Each time this is used, all future We Meet at Last DCs increase by 2.

The PCs recount the glory of the PCs' domain and the impressive accomplishments and prowess of the new masters of their lands, while also trumpeting what a fair and pleasant land it is and the benefits that citizens enjoy living there.
{@b Relevant Skills} Intelligence (History), Charisma (Performance)
{@b Special} PCs offering free food and drink (costing 1d10 x 100 gp) gain a advantage on this check.

The PCs arrange a meeting with merchant leaders from the other nearby domains to find buyers for the goods produced in the PCs' domain and to obtain favorable prices on goods they wish to import to their country.
{@b Relevant Skills} Wisdom (Insight), any one tool proficiency.
{@b Special} PCs offering a bribe (1d10 x 100 gp) gain advantage their check.

name: Properties of Xoriat
rows: Creatures can walk on any surface—walls, floors, ceilings. If a creature falls, it does so in a random direction, not necessarily toward the floor.
Creatures are under the effects of the {@spell slow} spell.
The air within the region takes on a fluidic quality. There's no risk of drowning, but creatures must move by swimming, and all of the effects of underwater combat apply.
Creatures are under the effects of the {@spell haste} spell.
Creatures are under the effects of the {@spell mirror image} spell, and destroyed duplicates do not reappear.
Whenever a creature is hit with an attack, it becomes invisible until the start of its next turn.
Creatures can use a bonus action to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space they can see
Creatures are under the effects of the {@spell detect thoughts} spell, but can't use this to probe deeper into another creature's thoughts.
Creatures are under the effects of the {@spell gaseous form} spell, becoming misty clouds of thought energy. Creatures can speak (forming sounds with their thoughts) in this form

Creatures take on the appearance of a random creature in the region. This has no effect on abilities, and size remains unchanged (so if a halfling takes on the appearance of an ogre, they are a small ogre).
Creatures gain {@sense truesight} with a range of 60 feet.
Creatures are vulnerable to psychic damage, even creatures that are normally immune to it.

Size depends on perspective—is the mountain on the horizon enormous, or can you reach out and hold it in your hand? All creatures are randomly under the effects of the {@spell enlarge/reduce} spell. At the start of its turn, a creature rolls {@dice 1d3}. On a 1, its size is reduced, on a 2, the creature is its normal size, and on a 3, its size is enlarged

entries: The venom of a pseudodragon has a soporific effect that some alchemists have actually used to create a draught to treat insomnia. Of course, in its pure state, it can still be used as an effective tranquilliser.

entries.name: Use:
entries: Can be used to coat 1 piece of slashing or piercing ammunition or one slashing or piercing weapon. Applying the poison takes an action. The next time that the coated ammunition or weapon successfully hits a creature, that creature must succeed on a {@dc 11} Constitution saving throw or become {@condition poisoned} for 1 hour. If the saving throw fails by 5 or more, the target falls {@condition unconscious} for the same duration, or until it takes damage or another creature uses an action to shake it awake.

name: Psionic Flaw
rows: Your anger grows harder to control, your eyes change color and start glowing when you become angry.
You hear a faint screaming at all times. It sounds almost...familiar.
A strange swirling tattoo-like scar very slowly grows from where it pierces you that burns painfully.
When you sleep, you have nightmares about another life filled with horror, fear and revulsion.
You cannot remember your own name, even when told.
You grow small vestigial tentacles along your jawline like a strange beard after being attuned to it for {@dice 1d4} days.

name: Psionic Items Table
rows: {@footnote Mantle of the Mind|This item does not appear in the source text.}

items: 1 psionic creature of CR 7 or higher*

footnotes: * The creature can be alive or dead, but must have died within 24 hours of starting the craft. On success, the creatures soul is consumed, and it can't be resurrected while the soul shard exists. The discipline and effect can be tailored to the creature used as per the GM's discretion.

name: Psionic Surge Table
rows: Roll on this table at the start of each of your turns for the next minute, ignoring this result on subsequent rolls.
You float {@dice 1d10} inches off the ground for the next hour.
You teleport to a random unoccupied space within 60 feet.
You can speak only in {@language Deep Speech} for the next minute.
You leave footprints that glow with an otherworldly light for the next hour.
Your jump distance is tripled for 1 minute.
You manifest {@spell disguise self}, taking on the appearance of the nearest humanoid.
You manifest {@spell levitate} on yourself. This spell does not require concentration.
Your skin becomes translucent for 1 minute.
For the next minute, you can see into the Ethereal Plane out to a 30-foot radius.
You loose all distinctive features and appear as an average person of your race.
You emit light in a 10-foot radius for 1 minute.
You briefly see a fond childhood memory of a random creature within 60 feet.
You are proficient in all skills for 1 minute.
You regain expended Psi Points equal to your Intelligence modifier.
Up to three creatures you choose within 30 feet of you take {@damage 4d10} psychic damage.
You regain all expended Hit Dice.
Your Strength score becomes 4 for 1 minute.
You manifest sleep at the level of the spell that triggered this surge targeting yourself.
You manifest {@spell confusion} targeting yourself. This spell does not require concentration.
You manifest {@spell grease} centered on yourself.
You are {@condition frightened} by the nearest creature until the end of your next turn.
You resist all damage for the next minute.
You manifest {@spell hypnotic pattern} centered on you. This spell does not require concentration.
For the next minute, you regain 5 Psi Points at the start of each of your turns.
You can immediately take one extra action.
You manifest {@spell fly} on a random creature within 60 feet. It must concentrate on this effect.
Maximize the damage of the next spell you manifest within the next minute.
For the next minute, you can teleport up to 20 feet as a bonus action.
You manifest {@spell invisibility} targeting yourself. This spell doesn't require your concentration.
You regain all expended Psi Points.

name: Psychic Injury
rows: {@b Mental Break.} Roll on the {@table Long Term Madness|WoBrCa} table, you gain that madness effect until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
{@b Bout of Madness.} Roll on the {@table Bout of Madness|WoBrCa} table. You gain that bout for {@dice 1d10} minutes.
{@b Confusion.} You are under the effects of the {@spell Confusion|XPHB} spell for 1 minute.
{@b Mental Agony.} You take additional psychic damage equal to your level.
{@b Mental Pain.} You take additional psychic damage equal to half your level (round up).

name: Pteranodon
rows: The wing of the pteranodon resembles an organic canvas stretched over skeletal bone. The canvas itself is quite useful for the creation of small sails and similar equipment, and merchants will pay a decent amount for an intact sample.
The pteranodon's beak in many ways resembles a lance formed of keratin. Evidently, many primitive cultures agree, and seeing a tribe armed with pteranodon lances is not uncommon.

name: Purple Worm
rows: It is a simple fact of Underdark life that you need to have a purple worm ward if you wish to have a long-term settlement. Ironically, these wards require the blood of a purple worm in order to be created. In a way, though it is fitting that only a society that can kill a purple worm can be protected from them. Natural selection at its finest, as it were.

entries: The incredibly corrosive bile of a purple worm is coveted by miners for being able to literally eat through rocks that would otherwise take weeks of work to break through. Just be careful when harvesting it, however, you don't want to be known as the fool who was eaten by an already slain purple worm.

entries.name: Use:
entries: As an action you may make a ranged weapon attack to throw a vial of purple worm bile at a target within 20 feet, shattering it on impact. Make a ranged attack against the target, treating the vial as an improvised object. On a hit, the target suffers {@damage 5d6} acid damage.

rows: Purple worm teeth resemble stalactites and stalagmites in their cavernous mouth more than anything else. Larger than a grown human's arm, these teeth make very good crafting materials and are a rich source of ivory. Alternatively, they can be crafted into fine weapons.
{@filter Any +2 melee piercing weapon|items|source=|type=melee weapon|category=|weapon damage type=p|bonus=weapon attack and damage rolls (+2)}

Despite what you may think, it is not much safer to be on the opposite side of a purple worm's mouth, as its tail is perhaps even more deadly. When the stinger head is taken and re-crafted into a weapon, it can deliver payloads of venom just as it did when attached to its original owner.

With all the dirt and rock that a purple worm chews through, it inevitably swallows some precious gems and metals. These are not digested easily and often clump together in the purple worm's stomach. Melded together by digestive acids and pressure, they form beautiful unique pearls that fetch incredibly high prices on open markets.

name: Pyronica's Wild Magic Surge
rows: Blue fire tornado erupts around Pyronica. All creatures within 30 ft take 28({@damage 8d6}) fire damage (DEX save {@dc 19} half).
Pyronica's head turns into a laughing jack-o-lantern for 1 minute. Fire spells deal + 7({@damage 1d12}) psychic damage but gains vulnerability to bludgeoning.
Bill Cipher's eye appears on Pyronica's palm. She can cast {@spell eyebite} (save {@dc 19}) as bonus action for 1 minute.
Gravity reverses in 50-ft radius. Creatures fall upward taking 21({@damage 6d6}) fall damage. Lasts 1 round.
Pyronica polymorphs into a {@creature Salamander} for 3 rounds. Retains spellcasting.
Every flammable object within 100ft ignites. Nonmagical weapons in area take 11({@damage 3d6}) fire damage.
Pyronica swaps places with nearest ally {@table Henchmaniacs|billcipher} via a blue fire portal.
Pyronica's next fire spell petrifies targets into stone candy on failed save (Constitution save {@dc 19} negates).
Rainbow fire rains in 60-ft circle for 3 rounds. Ground becomes difficult terrain and deals 7({@damage 2d6}) fire damage/round when starting turn inside.
Pyronica grows third flaming arm. Can make extra Chaos Beam attack each turn for 1 minute.
All creatures within 60ft grow flaming afros. Take 2({@damage 1d4}) fire damage/round until extinguished (action to remove).
Pyronica's hair turns into a sentient fire snake. Gains {@spell Spirit Shroud|TCE} ability for 1 minute.
Pyronica's skin becomes molten lava. All melee attackers take 7({@damage 2d6}) fire damage for 1 minute.
Pyronica's laughter echoes, causing all creatures within 30ft to make a Wisdom saving throw {@dc 19} or be {@condition frightened} for 1 minute.
Pyronica's eyes shoot beams of blue fire. Each creature in a 30ft line must make a Dexterity saving throw {@dc 19} or take 22({@damage 4d10}) fire damage.
Pyronica's {@creature Shadow Demon|MM|shadow} detaches  and attacks nearest creature. Lasts 1 minute.
All coins within 100 ft melt into flaming slag.
Pyronica grows to Huge size for 1 min. Double damage dice but AC reduced by 4.
Blood turns to liquid fire. Critical hits against her spray 15-ft radius dealing 11({@damage 3d6}) fire damage.
Swaps personalities with nearest creature for 1 minute. Each controls the other's body.
All nonmagical metal within 50ft glows red-hot. Creatures touching nonmagical metal take 14({@damage 4d6}) fire damage.

Becomes magnetized. Metal objects within 100ft fly toward her people holding metal objects drop them if able or are dragged 20ft towards Pyronica and take 11({@damage 4d10}) bludgeoning damage. Negated by a Strength saving throw {@dc 19}.
Time stutters. Takes 2 extra turns immediately then loses next 2 turns.
Chaos Beam attacks random creatures within range for 3 rounds.
An eye appears on Pyronica's forehead for the next minute. During that time, she has advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight.
10-ft Bill Cipher illusion appears. Wisdom saving throw DC 19 for hostile creatures or be frightened 1 minute.
Fire spells heal instead of harm for next minute. Undead are damaged normally.
Turns invisible but leaves blazing footprints. Ends when attacking.
Ages ({@dice 1d20}) years on even results or de-ages on odd results.
Next spell affects Pyronica instead of target.
All creatures within 60ft swap places randomly via blue fire portals.

Pyronica is transported to the Astral Plane until the end of her next turn, after which time she returns to the space she previously occupied or the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.
Eyes shoot laser beams at random targets whitin 150ft twice per turn dealing 26({@damage 4d12}) radiant damage.
Creates flaming clone as per {@spell Similacrum|phb} but with only 40 hp and copying every move Pyronica makes. Lasts 1 minute.
Next spell casts at 9th level but Pyronica takes 55({@damage 10d10}) psychic damage.

{@dice 1d6} {@creature flumph||flumphs} controlled by the nearest player character appear in unoccupied spaces within 60 feet of Pyronica  and are {@condition frightened} of her. They vanish after 1 minute.
Skin oozes napalm. Fire heals her but contact with water deals 11({@damage 2d10}) acid damage for 1 min.
Her voice becomes the same as Bill Cipher's. Can cast {@spell command} ({@dc 19}) as bonus action 3 times.
Shadow winks. Wisdom saving throw {@dc 19} or dance uncontrollably as per {@spell Otto's Irresistible Dance|phb}.
Glows like torch. Bright light 120 ft, dim light 240 ft for 1 hour.
Laughting fit. Pyronica deals 14({@damage 4d6}) psychic damage in 30-ft radius. Charisma saving throw to half damage {@dc 19}.
Hair sets sky on fire. Daylight becomes dim light for 1 mile for 1 hour.
Swaps current hit points with nearest creature.
Resistant to all damage but speed halved for 5 rounds.

Next spell also summons {@dice 1d10}: 1-3 {@creature Animated Object (small)|PHB|chair}, 4-6 {@creature Animated Object (large)|PHB|piano}, 7-9 {@creature Animated Object (medium)|PHB|anvil}, 10 {@creature Polar Bear|MM}.
Sneezes miniature supernova. All creatures within 15ft are blinded for 1 round (Constitution saving throw {@dc 19} negates).
Next damaged creature must save {@dc 19} or cast {@spell fireball} on itself.
Pyronica can't speak for the next minute. Whenever she trys, pink bubbles float out of her mouth.
Emits insulting smoke signals. Creatures reading them take 11({@damage 3d6}) psychic damage.
Fire spells deal cold damage instead and freeze targets for next minute.
Becomes two-dimensional. Move through cracks but attacks against her have advantage.
Attracts lightning. Next 3 electrical attacks automatically hit her.
Spells gain sarcastic commentary. Hit targets have disadvantage on next save.
Whip sings show tunes. Charisma saving throw {@dc 19} or are {@condition incapacitated} by singing until the end of Pyronica's next turn.
Pyronica regains her lowest-level expended spell slot.
Tears are liquid fire. Adjacent creatures within 5ft take 7({@damage 2d6}) fire damage/round for 1 min.
Pyronica casts {@spell grease} centered on herself.
Pyronica casts {@spell fog cloud} centered on herself.
Becomes living firework. Explodes on her next turn for 110({@damage 20d10}) fire damage in 40-ft radius.
Rolls on this table at the start of each of her turns for the next minute, ignoring this result on subsequent rolls.
Casts {@spell mirror image} on Bill Cipher if present, otherwise on herself.
Spells cause explosive flatulence. Knocked prone but pushes enemies 10 ft.
Fire spells create stained glass windows depicting the battle.
Supernaturally funny. Charisma saving throw {@dc 19} or laughs uncontrollably being {@condition incapacitated} for the following 2 rounds.
Pyronica casts {@spell magic missile} as a 9th-level spell.
Gains flaming halo. Advantage on Charisma checks but vulnerability to all damage if dousted in holy water until the next long rest.

Pyronica turns into a potted plant (10 hp; ac 10). While a plant, she is {@condition incapacitated} and is vulnerabile to all damage. If she drop to 0 hit points, her pot breaks, and her form reverts.
Each creature within 30 feet of her becomes {@condition invisible} for the next minute. The invisibility ends on a creature when it attacks or casts a spell.
Whip turns to snakes. Pyronica can speak only in Ignean.
Pyronica gains resistance to all damage for the next minute.
A random creature within 60 feet of her becomes {@condition poisoned} for {@dice 1d4} hours.
Illusory butterflies and flower petals flutter in the air within 10 feet of her for the next minute.
Emits radio waves. Constructs within 100 ft malfunction for 3 rounds.
Hair detaches and becomes a {@creature Fire Elemental|MM}. Attacks random targets.
Juggles her own head. Cast spells with a casting time of an action as bonus actions but attacks against her have advantage.
Each creature within 30 feet of her takes {@damage 1d10} necrotic damage. She regain hit points equal to the sum of the necrotic damage dealt.
Spells cause jazz hands. Targets must succed Charisma saving throws {@dc 19} or waste their next turn snapping fingers.
Sweat becomes Greek fire. Grapplers take 18({@damage 5d6}) fire damage each round.
Gains a flaming monocle. Sees invisibility but blinded in one eye and has disadvantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight
Shadow high-fives her. Gains 50 temp HP but 2 {@creature shadow||shadows} spawn within 5ft of her and oppose her for 1 min.
Turns to living smoke for 1 min. Can't attack but immune to physical damage.
Fire spells summon Bill Cipher graffiti which wisper incessently.
Develops pyrophobia. Disadvantage on fire attacks but gains cold immunity.
Breakdances. Movement doesn't provoke Attaks of opportunity but ends turn prone.
Magic causes karaoke. Charisma saving throws {@dc 19} or use their next action to sing.
Becomes weightless. Floats 5 ft up but pushed 10 ft by any damage.
Spells create explosive bubbles. Effects contained in floating bubbles that pop randomly.
Hiccups fireballs. Casts {@spell fireball} centered on self 3 times over 3 rounds.
She gains +3 to attacks but cannot speak for 3 rounds.
If Pyronica dies within the next minute, she immediately come back to life as if by the {@spell reincarnate} spell.
Next spell creates Nightmare Realm portal. 10-ft gateway sucks in creatures Strength saving throw {@dc 19} within 15ft. On failure targets are transported to the fire plane.
Develops multiple personalities. Each round: 1-2 aggressive, 3-4 cowardly, 5-6 helpful to enemies.
Fire spells paint flaming murals in air that last 24 hours.
Causes amnesia. All within 60 ft forget last minute (Wisdom saving throw DC 19 negates).
Pyronica and all creatures within 30 feet of her gain vulnerability to piercing damage for the next minute.
Laughter creates concussive waves. All within 20 ft are pushed 15 ft and fall prone (Strength saving throw {@dc 19}.
Pyronica teleports up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space of her choice that she can see.

name: Quaggoth
rows: Shaggy and coarse, it would not be immediately apparent that quaggoth fur has much use as anything except as a trophy. The fur however has remarkable insulation qualities, and while uncomfortable, can stuff a coat to keep an adventurer warm in even the deepest and darkest Underdark tunnel.

Due to their horrible Underdark diets, quaggoths have developed several enzymes and antibodies that make them immune to poisons. If used in an alchemy recipe, it creates a potion of poison resistance.

entries: The psionic energy of the Underdark occasionally causes mutations in the susceptible quaggoth population, creating what is known as a thonot. Their brains are noticeably larger and capable of psionic feats themselves. When eaten, these psionic abilities are temporarily bequeathed to the eater.

entries.name: Use:
entries: You may spend an action to eat this brain. For the next hour, you may cast the {@spell feather fall} and {@spell mage hand} spells at will without using a spell slot or requiring any spell components.

name: Quantum Chaos Box Contents
rows: {@dice 1d4} hostile {@creature swarm of rats|MM|swarms of rats} under the effect of {@spell fire shield}
{@dice 1d12} berries created by the {@spell goodberry} spell.
A small piece of a star. It explodes violently. All creatures within 20 feet must make a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 3d12} fire damage, or half as much on a successful save.
The last consumable item you used, of uncommon rarity or less, or a {@item potion of healing|DMG} (if no consumable item applies).
A small wooden toy. It looks quite old.
A key. Someone probably lost it.
{@dice 1d4} delicious looking fresh fish. Cooking and eating them gives a creature up to 10 temporary hit points, as long as they are cooked within 1 hour of opening the box.
Another box that looks identical to the {@item Quantum Chaos Box|KTKCG}, just very slightly smaller. It is a hostile {@creature mimic}.

A letter written in an incomprehensible language. If somehow decoded it might be a mundane letter, or a {@item scroll|KTKCG|spell scroll} for {@filter a spell on the Warlock spell list of 3rd level or lower|spells|level=1;2;3|class=warlock}.
A single bean from a magical {@item bag of beans|DMG}.

name: Quasit
rows: Quasit venom is more of an annoyance than a serious threat, but the paralysis side effect can certainly ruin someone's day. When mixed with other ingredients however, this venom can serve as one of many potential bases for a potion of poison.

entries: Quasit blood is as thin and slippery as the demon it came from, but serves as an excellent spell component for lower-tier magic.

entries.name: Use:
entries: The next time you cast the {@spell find familiar} spell, you may consume a vial of quasit blood instead of using the usual material component of the spell. If you do, your summoned familiar gains the magic resistance trait described in the quasit's statblock. Your familiar also shares this trait with you so long as you are within 10 feet of it. Both of these effects last for 1 hour, or until your familiar next disappears or is dismissed.

name: Quetzalcoatlus
rows: The sharp beak of a quetzalcoatlus is capable of piercing flesh, bone, and armor alike. It only makes sense that when reinforced with some metal, it makes for a wonderful lance.

name: Quick Stats
footnotes: Arrows are indicated when the adventures use a creature's maximum or minimum Hit Point and Damage Rolls. These adjustments help to balance the encounters.
↑ Use Maximum Hit Points and Damage Rolls for this creature.
↓ Use Minimum Hit Points and Damage Rolls for this creature.

name: Quickling

entries: Quickling blood remains in motion even after it is drained from its body. Thinner than the blood of any other mortal creature, a quickling's blood is loaded with adrenaline and other enzymes that when drunk by a humanoid, slows their perception of time and gives them enhanced reflexes. The crash after the effect has worn off can be rather harsh however.

entries.name: Use:
entries: You may spend your action to drink this blood. If you do so, you gain an extra reaction per round on top of your usual amount. This benefit lasts for 1 hour, after which you suffer one level of {@condition exhaustion}.

rows: The hide of a quickling is extraordinarily smooth, allowing it to reduce wind resistance as much as physically possible. While it may seem barbaric, their hide makes a wonderful base for the ubiquitous boots of speed.

name: Raiding Roll
rows: Lost over half the warriors; return phase rolls have Dis{@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}; return phase takes an extra week.
Heavy casualties; return phase takes an extra week.
Important NPC taken captive or {@filter Uncommon magic item|items|rarity=uncommon} found
Important NPC taken captive or {@filter Rare magic item|items|rarity=rare} found
Add the maximum possible result of the spoils die as a bonus to the spoils die roll.

name: Raise Dead Random Effects
rows: {@b Nimbus.} The target is surrounded by a glow or halo equivalent to {@spell faerie fire}.

{@b Thundercrack.} When {@spell raise dead} is cast, the target's return to life is heralded by a crack of thunder and a stroke of lightning. These can be heard and seen for at least a mile and may be accompanied by a sudden, brief storm.

{@b Neophyte.} The raised creature forgets one language, one spell or feat, one friend, and one class ability. These memories return in a random sequence at a rate of one per week until all are recovered.
{@b Exhaustion.} Restoring a soul is as debilitating on the caster as on the dead. The caster suffers the same penalty on attack rolls, saving throws, and ability checks as the raised creature.

{@b Voice of the Afterlife.} The raised creature gained subconscious knowledge of a distant plane during its sojourn in the realm of the dead. It now speaks either {@language Abyssal}, {@language Celestial}, {@language Infernal}, Satarre, or Umbral (player's choice).

{@b Breath of Life.} The caster absorbs one magical disease, curse, or similar effect from the target creature into him- or herself. The affliction ends on the newly-raised creature but takes full effect on the caster, who must get it cured or removed by standard means.

{@b Gravetouched.} The raised creature has an uncanny voice or appearance that frightens nonhostile animals (including mounts), children, and even adults unaccustomed to such things. Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) checks are made with advantage.

{@b Raging Spirit.} The raised creature returns to life in the grip of intense and uncontrollable rage. It immediately attacks the caster and anyone else nearby, including friends, acolytes, etc. This anger ends when the creature becomes {@condition unconscious} or when it's affected by {@spell calm emotions} or comparable magic.

{@b Mild Spirit.} The raised creature returns to life possessed of a gentle kindness. It refuses to fight, argue, or even defend itself for a period of {@dice 1d6 + 1} days. This unnatural calm can be removed by a {@spell calm emotions} spell. It also ends if the creature is rendered {@condition unconscious} by an attack.

{@b  Altered Spirit.} The raised creature returns to life with a random alignment different from its previous one. This lasts for {@dice 1d6 + 1} days. The creature's alignment returns to normal if the creature is affected by a {@spell remove curse} spell or if it's rendered {@condition unconscious} by an attack.
{@b  Armor of the Planes.} The raised creature gains resistance to necrotic, fire, cold, or lightning damage for seven days (caster's choice).

{@b  Servitor.} The raised creature is {@condition charmed} by the caster. While {@condition charmed} in this way, the creature serves the caster loyally as repayment for restoring him or her to life. The length of this service is determined by the caster's spellcasting level: up to level 11 = one week; level 12 to 14 = two weeks; level 15 or higher = one year. The effect is broken if the caster or the caster's companions cause direct harm to the {@condition charmed} creature or its loved ones.

name: Rakshasa
rows: The hatred and malice inherent in a rakshasa is embodied in their deformed claws, capable of imparting a curse that spites any it strikes. When burned in an occult ritual, the ashes can create a dye used in dark rituals to curse unwary hoarders of magical items.

The rakshasa's tendency to kill and subsume the lives of its victims is almost legendary. The heart of the rakshasa drips with this malicious coveting of others' identities, and can be refashioned into an amulet that allows its wielder to do the same.

While not as potent once removed from its original body, the removed hide of a rakshasa still carries the magical resistance that it is famous for. When reinforced properly, it becomes a fearsome cloak that shrugs off weak spells.

name: Random Bazaar Encounters
rows: As the party browses the stalls, they notice someone has lifted an item from them. A quick chase ensues through a labyrinth of corridors and stalls. If they catch the thief, they may find their pockets also filled with stolen contraband they didn't put there.

{@homebrew A} flask explodes from the alchemist's stall, releasing a strange vapor. Everyone in the vicinity must succeed on a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned} for {@dice 1d4} rounds.

The party walks through an area where the magical weave is particularly tangled. A spell cast within this zone has a {@table wild magic surge|PHB} effect. This area is well-known to black marketeers, who sometimes lure adversaries here.

The party hears cheers and jeers from a hidden alcove. If investigated, they find an underground fight club. Betting is encouraged, and one party member may choose to participate for a cash prize and potential renown.

A food vendor offers free samples of an exotic dish. Those who try it and succeed on a {@dc 16} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check realize there's a very illegal component to the dish. The vendor might offer to pay for the party's silence or become hostile, depending on their reaction.

A young child approaches the party, claiming to be lost. However, the child is actually bait for an ambush, or perhaps they are genuinely lost and in possession of an artifact or important piece of information.

name: Random Chaos Events
rows: The characters hear ghostly whispering from the darkness from a group of {@dice 1d4+1} {@creature geist|SGttEH|geists} of victims killed in the cavern. The geists are hostile and will attack the party if they are not placated with a successful {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check.

Geometric patterns and shapes seem to ebb and flow in silvery lines across the surface of the walls. Creatures feel drawn to them, and attempts to read them must succeed on a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw or gain a {@table short-term madness|SGttEH} effect {@homebrew |(see the "Steinhardt's Madness System" chapter in Steinhardt's Guide to the Eldritch Hunt)}. The patterns disappear after 1 minute.

The characters see {@dice 1d4+1} {@creature gargoyle} statues etched into niches in the room's upper walls. The statues are hostile and attack the party, but a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}) check reveals that they can be instantly deactivated by reciting an ancient prayer inscribed on one of the statues.

The sound of a child weeping can be heard from the next room. The sound continues to come from a distance, no matter which direction the characters move. The sound lasts 30 minutes before it ends with a choked-off scream of terror.

The cave floor gives way beneath a random character, and they must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or fall 20 feet down into a pit filled with {@dice 1d4+1} {@creature giant centipede|MM|giant centipedes}. The {@creature giant centipede|MM|centipedes} are hostile and attack the party.

A wave of eldritch energy washes over the party, and each character must make a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the character's mouth begins to melt and flow into a solid piece of smooth flesh (or metal), and they cannot speak. This effect lasts for 10 minutes or until removed by a '{@spell remove curse}' spell or similar effect.

{@footnote 45|This value is duplicated in the source.}-46
footnotes: {@note Due to the limitations of 5etools' engine, the following table is not interactive. However, you can use this {@dice d100} to save some typing, or one of the environment-specific tables in the column headings.}

footnotes.name: Aldani
entries: The characters are shadowed by {@dice 1d4} {@creature aldani (lobsterfolk)|Toa|aldani} ({@adventure appendix B|BelzorMM|12}), which are noticed by any character with a passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) score of 12 or higher. The aldani don't communicate with others unless they must, and they won't fight unless the characters refuse to take a bribe to leave the area. The aldani aid the characters only if they're offered something of great value in return–for example, an offer to drive off a pack of predatory sahuagin encroaching on their territory.

footnotes.name: Ankheg
entries: A group of {@dice 1d3} {@creature ankheg|mm|ankhegs} bursts up from beneath the ground to ambush the characters. Any character without {@sense tremorsense|MM} is surprised by the attack. Ankhegs prefer Small creatures, which they grab with their mandibles and drag back underground to consume.

footnotes.name: Bandits
entries: A marauding gang of bandits confronts the party. The gang consists of a {@creature bandit captain} and {@dice 3d6 + 2} {@creature bandit|mm|bandits}, all wearing cloaks and mounted on {@creature riding horse|mm|riding horses}. There is a {@chance 25} chance that the bandits attack without provocation. Otherwise, the captain promises not to attack in exchange for a toll (no less than 100 gp worth of treasure). If the characters pay up, the captain bids them a safe journey before departing peacefully.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Each bandit carries a pouch containing {@dice 1d10} gp. The bandit captain's pouch holds {@dice 2d10} gp and {@dice 1d6} gems worth 100 gp each.

footnotes.name: Barbarians
entries: The characters encounter a group of {@dice 2d6 + 2} {@creature tribal warrior|mm|tribal warriors}, led by a {@creature berserker}. If the encounter occurs during the day, the barbarians are prowling the countryside while hunting wild game; if the encounter occurs at night, they are camped.

entries.name: The North
entries: If this encounter occurs in The North, the characters encounter an Uthgardt Barbarian tribe, led by an {@creature Uthgardt shaman|SKT} ({@adventure appendix B|BelzorMM|12}) with an additional {@creature berserker} bodyguard.

entries.name: Sea or Coast
entries: If the encounter occurs at sea or on the coast, the characters encounter {@dice 1d3} {@item longship|BelzorMM|longships}, each with ten {@creature berserker|mm|berserkers} and thirty {@creature tribal warrior|mm|tribal warriors} aboard. One of the {@creature berserker|mm|berserkers} serves as the captain. These hostile, bloodthirsty Northfolk raiders hail from Gundarlun, the Korinn Archipelago, Tuern, or the Whalebones. The {@item longship|BelzorMM|longships} have a speed of 3 miles per hour. If the vessel the characters are in moves at least as fast, the characters can flee from the barbarians and avoid an altercation.

footnotes.name: Blood Hawks
entries: A vicious kettle of {@dice 2d4+2} {@creature blood hawk|mm|blood hawks} attacks the party from above. These crimson raptors are fearless and attack large creatures without second thought. The hawks target already injured characters or those who look weaker than the rest of the party.

footnotes.name: Coelenites
entries: The characters are attacked by {@dice 1d4 + 1} {@creature coelenite|BelzorMM|coelenites} ({@adventure appendix B|BelzorMM|12}) who try and pull them down into the water and drown them. The {@creature coelenite|BelzorMM|coelenites} try to avoid leaving the ocean if possible but foray onto the shore or climb aboard boats to pursue their prey.

entries.name: Higher Levels
entries: If the characters are 4th level or higher, replace one of the {@creature coelenite|BelzorMM|coelenites} with a {@creature coelenite mass mind|BelzorMM} ({@adventure appendix B|BelzorMM|12}). The {@creature coelenite|BelzorMM|coelenites} telepathically threaten the characters with drowning unless they provide a tribute of food. The {@creature coelenite|BelzorMM|coelenites} can be appeased with food (four day's supply per coelenite in the group). Otherwise, they attack.

footnotes.name: Dolphins
entries: The characters spot a pod of {@dice 3d4} {@creature dolphin|vgm|dolphins} ({@adventure appendix B|BelzorMM|12}). If the characters are above the surface of the water, they notice the beautiful creatures leaping between the waves. They are naturally inquisitive and might come within 10 feet of the boat to take a look.

A {@creature dolphin|vgm} that is successfully {@condition grappled}, caught in a {@item net|phb}, or otherwise prevented from escaping can be trained as a mount by a character with proficiency in {@skill Animal Handling} who spends a few hours a day working with the mammal. At the end of 1 week, the character makes a DC 15 Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) check. On a success, the dolphin becomes a willing mount for any humanoid.

footnotes.name: Druid
entries: The characters encounter a {@creature druid} who might be a member of the Emerald Enclave or simply devoted to protecting a certain area of wilderness. Most druids are happy to give guidance on traversing their lands, provided the characters are respectful of the environment on their travels. There is a {@chance 50} chance that the druid is accompanied by an animal companion. Two sample druids are presented below, but you can create others.

Jillian Leafgather (NG female lightfoot halfling) is a member of the Emerald Enclave accompanied by her massive, relentlessly slobbering {@creature mastiff}, Bungo. Jillian despises animal cruelty, and even considers insulting animals verbally to be intolerable. She knows a few shortcuts around the Sword Mountains and Neverwinter Wood, which she happily shares with characters in need. The shortcuts allow characters to move at a fast pace without any penalties.

Orsik Oakenheim (CE male mountain dwarf) is wild and rugged. He believes that the wilds should overtake civilisation, and all folk should go back to living as nomadic tribes in the wilderness. He wears a huge fur coat and trapper hat which conceals eight {@creature twig blight|mm|twig blights}. Orsik happily converses with characters, but if he deems them too involved with society, he tries to orchestrate their deaths. This can be achieved by sending characters into dangerous terrain such as scree slopes, {@trap quicksand} or predator territory. He also sends his {@creature twig blight|mm|blights} to steal things from the characters such as identification papers, faction emblems or {@item holy symbol|phb|holy symbols}.

footnotes.name: Elves
entries: A band of {@dice 3d6} wood elves offers to escort the party through the forest, steering the characters around the elves' hidden settlements. If they accept the offer, the characters have no hostile encounters while passing through the forest. If the characters refuse, the elves offer no further assistance and disappear into the woods. The elves use the {@creature wood elf|skt|scout} statistics, with the {@footnote following changes|Included in the linked statblock.}:

items: Their speed is 35 feet, and they can attempt to {@action hide} even when they are in an area only lightly obscured by foliage, heavy rain, falling snow, mist, and other natural phenomena.
They have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition charmed}, and magic can't put them to sleep.
They have darkvision out to a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Sea
entries: If this encounter occurs at sea, the characters encounter {@dice 3d6} friendly sea elf {@creature scout|mm|scouts}. These elves might be from Tir faoi Thoinn, Iumathiashae, or Waterdeep. They know the location of all the Island Kingdoms and underwater locations. Characters can hire a sea elf guide for 1 gp a day.

There is a {@chance 10} chance that one of the aquatic elves is a {@creature malenti|BelzorMM} ({@adventure appendix B|BelzorMM|12}); a sahuagin born with a mutation that makes it resemble an aquatic elf. The malenti spies on the characters as best it can and reports back to its sahuagin allies when it can about their movements and plans. This information eventually makes its way to the Colony of Zellix'Phor and could be used to set up an ambush with one of the mind flayers when the characters made port.

footnotes.name: Floating Debris
entries: The characters notice something floating one hundred feet away. A successful DC 16 Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check reveals the nature of the debris. Roll a {@dice d6}:
Barrels and crates.
Shattered wooden planks.
Chests.

entries.name: Barrels and Crates
entries: Bobbing on the waves are {@dice 4d4} crates and {@item barrel|phb|barrels} filled with goods. These may contain alcohol, {@item rations (1 day)|phb|rations}, rope or other basic items typically found aboard ships.

entries.name: Shattered Wooden Planks
entries: Planks of shattered wood float atop the ocean. Clearly, these are remnants of a ship which has been recently attacked and perhaps destroyed. There is a {@chance 50} chance that a pirate ship is nearby (see "Pirate Ship" in this section).

entries.name: Chests
entries: Mostly sunk beneath the water's surface are {@dice 1d4} {@item chest|phb|chests}. These must have been jettisoned from another vessel. The {@item chest|phb|chests} are locked and keyless and require a successful DC 14 Dexterity check with {@item thieves' tools|phb} or a successful DC 16 Strength check to open. Inside are valuable items worth 100 gp, such as money, gems, candlesticks, jewellery and the like. There is a {@chance 10} chance that the chest contains a more expensive item worth 250 gp, such as a gemstone or {@table 250 gp art objects|dmg|art object}. This could be replaced with a magic item (roll once on {@table Magic Item Table A} in chapter 7 of the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}).

footnotes.name: Ghost Ship
entries: A merchant ship appears on the horizon but appears to be drifting very slowly. A successful DC 16 Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check reveals that the deck is empty, and the ship appears to be adrift.

If the characters decide to board the ship, they discover that it is entirely empty. There is a {@chance 50} chance that they can salvage useful items from the vessel such as {@item rations (1 day)|phb|rations}, alcohol, rope and the like.

entries.name: Haunted
entries: There is a {@chance 50} chance that the ship is haunted by the dead crew. If so, there are {@dice 3d4} {@creature ghost|mm|ghosts} aboard the ship who lash out at characters that disrespect the ship by stealing, breaking into cabins etc. If characters can calm the ghosts by offering them eternal rest, they reveal that their ship was attacked by mutated pirates. They had piscine features, such as shark jaws, crab claws, and pufferfish spines. Any of the crew who resisted the creatures were killed and those who remain were taken aboard as hostages.

entries.name: Repeat
entries: If this encounter occurs again, consider replacing the {@creature ghost|mm|ghosts} with {@creature specter|mm|specters} or {@creature poltergeist|mm|poltergeists} who cannot be brought to an eternal rest.

footnotes.name: Giant Boar
entries: The characters encounter a {@creature giant boar} chasing down a portly halfling. Unless they intervene, the halfling is caught and gored to death by the beast. The halfling's name is Nerrywill Underbarrow (NG male stout halfling {@creature commoner} with a {@item dagger|phb}, proficiency with {@item cook's utensils|phb} and the additional skill: {@skill Perception} {@dice 1d20+4|+4}). If the characters save his life, the tubby fellow pledges himself to the party for as long as he is helpful. He's a great chef and has a remarkably good eye. He keeps all his possessions in his pack and is willing to travel to the ends of the earth (and beyond) with his saviours.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Nerrywill carries a battered brass {@item spyglass|phb} engraved with his initials (850 gp), and a {@item backpack|phb} containing a {@item dagger|phb} (2 gp) and {@item cook's utensils|phb} (1 gp).

footnotes.name: Giant Crab
entries: A {@creature giant crab} scuttles out from a kelp forest or coastal cave and attacks a random character. The target is surprised unless they have a passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) of 14 or higher. The crab attempts to {@action grapple} the character, then drop overboard with them and drown them (see "{@quickref Suffocating||2}" in chapter 8 of the {@i Player's Handbook}). If the encounter occurs at sea, the crab claws its way up the hull to ambush the character.

entries.name: Higher Levels
entries: If the characters are above 4th level, consider using a {@creature hulking crab|SKT} ({@adventure appendix B|BelzorMM|12}).

footnotes.name: Giant Lightning Eel
entries: A {@creature giant lightning eel|tftyp} ({@adventure appendix B|BelzorMM|12}) shoots out from a coral reef or rocky crevasse to attack a random character. The character targeted by the eel is surprised unless they have a passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) score of 13 or higher.

footnotes.name: Giant Octopus
entries: A {@creature giant octopus} shows some curiosity in the characters. The intelligent animal uses its dextrous tentacles to search their backpacks for food or curious treasures that it can steal away to its hoard. So long as the characters don't attack it, the octopus is not hostile. If the octopus finds a {@item rations (1 day)|phb|ration} or shiny treasure on the characters, it attempts to steal it. The octopus makes a Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check against the characters passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}). If the octopus succeeds, it steals the item and swims back to its lair.

entries.name: Higher Levels
entries: If the characters are above 5th level, consider using a colossal octopus ({@adventure appendix B|BelzorMM|12}).

footnotes.name: Giant Sea Horses
entries: The characters encounter {@dice 1d4} friendly {@creature giant sea horse|mm|giant sea horses}. Like their smaller kin, giant sea horses are shy, colourful fish with elongated bodies and curled tails. These creatures are often trained as mounts by aquatic elves.

A giant sea horse that is {@condition grappled}, caught in a {@item net|phb}, or otherwise prevented from escaping can be trained as a mount by a character with proficiency in {@skill Animal Handling}. At the end of 1 week with the animal, the character makes a DC 15 Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) check. On a success, the giant sea horse becomes a willing mount for any humanoid.

footnotes.name: Giant Shark
entries: A {@creature giant shark} surges through the water toward the party and attacks a random character. The size of the creature makes it impossible to miss, and the characters each have a turn to try and flee or {@action hide} before it arrives and attacks. Giant sharks are 30 feet long and utterly fearless.

entries.name: Ships
entries: If this encounter occurs while the characters are on a ship, the giant shark attacks whatever vessel the characters are on. These enormous fish are capable of sinking smaller ships but are just as likely to ram larger ones to try and knock unsuspecting crew overboard. If the shark rams the ship, and characters on deck must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw or be thrown overboard.

footnotes.name: Giant Spider
entries: The characters are ambushed by a {@creature giant spider}.

entries.name: Forest
entries: The {@creature giant spider} drops down from the canopy above onto a random character. The character is surprised unless they have a passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) of 17 or higher.

entries.name: Mountain
entries: A random character inadvertently blunders into the spider's {@hazard webs|dmg|web} (see "{@book Dungeon Hazards|dmg|5|Dungeon Hazards|0}" in chapter 5 of the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}). The spider quickly emerges from a concealed cave to gather its dinner

entries.name: Sea
entries: Whilst travelling through an area of low visibility, such as a rocky crevasse or a coral reef, a random character is attacked by a {@creature giant spider} with a swim speed of 30 ft. The character is surprised unless they have a passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) of 17 or higher.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: If the characters succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check, they can track back to the spider's lair; a sheltered cave covered in sticky webs with corpses hanging from the ceiling. There is a {@chance 25} chance that one of these corpses has a magic item, determined by rolling on {@table Magic Item Table B} in chapter 7 of the {@i Dungeon Master's Guide}.

footnotes.name: Goblinoids
entries: A typical goblin patrol or hunting party consists of a {@creature goblin boss} leading {@dice 2d6 + 3} {@creature goblin|mm|goblins}. Goblins tend to have their own territories which they seldom leave. Goblins prefer to hunt at night and lay low in ambush positions during the day.

A night encounter with goblins involves an attack on the characters' camp. A character standing watch with a passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) of 16 or higher detects the goblins moving into attack positions and can rouse the rest of the party. If no one on watch notices the goblins, all characters are surprised.

If this encounter occurs while the characters are traveling during the day, any characters with a passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) of 16 or higher spots the tell-tale signs of an ambush: disadvantageous terrain coupled with an eerie silence not normal for the environment.

Goblins bargain for their lives if captured. If the characters can force or coerce a vow of cooperation from goblin prisoners, they will serve as guides. Goblins in their home territory have the following additional skill: {@skill Survival} {@dice 1d20+1|+1}.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The gang of goblins have amassed 50 gp of assorted goods from ambushing travellers.

entries.name: Higher Levels
entries: If the characters are above 4th level, there is a {@chance 50} chance that the goblins are led by {@dice 1d4 + 1} {@creature bugbear|mm|bugbears} and the {@creature goblin boss} is replaced by a {@creature bugbear chief}. When under the command of bugbears, goblins do not flee unless all the bugbears are killed.

footnotes.name: Harpies
entries: A beautiful song carries in on the wind toward the party. Flying toward them are {@dice 1d4 + 2} {@creature harpy|mm|harpies}. As soon as the {@creature harpy|mm|harpies} are within 300 feet, they use their luring song to try and charm the characters. The {@creature harpy|mm|harpies} attempt to lure any enthralled characters into dangerous terrain such as scree slopes or overboard a ship. {@creature Harpy|mm|Harpies} might also pair up to {@action grapple} a character and fly off with them to their lair. {@creature Harpy|mm|Harpies} typically lair in isolated caves accessible only by climbing, such as rocky outcroppings, clifftops or skerries.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Each harpy has a {@chance 25} chance of wearing some basic jewellery worth 50 gp, such as a silver necklace or bronze anklet.

footnotes.name: Hill Giants
entries: A band of {@dice 1d3} {@creature hill giant|mm|hill giants} is searching for homesteads to pillage or bands of travellers to capture. The giants hurl rocks at any small folk they see. {@creature Hill giant|mm|Hill giants} are dim creatures and are easily tricked by misdirection and illusions. Characters might even be able to slip past a group of them while they argue with each other about who has the biggest belly, or whose feet smell the worst.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The giants carry a sack with them which contains a bundle of mundane items such as wagon wheels, tombstones, beehives and casks of ale.
